# Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta

מסכת דרך ארץ זוטא

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta)

הדרכות מוסר לתלמידי חכמים, דרשות על ימות המשיח וכן פרק העוסק בשבח השלום.

Characteristics of a scholar, teachings about the messianic age, and a chapter extolling peace.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 128, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 128)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:1)


דרכן של תלמידי חכמים עניו ושפל רוח זריז ממולא עלוב ואהוב לכל אדם. שפל לאנשי ביתו ירא חטא ודורש את האדם לפי מעשיו. ואומר כל מה שיש בעוה״ז אין לי חפץ בהם [לפי שאין העוה״ז שלי] יושב ומשנה ומטנף כסותו לפני רגלי תלמידי חכמים. ואין איש רואה בו דבר רע. שואל כענין ומשיב כהלכה.


The characteristics of a scholar are that he is meek, humble,¹ alert, filled [with a desire for learning],², ‘bright’, as in Ḳid. 29b (Sonc. ed., p. 141). Cf. KR III, 2, p. 443, n. 13. modest, beloved by all, humble to the members of his household and sin-fearing. He judges a man [fairly] according to his deeds,³ and says ‘I have no desire for all the things of this world because this world is not for me’. He sits and studies,⁴ soiling his cloak at the feet of the scholars.⁵ H reads *mith‘aṭṭef*, ‘wrapped in his cloak’, perhaps in the same sense as in Aboth I, 4 (Sonc. ed., p. 3), ‘Suffer thyself to be covered by the dust of their feet’, i.e. sit in the dust on the ground at their feet while they teach. GRA reads *maṭṭil*, ‘and throws his cloak in front of the feet of scholars’, perhaps for them to sit on. For a different explanation, cf. KR III, p. 444, n. 17. In him no one sees any evil. He questions according to the subject-matter⁶ and answers to the point.⁷

footnotes:
¹ Cf. Aboth IV, 4 (Sonc. ed., p. 45).
² H reads memullaḥ
³ He does not, e.g., interpret a man’s good actions as determined by ulterior motives and does not show favour where it is not deserved.
⁴ H omits ‘and studies’.
⁵ For meṭannef
⁶ Cf. Shab. 3b (Sonc. ed., pp. 5f.), ‘R. Ḥiyya said to Rab: “When Rabbi is occupied with one tractate, do not ask him a question relating to another” ’.
⁷ lit. ‘in accordance with the accepted decision’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:2)


הי' כנוד בקוע שנתפתח להכניס הרוח וכערוגה עמוקה שמחזקת את מימיה. וכקנקנה זפותה שמשמרת את יינה. כספוג שהוא סופג את הכל. אל תהיה כפתח גדול שמכניס את הרוח ולא כפתח קטן שמנבל את היקרים. היה כאסקופה התחתונה שהכל דשין בה וכיתד הנמוכה שהכל תולין בה:


Be like a gourd split open that the wind may enter,⁸ like a deep furrow which retains its water,⁹ like a jar coated with pitch which preserves its wine,¹⁰ and like a sponge which absorbs all.¹¹
Be not like a wide opening which allows the wind to rush in,¹² or like a narrow opening which injures the valuable [as they press through].¹³ Be like a doorstep on which everyone treads¹⁴ and like a low peg which is within the reach of all.¹⁵

footnotes:
⁸ Let your mind be open to receive instruction. For readings which add the negative, cf. ARN p. 85 and KR p. 449.
⁹ Such a bed yields good produce; so must a scholar study continuously and raise good disciples.
¹⁰ i.e. he must have a retentive memory.
¹¹ Cf. Aboth V, 18 (Sonc. ed., V, 15, p. 69).
¹² i.e. do not cultivate associates indiscriminately, yet do not be so unapproachable that worthy companionships cannot get near to you. Or, do not create a stir on entering and leaving; or, do not allow petty and frivolous ideas to enter your mind.
¹³ By having to stoop or squeeze in; i.e. do not cause people worthy or your association to demean themselves or hold aloof.
¹⁴ i.e. be ready to learn from all.
¹⁵ lit. ‘on which all hang [their things]’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:3)


אם לקית בממונך זכור איוב שלקה בממונו ובגופו. אם לקית בגופך. זכור דתן ואבירם שירדו חיים שאולה.


If you suffered monetary loss, remember Job who was smitten both financially and physically. If you have been smitten physically, remember Dathan and Abiram who descended alive into Sheol.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ Cf. Num. 16, 32f.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:4)


אל תכשל בעיניך שאין מכשול אלא בעינים.


Do not be enticed into sin by your eyes, because enticement into sin is caused only through the eyes.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ Cf. Soṭah 8a (Sonc. ed., p. 35), ‘We have learnt a tradition that the evil impulse only bears sway over what a person’s eyes see’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:5)


אל תבוש מן השנים שמא תאכל יותר מדאי.


Do not cause yourself to feel ashamed by your teeth¹⁸ lest you eat more than is good for you.¹⁹ instead of *shemma’*.

footnotes:
¹⁸ GRA reads: ‘Do not be attracted to appetizing dishes’.
¹⁹ lit. ‘more than is sufficient’. NY quotes a reading: ‘That you do not give them too much to eat’. Another and better variant is: ‘That you eat not’, etc., i.e. shello’


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:6)


[ס״א ואל תמשוך מן המצות ואל תמשוך למינות] אל תדרוש מן הצדוקים שמא תמשך לגיהנם.


Do not turn away from meritorious deeds and do not be attracted to heresy.²⁰, a term for the teachings of the early Jewish-Christians. Do not inquire of Sadducees²¹ lest you be drawn into Gehinnom.²²

footnotes:
²⁰ Heb. minuth
²¹ A party holding views antagonistic to those of the Pharisees. They regarded only those observances obligatory which are in the written Torah and did not acknowledge what was derived by Rabbinical interpretation.
²² By abandoning the Torah.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:7)


אם אומרים עליך אחרים דבר רע אל תענם. גדול יהיה בעיניך כקטן. אם אמרת על אחרים דבר רע קטן יהיה בעיניך כגדול עד שתלך ותפייס עליו:


If others speak evil of you, answer them not; should it be a serious [calumny], regard it as slight. If, however, you spoke evil of others, though [the calumny] be slight, regard it as serious [and do not rest] until you go and pacify them.²³

footnotes:
²³ On the evil of slander, cf. ‘Arak. 15b (Sonc. ed., pp. 86ff.).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:8)


אל יהי פקדונך ופרקך רע שאין שבחה של תורה


Let not your [behaviour during] adolescence be of blemished repute, for this would be derogatory to the Torah; but let it be of unblemished repute, for this would tend to glorify the Torah.²⁴

footnotes:
²⁴ The translation follows GRA.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:9)


הוי אוהב את התורה ומכבדה. (אלא יהי טוב שכן שבחה של תורה). הוי אוהב את הבריות ומכבדן.


Love and honour the Torah.²⁵ Love your fellow-creatures and respect them.²⁶

footnotes:
²⁵ By carrying out your duties towards God.
²⁶ By observing your duties towards them.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:10)


העבר רצונך מפני רצון חבירך שכן עשתה רחל ללאה ודוד לשאול: העבר רצונך ורצון חבירך מפני רצון שמים שכן מצינו ביעקב שלא נשק ליוסף.


Set aside your will in face of the will of your fellow,²⁷ for so did Rachel towards Leah and David towards Saul.²⁸ Set aside your will and the will of your fellow in face of the will of Heaven, for so we find it with Jacob who did not kiss Joseph.²⁹

footnotes:
²⁷ When they conflict; cf. Aboth II, 4 (Sonc. ed., p. 14).
²⁸ Cf. KR IV, p. 454f.
²⁹ Cf. ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:11)


הוי אוהב את השמא ושנא את הכמה. רבי חדקא היה אומרה בלשון אחרת הוי אוהב את השמא ושנא את הכמה בכך:


Love the [term] ‘perhaps’ and hate the [expression] ‘how much?’³⁰ R. Ḥidḳa expressed this in another way: Love the [term] ‘perhaps’ and hate the [expression] ‘what of it?’³¹

footnotes:
³⁰ i.e. ‘how much harm will it do to me?’ Or, be envious of others by saying, ‘Look how much So-and-so possesses!’
³¹ If I commit this trivial sin; so GRA, lit. ‘What is in it?’ it is of little consequence.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:12)


הרחק מן המביא לידי עבירה ומן הכיעור ומן הדומה לכיעור שמא יחשדוך אחרים בעבירה.


Keep aloof from anything that may lead to sin, from anything hideous and from whatever seems hideous,³² lest others suspect you of sin.

footnotes:
³² Cf. Ḥul. 44b (Sonc. ed., p. 239).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:13)


אל תלשין את חבירך. שכל המלשין את חבירו אין לו רפואה.


Slander not your fellow because there is no remedy for him who slanders his fellow.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:14)


אל תאכל לחם עם כהן עם הארץ שמא תחלל קדשי קדשים.


Do not eat bread with a *kohen* who is an *‘am ha-’areẓ* lest he give you sacred food to eat.³³

footnotes:
³³ Cf. Ned. 20a (Sonc. ed., p. 56).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:15)


הרחק מן התרעומת שמא תתרעם על אחרים ותוסיף לחטוא:


Refrain from grumbling lest you grumble against others and be led into further sin.³⁴

footnotes:
³⁴ Cf. below, IX, 1, p. 589.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:16)


ז׳ אבות כרותי ברית. אלו הן אברהם. ויצחק. ויעקב. משה. ואהרן. ופינחס. ודוד. באברהם כתיב (בראשית ט״ו:י״ח) ביום ההוא כרת ה׳ את אברם ברית לאמר. ביצחק כתיב (שם יז) ואת בריתי אקים את יצחק. ביעקב כתיב (ויקרא כ״ו:מ״ב) וזכרתי את בריתי יעקב. במשה כתיב (שמות ל״ד:כ״ז) כי ע״פ הדברים האלה כרתי אתך ברית ואת (בני) ישראל. באהרן כתיב (במדבר י״ח:י״ט) ברית מלח עולם הוא לפני ה׳. בפינחס כתיב (שם כה) והיתה לו ולזרעו אחריו ברית כהונת עולם. בדוד כתיב (תהלים פט) כרתי ברית לבחירי נשבעתי לדוד עבדי:


There were seven patriarchs with whom a divine covenant was made, viz.: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Phinehas and David. In connection with Abraham it is written, *In that day the Lord made a covenant with Abraham saying*.³⁵ In connection with Isaac it is written, *But My covenant will I establish with Isaac*.³⁶ XVII, 21. In connection with Jacob it is written, *Then will I remember My covenant with Jacob*.³⁷ In connection with Moses it is written, *For after the tenor of these words I have made a covenant with thee and with Israel*.³⁸ In connection with Aaron it is written, *It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the Lord*.³⁹ In connection with Phinehas it is written, *And it shall be unto him, and to his seed after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood*.⁴⁰ XXV, 13. In connection with David it is written, *I have made a covenant with My chosen, I have sworn unto David My servant*.⁴¹ means schools), Moses of meekness, Aaron of peace-making, Phinehas of zeal on behalf of God, and David of singing His praise.

footnotes:
³⁵ Gen. 15, 18.
³⁶ ibid.
³⁷ Lev. 26, 42.
³⁸ Ex. 34, 27.
³⁹ Num. 18, 19.
⁴⁰ ibid.
⁴¹ Ps. 89, 4. Perhaps this passage is quoted here to teach men to emulate their special characteristics. Abraham stands as the example of hospitality, Isaac of self-sacrifice, Jacob of scholarship (cf. Gen. 25, 27, where according to Rabbinic interpretation tents


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:17)


ז׳ אבות שכנו בכבוד עולם ולא שלטה בהן רמה ותולעה ואלו הן. אברהם ויצחק ויעקב ומשה ואהרן ועמרם אביהם. וי״א אף דוד שנאמר (שם טז) לכן שמח לבי ויגל כבודי אף בשרי ישכון לבטח:


The following seven patriarchs have gone to their eternal rest with great honour and worms and maggots had no dominion over them, viz.: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Miriam and their father Amram.⁴² Some say: Also David, as it is stated, *Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth; my flesh also dwelleth in safety*.⁴³

footnotes:
⁴² In B.B. 17a (Sonc. ed., p. 86), ‘and Benjamin the son of Jacob’.
⁴³ Ps. 16, 9, the last words being understood as ‘unaffected by worms’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/1:18)


ט׳ נכנסו בחייהם בג״ע. ואלו הן חנוך בן ירד ואליהו ומשיח ואליעזר עבד אברהם וחירם מלך צור ועבד מלך הכושי ויעבץ בנו של רבי יהודה הנשיא ובתיה בת פרעה וסרח בת אשר ויש אומרים אף ר׳ יהושע בן לוי:


There were nine⁴⁴ who entered the Garden of Eden alive, viz.: Enoch the son of Yered, Elijah, the Messiah, Eliezer the servant of Abraham, Hiram, king of Tyre,⁴⁵ has crept in by mistake and the text should read ‘Hiram of Tyre’, who was of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Kings 7, 13f.). Ebed-melech the Cushite, Jabeẓ the son of R. Judah the Prince, Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, and Seraḥ the daughter of Asher. Some say: Also R. Joshua b. Levi.

footnotes:
⁴⁴ For the list, cf. KR III, p. 461, and notes
⁴⁵ It is more likely that the word king



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:1)


כל דרכיך יהיו לשם שמים. הוי אוהב את השמים וירא מן השמים. הוי חרד ושש על כל המצות.


Let all your undertakings be for the name of Heaven.² Love Heaven and fear Heaven. Hurry to perform in gladness all the precepts.

footnotes:
² Having a sincere and high purpose. ‘Heaven’ is a term for God.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:2)


שב לפני הזקנים והטה אזנך לשמוע את דבריהם והקשב אזניך לדברי חבירך. אל תהי נבהל להשיב. ותהא מחשב דברים כענין. ואומר על ראשון ראשון ועל אחרון אחרון. והוי מודה על האמת. ואל תדבר בפני מי שגדול ממך בחכמה.


Sit before the Elders and incline your ear to hear their words. Listen carefully to the words of your fellow; be not hasty to answer but give proper thought to your words. Speak of the first [point] first and of the last [point] last, and admit the truth. Speak not before him who is greater than you in wisdom.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:3)


ואם חפצת ללמד אל תאמר על מה שלא שמעת שמעתי. ואם שאלוך דבר קטן ואי אתה יודע בו אל תבוש לומר איני יודע. ואם שנית לך ולא שמעת אל תבוש לומר שנה לי. ואל תשא פנים לעצמך לומר (לא) שמעתי.


If you desire to study,³ do not say regarding what you do not understand, ‘I understand’.⁴ If you are questioned on [even] a trivial matter and you are not acquainted with it, be not ashamed to say, ‘I do not know’. If you were taught something which you did not grasp, be not ashamed to say [to the teacher], ‘Repeat it to me’ and do not pretend to yourself ‘I understood it’.

footnotes:
³ H adds ‘the Torah’.
⁴ GRA reads: ‘and if he desires to teach [you a certain subject], do not say, “I have heard it” ’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:4)


עשה דברים לשום פעולתן לדבר בהם לשמים: אל תשימם כעטרה להתעטר בהן. ולא כקורדום לאכול בהן ולא כמר לחפור בהן. קבל עליך דברי תורה בצער. ואל תהי מבקש עלבונך: חשבון יפה ופרק טוב יש הבטחה ויש אמתי:


Do [good] deeds for the sake of their Maker⁵, interprets, ‘for the performance of them’, i.e. doing good for its own sake and not from an interested motive. and speak of them⁶ for their own sake.⁷ Make not of them a crown wherewith to adorn yourself, an axe with which to chop or a spade with which to dig.⁸ Undertake to study the Torah [even] in straitened circumstances and disregard any insult. A well-ordered [moral] stock-taking and a virtuous adolescence [yield] security and truth.⁹

footnotes:
⁵ i.e. God, Who decreed them (so RN to Ned. 62a); but Baḥya ibn Paḳuda, in the Introduction to his Duties of the Heart
⁶ viz. words of Torah.
⁷ i.e. do not study in order to be called a Sage or Rabbi; cf. Ned. 62a (Sonc. ed., p. 197). So according to the emended text of GRA.
⁸ Cf. Aboth IV, 7 (Sonc. ed., IV, 5, p. 46).
⁹ GRA’s emendation may mean: ‘and your security will be real’, or, ‘your promise [which you give] will be true’. An alternative rendering of V may be: ‘[If your deeds] are well considered, and you have good breeding, your promise will be trustworthy’. Cf. the reading in KR IV, 7, p. 466.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:5)


הוי אוהב את התורה ומכבד את התורה. אוהב את הצדקות ואת התוכחות ואת המישרים. ואל תרדוף אחר כבוד. ואל תגיס דעתך בהוראה. דע שמן היום למחר בין שהוא שלך בין שאינו שלך . את שלך אינו שלך ואת שאינו שלך למה הוא לך (והיה שלך) עליו הכתוב אומר (חבקוק ב׳:ו׳) הוי המרבה לא לו עד מתי ומכביד עליו עבטיט. למוד להיות גומר בטוב.


Love and honour the Torah; love righteous ways, reproofs¹⁰ (Prov. 9, 8). and uprightness. Do not run after honour; do not be presumptuous in giving decisions.
Realize that from now until tomorrow everything you have, whether it belongs to you or not, is not yours;¹¹ because what is yours is [in reality] not yours, so how can what is not yours be yours! Of him who regards what is not his as his own, Scripture declares, *Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! How long? and that ladeth himself with many pledges!*¹² Accustom yourself to end on an auspicious note.¹³

footnotes:
¹⁰ Levelled at you. Cf. Reprove a wise man, and he will love thee
¹¹ ‘Is not yours’ is added by GRA.
¹² Hab. 2, 6.
¹³ i.e. if you must criticize or predict misfortune, your last words should inspire confidence and comfort. Or, ‘accustom yourself to finish anything good which you began to do’, otherwise it will be credited to him who completes it. Other possible interpretations are: ‘Accustom yourself to complete a deal with goodness’, i.e. there should be no cause for resentment by the other party; ‘Accustom yourself to end everything well’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:6)


הוי עלוב ואהוב לכל ושפל רוח [בפני כל אדם הוי כנוד שאינו בקוע וכפתח שאינו נפתח להכניס את הרוח וכאסקופא התחתון שהכל דשין בה ס״א] ולשון רכה הוי קל לראש ונוח לתשחורת. סוחר טוב. ורווח כתף.


Be modest and amiable towards all, and be humble and gentle of speech. Be quick [to render service] to a superior and easy of approach to a suppliant [for your service].¹⁴ [Be like] a good merchant¹⁵ and broad-shouldered.¹⁶, ‘liberal with money’. Another interpretation is: ‘Be like a good merchant (i.e. well stocked with goods so that a customer need not be kept waiting while the required article is brought from outside), and like a carrier who can carry a big load easily’. The meaning may then be: Be well stocked and carry a heavy load of learning, so that you are ready to supply knowledge to an inquirer.

footnotes:
¹⁴ Cf. DER II, p. 540, n. 41.
¹⁵ Who can distinguish between the genuine and the spurious; so know how to react towards different types of persons.
¹⁶ i.e. able to deal with all types. H reads reḥab kesef


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:7)


הרחק מן המביא לידי עבירה. הוי נרתע מחטא הקל שלא יביאך לחטא חמור. הוי רץ למצוה קלה ובורח מן העבירה שמא תביאך לחמורה.


Keep aloof from anything which may bring you to sin. Recoil from [even] a minor sin that it may not lead you to a major sin. Hasten to [perform] a light precept¹⁷ and flee¹⁸ from even] a trivial transgression lest it will lead you to commit a grave transgression.

footnotes:
¹⁷ Cf. Ps. 119, 60. One is more liable to be slack and procrastinating with an easy task and so forget it; to obviate this a man should hasten to perform it as soon as it presents itself.
¹⁸ Not merely avoid, but put as long a distance as possible between yourself and transgression.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:8)


יהי כבוד חבירך חביב עליך כשלך. הוי מיקר את כל האדם. אל תאמר אחנוף לזה שיאכילני ולזה שישקני ולזה שילבישני ולזה שיכסני מוטב שתתבייש מעצמך ואל תתבייש מאחרים. ואל יביישך [שינייך] ואל יבזך פיך. ואל יקללך לשונך ואל יכלימוך שפתיך. ואל תשתחוה לדבריך:


Let the honour of your fellow be as dear to you as your own.¹⁹ Show respect to all persons; say not, ‘I will flatter this man that he may give me to eat, or that he may give me to drink, or another man that he may clothe me, or yet another that he may give me shelter’.²⁰
It is better that you be ashamed of yourself²¹ than be put to shame by others.²² Let not your teeth bring shame upon you,²³ nor your mouth bring you to abuse.²⁴ Let not your tongue [cause others to] curse you or your lips discredit you, and do not bow down to your words.²⁵, ‘do not spread your words’, i.e. do not be verbose.

footnotes:
¹⁹ Cf. Aboth II, 15 (Sonc. ed., II, 10, p. 20).
²⁰ Cf. Beẓah 32b (Sonc. ed., p. 165): ‘He who is dependent on another’s table, the world is dark for him and his life is no life’.
²¹ i.e. be the first to recognize your faults and rectify them.
²² Cf. Sanh. 42a (Sonc. ed., p. 274).
²³ i.e. by spending more than you can afford on food so that you become reduced in circumstances.
²⁴ By drinking more than is good for you.
²⁵ Do not speak in haste without premeditation so that you will not have to humble yourself by asking pardon or having to retract. Other possible interpretations are: Do not regard your words as dogmatic; or, do not be self-opinionated; or, do not be a slave to your words, i.e. refrain from making a promise. H reads tishtaḥ


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:9)


אם חפץ אתה להדבק באהבת חבירך. הוי נושא ונותן בטובתו. ואם אתה רוצה להתרחק מחטא צא וחשוב ועיין בסופו. חשוק נפשך במצוה שנן ורנן בפתחיה.


If you desire to secure your fellow’s love, concern yourself with his welfare. If you want to keep away from sin, go, reflect and consider its consequences well. Take delight in the performance of a *miẓwah*, study hard and exult in [carrying it out] in all its details.²⁶, but there is no MS. confirmation for it. A suggested reading is, *shekan urebaẓ biftaḥeha*, ‘Dwell and couch at the doors of [the Academy]’; i.e. by constant study make yourself familiar with the *miẓwoth*.

footnotes:
²⁶ So GRA who conjectures bifraṭeha


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/2:10)


אם הטיבות הרבה יהי בעיניך מעט ואל תאמר משלי הטיבותי. אלא שהטיב לך. וצריך אתה ליתן הודאה לשמים. ואם הטיבוך מעט יהיה בעיניך הרבה. אל תאמר בשביל מעשיו ההגונים הטיבו לי. אלא בשביל מעשיו שאינן הגונים לי הטיבו לי שנאמר (דברים ז) ומשלם לשנאיו אל פניו להאבידו ואם הריעות מעט יהי בעיניך הרבה ואמור אוי לי כי חטאתי אוי לי כי בא מכשול על ידי. אם הריעוך הרבה יהי בעיניך מעט ואמור כמעט נגביתי והלא יתר מכאן הייתי ראוי:


If you did [someone] a great favour regard it as small, and do not say, ‘I did this good act with my own [money]’. Rather was it [from what God] had graciously given you and you should offer thanks to Heaven.²⁷ If others have done you a slight favour regard it as if it were great, and do not say, ‘The favour was done to me because of my worthy acts’, but [say, ‘In spite of] my unworthy acts a favour was done to me’, as it is stated, *And repayeth them that hate Him to their face, to destroy them*.²⁸
If you wronged someone slightly regard it as a great wrong and exclaim, ‘Woe is me, for I have sinned! Woe is me, because harm was done through me!’ If others did you a great wrong regard it as small and exclaim, ‘I suffered slightly; I deserved more’.

footnotes:
²⁷ For the means with which to do good.
²⁸ Deut. 7, 10. It is better not to receive the reward in this world but to store it up for the hereafter



## Chapter 3

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:1)


תן דעתך עד שיצא מפיך חשוב מעשיך בדרך ארץ. ותן שכר לפסיעותך. צדק הדין עליך והוצא עצמך [מן התרעומות].


Reflect before [the word] issues from your mouth. Consider your actions in accordance with good manners. Set a reward for every step you take.¹ Submit to [divine] judgment and refrain from grumbling.

footnotes:
¹ i.e. see that your steps are directed to perform deeds which deserve a reward.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:2)


הוי דן את חבירך לכף זכות. ואל תכריעהו לכף חובה. הוי שש בחלקך. והתנאה במיעוטך. ואל תשנא את המוכיחך. יהי חלקך מבורך לעולם. עין טובה ונפש שביעה:


Judge your fellow in the scale of merit² and do not turn the scale against him.³ Rejoice in your lot and enjoy the little you have. Hate not him who reproves you. Your lot will always be blessed if you possess a bountiful eye⁴ and a contented soul.

footnotes:
² Seek a favourable interpretation of his actions even though they seem suspicious. Cf. Aboth I, 6 (Sonc. ed., p. 5).
³ Take a charitable view of his deeds.
⁴ Well disposed, generous; cf. Prov. 22, 9.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:3)


למוד לשונך לומר איני יודע שמא תתבדה ותאחז.


Accustom your tongue to say, ‘I do not know’, lest you be led to falsehood and be apprehended.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:4)


אם רפית במצוה אחת. סופך לרפות באחרת. (וכן) כיוצא בה אם הקלות פומך להקל מצוה אחת סופך להקל באחרת (וכן) כיוצא בה (ואין לך בצערך). ואם עברת על דברי תורה ברצונך מעבירים אותך ברצונך ושלא ברצונך. אם נטלת שאינו שלך. את שלך יטלו ממך.


If you are negligent in [the performance of] one precept you will eventually be negligent with another like it. If you belittle⁵ one precept you will eventually belittle others like it.⁶ If you transgress the words of the Torah intentionally, you will be made to transgress them intentionally or unintentionally.⁷ [58*b*] If you take for yourself anything which is not yours, what is yours will be taken from you.

footnotes:
⁵ lit. ‘speak lightly of’.
⁶ V adds in brackets ‘and you have done nothing for your trouble’ in fulfilling the precepts since you regard them of small worth.
⁷ Circumstances will make it impossible for you to perform the precepts even if you are desirous of making good former lapses.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:5)


והוי זהיר בקדשים בין בנתינתן בין באכילתן.


Be careful with consecrated objects both when giving them⁸ or Levite; do not withhold them. and when eating them.⁹

footnotes:
⁸ To the kohen
⁹ They must be eaten in a state of ritual cleanliness.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:6)


הוי עלוב ואהוב להשיב ליודעך [ושפל רוח בפני כל האדם לאנשי ביתך יותר מכל אדם ואם תתרעם ותלחם עם ביתך סופך לגיהנם ס״א] עלוב ואהוב לכל אדם ולאנשי ביתך.


Be humble and affable to all persons and particularly to the members of your household.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ According to the text emended by GRA. V and H read: ‘Be humble and affable to return [a salutation] to your acquaintance. Be lowly of spirit with all men, with the members of your household more than with all men; and if you grumble and fight with your household, your end is for Gehinnom’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:7)


תחלת נדרים פתח לאולת. תחלת טומאות פתח לעבודת כוכבים. תחלת קלות ראש בנשים פתח לניאוף:


The first stage of vowing leads to folly; the first stage of [ritual] uncleanness leads to idolatry; the first stage of levity with women leads to unchastity.¹¹

footnotes:
¹¹ Cf. Ned. 20a (Sonc. ed., p. 56).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:8)


אם ערבת ערבת על מנת לשלם ואם לוית לוית ע״מ לפרוע. ואם הלוית הלוית ע״מ לתבוע. הוי מחשב להשבה ולהפסיק את החשבון. קנה שם טוב קנה לעצמו. קנה לו דברי תורה קנה לו חיי העוה״ב.


If you make yourself a surety [for another] it should be with the object of paying [that surety];¹² or if you become a guarantor it should be with the object of paying [the guarantee].¹³ If you borrow [money] it should be with the object of repaying [the loan];¹⁴ and if you lend money bear in mind that you may have to claim it¹⁵ and that you might [even] have to make a settlement.¹⁶, ‘lose the sum’.
If one has acquired for himself a good name,¹⁷ he has acquired it for himself.¹⁸ If one has acquired for himself words of Torah, he has acquired for himself the life of the World to Come.

footnotes:
¹² If called upon to do so.
¹³ Therefore do not offer to become a guarantor lightheartedly.
¹⁴ So borrow only if you are in a position to repay.
¹⁵ And have difficulty in collecting it.
¹⁶ And lose part of the sum loaned. Another reading is lehafsid
¹⁷ Cf. Prov. 22, 1; Eccl. 7, 1; Aboth II, 8 (Sonc. ed., II, 7, p. 17).
¹⁸ In the sense that, unlike any other possession, it cannot be transmitted to another.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:9)


אין הביישן למד. ואין הקפדן מלמד [ואין עם הארץ חסיד ואין בור ירא חטא] ולא כל המרבה בסחורה מחכים: [ושים עצמך בתורה יותר מעל סחורה]:


A shamefaced person is not apt to learn, nor is an impatient person fitted to teach. An ignorant person¹⁹ cannot be pious, an uncultured person²⁰ sin-fearing,²¹ or anyone who engages much²² in business become a scholar. Put your mind, therefore, to the study of the Torah rather than to business.

footnotes:
¹⁹ For this passage, cf. Aboth II, 6 (Sonc. ed., II, 5, p. 15, nn. 3-8).
²⁰ One devoid of knowledge and ethical principles.
²¹ He may avoid sin from fear of the consequences but not from ethical motives.
²² And leaves little or no time for study.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:10)


חמש עשרה מדות נאמרו בת״ח ואלו הן. נאה בביאתו. חסיד בישיבתו. ערום ביראה. פקח בדעת. חכם בדרכיו. כונס וזכרן. מרבה להשיב. שואל כענין ומשיב כהלכה. ומשיב על כל פרק ופרק דבר. הולך אצל חכם. ולמד ע״מ ללמד. ועל מנת לעשות:


Fifteen characteristics are mentioned in connection with a scholar, viz.: he is decorous in his entering and leaving,²³ modest in his sitting,²⁴ subtle²⁵ in the fear [of God], shrewd in knowledge, discerning in his ways, [his mind] is absorptive and retentive, he answers fully,²⁶ asks in accordance with the subject-matter²⁷ and answers in accordance with the accepted decisions, listens [to others]²⁸ and enlarges upon each subject, goes [to seek instruction] from the wise and learns in order to teach and practise.

footnotes:
²³ ‘And leaving’ is inserted by GRA.
²⁴ Does not rush to occupy a front seat.
²⁵ In devising ways of manifesting his fear; cf. Ber. 17a (Sonc. ed., p. 102).
²⁶ He takes a considerable time before answering.
²⁷ Cf. above I, 1, n. 6.
²⁸ Added by GRA.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/3:11)


אל תהא כאסקופה העליונה שמונעת את הרגלים (וסופה להסתר ס״א). ולא כאמצעית שכל היושב על ידו זועף וסופה להסתר. היה כאסקופה התחתונה שרוב בני אדם דורסין אותה לסוף כל הבנין כולה נסתר והיא במקומה עומדת:


Be not like the topmost lintel which is inaccessible to the feet or like the doorpost²⁹ where anyone who sits by it is troubled and which ultimately collapses. Be like the doorstep³⁰ on which most people tread but which remains when the whole building is in ruins.³¹

footnotes:
²⁹ lit. ‘the middle [post]’.
³⁰ lit. ‘the nethermost post’.
³¹ Referring to the quality of humility. GRA emends the text to read: ‘Be not like a lintel which can injure the face (by a person crashing into it), nor like the doorpost which can hurt the legs and ultimately collapses; but be like the doorstep on which most people tread and which remains in its place even when the whole building collapses’.



## Chapter 4

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:1)


תלמידי חכמים נאים בחבורה. ואין עמי הארץ נאים בחבורה.


Scholars lend dignity to a company,¹ but not so ignorant men.

footnotes:
¹ Or, ‘behave well in a company’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:2)


העוסק במקרא מדה שאינה מדה. במשנה מדה שנוטלין עליה שכר. תלמוד אין לך מדה גדולה מזו. ולעולם הוי רץ למשנה יותר מן הש״ס.


He who occupies himself [only] with the study of Scripture is but of indifferent merit;² with Mishnah is meritorious and rewarded for it; with Talmud there can be nothing more meritorious. Yet run always to the Mishnah more than to the *Shas*.³

footnotes:
² lit. ‘it is meritorious and not meritorious’, because the Written Torah can only be understood with the aid of the Oral Torah.
³ Because it is more easily absorbed. For this passage, cf. B.M. 33a, b (Sonc. ed., p. 206).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:3)


עשה תורתך בחנם ולא תטול עליה שכר שהמקום נתנה בחנם. ואין נוטלין שכר על דברי תורה. ואם אתה נוטל שכר על דברי תורה נמצאת מחריב את כל העולם כולו: אל תאמר אין לי ממון. שכל הממון שלו הוא שנאמר (חגי ב׳:ח׳) לי הכסף ולי הזהב (אמר) [נאום] ה׳ צבאות. אם עשית צדקה תזכה לממון. ואם זכית לממון עשה ממנו צדקה בעוד שהוא בידך קנה ממנו העולם הזה ותנחול העוה״ב שאם אין אתה עושה ממנו צדקה יעוף פתאום שנאמר (משלי כ״ג:ה׳) התעיף עיניך בו ואיננו:


Do your [teaching of] Torah gratuitously and accept no remuneration for it; because the Omnipresent gave it gratuitously⁴, this does not apply to Scripture, for the teaching of which a fee is allowed. and one may not take a fee for the [teaching of] words of Torah. If you should accept remuneration for the [teaching of] words of Torah, you will consequently destroy [the moral constitution of] the entire world. Say not, ‘I have no money’, since all money is His,⁵ as it is stated, *Mine is the silver, and Mine the gold, saith the Lord of hosts*.⁶
If you practise charity you will merit wealth; and if you merited wealth practise charity with it. While you still possess it [live in such a manner that you] gain through it this world and also inherit the World to Come; for if you do not practise charity with it, it will suddenly disappear, as it is stated, *Wilt thou set thine eyes upon it? It is gone*.⁷

footnotes:
⁴ Cf. Ned. 36b-37a (Sonc. ed., p. 113). As Moses taught the Elders gratuitously so must they pass their teaching on to others without pay. According to the Talmud, loc. cit.
⁵ He will provide you with sustenance without having to take payment for teaching.
⁶ Hag. 2, 8.
⁷ Prov. 23, 5.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:4)


אל תאמר איש חכם פלוני ואני איני חכם. שלא שמשת כיוצא בו. ואל תאמר איש פלוני עשיר ואני איני עשיר. שאין כל אדם זוכה לשתי שולחנות. ואל תאמר איש פלוני נאה ואני מכוער. שבשעת המיתה אדם עושה כנבלה. ולא עוד אלא שהנבלה מוכרה לנכרי או נתנה בחנם ונבלת אדם אין כל בריה יכולה להשגיח עליה. [אל תאמר איש פלוני צדיק ואני איני צדיק ששניכם עתידים ליתן את הדין ס״א] אל תאמר איש פלוני גבור ואני חלש. שאין גבורה אלא בתורה שנאמר (תהילים ק״ג:כ׳) ברכו ה' מלאכיו גבורי כח עושי דברו לשמוע בקול דברו.


Say not, ‘That man is wise⁸ but I am not wise’,⁹ because you did not attend [upon scholars] as he did.¹⁰ Say not, ‘That man is rich but I am not rich’,¹¹ because not everyone has the privilege to enjoy two tables.¹² Say not, ‘That man is handsome but I am ugly’, because at the hour of death man becomes carrion; furthermore [animal] carrion may be sold to a Gentile or may be given as a gift, but no one cares for human carrion.¹³ Say not, ‘That man is righteous but I am not righteous, because both of you are destined to give an account before the Most High. Say not, ‘That man is strong but I am weak’,¹⁴ because strength is only with [them who fulfil] the Torah, as it is stated, *Bless the Lord, ye angels of His, ye mighty in strength, that fulfil His word, hearkening unto the voice of His word*.¹⁵

footnotes:
⁸ Endowed by nature with great intellectual gifts.
⁹ i.e. I am not so endowed and therefore it is useless for me to study.
¹⁰ One must make every effort to gain knowledge; cf. Meg. 6b (Sonc. ed., p. 30).
¹¹ Although I am more God-fearing than he.
¹² i.e. enjoy prosperity in this world and the bliss of the hereafter.
¹³ So in death the difference between the handsome and the ugly ceases to exist.
¹⁴ And therefore unable to control my sinful desires.
¹⁵ Ps. 103, 20. So occupy yourself with the study of the Torah and you will increase moral strength.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:5)


דברי אלו יהיו על לבבך. דע מאין באת ולאן אתה הולך ולפני מי אתה עתיד ליתן דין וחשבון.


Take these words to heart: Know whence you came, and whither you go, and before Whom you are destined to give an account and reckoning.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ Cf. Aboth III, 1 (Sonc. ed., p. 26).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:6)


אל תתן עיניך בממון שאינו שלך. שהן משקעות שערי הרקיע. ואל תתן אזניך לשמוע דברים בטלים. שהן נכוות תחלה לאיבריך [ואל תתן עיניך בממון שאינו שלך שהוא מאפיל אותך כאישון לילה ואפילה ס״א] ואל יספר פיך לשון הרע שהוא נכנס תחלה לדון. ואל ימצא בידך לשון הרע לא דבר רע ולא דבר גזל שכל אבריך יעידו בך. ואל יקדמוך רגליך לדבר עבירה שמא יקדמך מלאך המות. אל תתירא מב״ד שלמטה. שהרי עדיך אוהבי ממון הם. אלא היה מתירא מב״ד של מעלה [שהרי יש לך עדים] שיהיו מעידין בך למעלה. ולא עוד אלא שמכריזין עליך(מריבה) בכל שעה ושעה.


Eye not [enviously] another’s wealth because it undermines the gates of heaven.¹⁷
Suffer not your ears to listen to idle chatter, because they are burnt first of [all] the organs.¹⁸ Eye not [enviously] another’s wealth, because it may cast you into thick darkness and gloom.
Let not your mouth repeat calumny, because it is the first to be summoned for judgment. Let there not be found with you calumny, any evil thing or anything stolen, because all your limbs will testify against you. Let not your feet hurry you to commit a sin lest the Angel of Death come to meet you.¹⁹
Be not afraid of an earthly court because the witnesses against you are lovers of money,²⁰, p. 587, in agreement with a variant cited in H, omits the negative and renders: ‘Fear the earthly tribunal, even though witnesses against you can be bribed; fear yet more the heavenly tribunal’.] but fear the heavenly Court because there are witnesses above who testify against you, and moreover [your sins] proclaim war on you incessantly.

footnotes:
¹⁷ To the envious the luminaries of heaven shine but dimly.
¹⁸ lit. ‘of the limbs’. From hearing unworthy or idle talk he may proceed to speak unworthy or idle words and then do unworthy or idle acts. The ear is, accordingly, the first organ to ‘catch fire’; cf. Keth. 5b (Sonc. ed., p. 18).
¹⁹ Lest you die before you make atonement.
²⁰ i.e. subject to bribery. [H. Loewe, Rabbinic Anthology


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:7)


אם עשית דברי בשמחה. פמליא שלי תצא לשחרך. ואף אני בעצמי אצא לקראתך. ואומר לך בואך בשלום.


If you fulfilled My words joyfully, My heavenly household will go out to greet you and I will greet you with the words, ‘Enter in peace’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:8)


עיניך שלא נתת בממון שאינו שלך. הם יאירו באישון חושך שנאמר (ישעיהו נ״ח:י׳) וזרח בחשך אורך ואפלתך כצהרים (הט) אזניך שלא שמעת בהם דברים בטלים הם יקשיבו לך שלום בעולם ויאזינו לחיי העוה״ב שנאמר (שם ל) ואזניך תשמענה דבר מאחריך לאמר זה הדרך לכו בו כי תאמינו וכי תשמאילו. פיך שלא סיפר לשון הרע עליו יהרגו כל בעלי הרוגים: פיך שעסק בתורה עליו יתברכו כל בעלי ברכה. ידיך ששמרת מגזל. מה יעשו לך כל בני עולה: ידיך שלא קפצת מן הצדקה. מה יעשו לך כל בעלי כסף וזהב: רגליך שלא קדמוך לדבר עבירה. מה יעשה לך מלאך המות.


Because your eyes have not looked [enviously] on another’s wealth, they will shine amidst thick darkness and gloom, as it is stated, *Then shall thy light rise in darkness, and thy gloom be as the noon-day*.²¹ Because your ears have not listened to idle chatter they will hear [words of] peace for you in [this] world and cause you to hear them in the World to Come, as it is stated, *And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying: ‘This is the way, walk ye in it; when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left*.’²² XXX, 21. Because your mouth did not recount calumny, all your adversaries will be slain by it.²³ Because your mouth occupied itself with [the teaching of] the Torah, all who are worthy of a blessing will bless themselves through it.²⁴ Because you withheld your hands from plunder, what can evil persons do to you? Because you did not close your hands from almsgiving, what can violent persons²⁵ do to you? Because your feet did not hurry you to commit a sin, what can the Angel of Death do to you?

footnotes:
²¹ Isa. 58, 10.
²² ibid.
²³ So GRA.
²⁴ They will wish for no greater blessing than will come to you for what you have earned by your mouth.
²⁵ lit. ‘owners of an arm’, the emendation of GRA. V has ‘owners of silver and gold’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/4:9)


דברי אלה התריתי לפניך ומה שתרצה תעשה ולא תאמר [לא] התרו בי: 
(אלו הפרקים נמצאו במחזור וויטרי)


I admonish you with these words of Mine. You can do as you please²⁶ but do not say, ‘I was not warned’.

footnotes:
²⁶ Since man is endowed with free will.



## Chapter 5

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:1)


מי שהוא ת״ח לא יאכל מעומד לא ילקלק באצבעותיו ולא יגסה בפני חבירו מיעוט שיחה מיעוט שחוק מיעוט שינה מיעוט תענוג מיעוט הן מיעוט לאו לאו:


A scholar should not eat standing, lick his fingers or belch in the presence of his fellow. He talks little, jokes little, sleeps in moderation, is frugal in pleasures and minimizes ‘[Yes], yes’ or ‘No, no’.¹

footnotes:
¹ Cf. Shebu. 36a (Sonc. ed., p. 211) where the repetition of ‘yes’ and ‘no’ is regarded as an oath. It may perhaps also mean to be sparing in making promises.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:2)


לעולם יהא אדם יודע אצל מי הוא יושב ואצל מי הוא עומד ואצל מי מיסב ואצל מי הוא מסיח ואצל מי הוא חותם שטרותיו:


A man should always make a point of knowing with whom he is sitting or standing, with whom he is sitting at table, with whom he is conversing and who is his co-signatory to a deed.²

footnotes:
² Cf. Sanh. 23a (Sonc. ed., p. 131).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:3)


בארבעה דברים תלמידי חכמים ניכרים. בכיסן בכוסן בכעסן ובעטיפתן. וי״א אף בדיבור:


By four things are scholars³ recognizable: by their cup,⁴ their purse,⁵ their temper⁶ (purse), *kos* (cup) and *ka‘as* (temper). The last indicates self-control. and by their attire.⁷ Some say: Also by their speech.⁸

footnotes:
³ In ‘Erub. 65b (Sonc. ed., p. 455) the wording is: ‘By three things may a person’s’, etc., not only a scholar.
⁴ By the amount of liquor they consume.
⁵ By what they spend their money on.
⁶ In the Heb. there is an effective alliteration: kis
⁷ A scholar was expected to maintain cleanliness in his attire. Cf. Shab. 114a (Sonc. ed., p. 557).
⁸ ‘Erub. adds ‘also by their laughter’ and omits ‘by their attire’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:4)


הדר תורה חכמה. הדר חכמה ענוה. הדר ענוה יראה. הדר יראה מצוה. הדר מצוה צניעות.


The adornment of [knowledge of] Torah is wisdom, the adornment of wisdom is humility, the adornment of humility is fear [of God], the adornment of the fear [of God] is the performance of meritorious deeds, the adornment of the performance of meritorious deeds is modesty.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ i.e. the unostentatious manner in which they are done.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/5:5)


לא יהא אדם ער בין הישינים ולא ישן בין העירים. ולא בוכה בין השוחקים ולא שוחק בין הבוכים. ולא יושב בין העומדים. ולא עומד בין היושבים. ולא קורא בין השונים. ולא שונה בין הקוראים. כללו של דבר אל ישנה אדם ממנהג הבריות:


A man should not be awake when among those who are asleep or asleep when among those who are awake. He should not weep when among those who are joyous or be joyous when among those who weep. He should not be sitting when among those who are standing or standing when among those who are sitting. He should not study Scripture when among those who study Mishnah or study Mishnah when among those who study Scripture. This is the general rule: A man should not act differently from the practice of his fellow-men.



## Chapter 6

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:1)


ארבעה דברים גנאי לתלמידים לא יהא אדם מחשיך בדרך ולא יצא כשהוא מבוסם ולא יכנס לבית הכנסת באחרונה ולא ירבה בישיבת של עמי הארץ:


Four things are unbecoming to scholars. One should not start out on a journey by night,¹ go out scented,² be the last to enter the Synagogue,³, reads *‘Beth Hammidrash’*. or frequent the society of ignorant persons.

footnotes:
¹ Either because of danger or not to arouse suspicion of immoral intention.
² According to Ber. 43b (Sonc. ed., p. 266) this applies to scenting one’s clothes and in a place where people are suspected of sodomy.
³ Ber. loc. cit.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:2)


לכניסה הגדול קודם. ליציאה הקטן קודם. לעליית הסולם הגדול קודם. לירידת הסולם הקטן קודם. לבית הוועד הגדול קודם. לבית הכלא הקטן קודם. לברכה הגדול קודם. והמהלך שואל בשלום היושב.


On entering the elder precedes, on leaving the younger precedes;⁴ when ascending a staircase the elder precedes, when descending a staircase the younger precedes; [when entering] a Council Chamber the elder precedes; [when entering] a prison the younger precedes; to pronounce a blessing⁵ the elder takes precedence. The passer-by greets one who is sitting.

footnotes:
⁴ Or, ‘the more important … the less important’. Cf. Ber. 61a (Sonc. ed., p. 381): ‘In conferring honour we commence with the greatest’.
⁵ At the beginning of a meal or to recite Grace after it.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:3)


לא יהא אדם מיסב בפני מי שגדול ממנו: בא לפרוס את הככר בוצע ממקום הצלי. ואם בא לאכול את הצנון ובצל אוכל ממקום העלין ולא יטול את הככר ויתלוש (בו שיש) ויחזרנו על השולחן: בא לשתות ברבים הופך פניו לצד אחר וישתה.


No person should sit down at table to eat before his elders [have taken their seat]. When cutting off a piece of bread [for Grace before meals] one should do so from the part that is baked into a crust.⁶ When one is about to eat a leek or onion, he should begin to eat from the leaves.⁷ One should not take hold of a loaf, bite a piece off and place it back upon the table. When about to drink water in public, one should turn his face away and drink.⁸

footnotes:
⁶ Cf. above, p. 553.
⁷ And not from the top; cf. above, p. 553.
⁸ Because it is customary for a scholar to exercise privacy both in eating and drinking.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:4)


ולא יהא אדם לא נוקדן ולא עומקן ולא גרגרן. ומותר על קלקלתו ואינו מתכבד מקלון חבירו:


A man should not be a caviller, trickster or tippler. He should overlook an insult and not glorify himself by his fellow’s humiliation.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ Cf. Meg. 28a (Sonc. ed., p. 168).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/6:5)


תחלת עבירה הרהור הלב. שניה לה ליצנות שלישית לה גסות הרוח. רביעית לה אכזריות. חמישית לה הבטלה. ששית לה שנאת חנם. שביעית לה עין הרע. הוא שאמר שלמה (משלי כ״ו:כ״ה) כי יחנן (את) קולו אל תאמן בו וגו׳:


The first stage in committing a sin is impure thought, the second is scoffing, the third haughtiness, the fourth cruelty, the fifth idleness, the sixth causeless hatred and the seventh an evil eye.¹⁰ That is what Solomon said, *When he speaketh fair, believe him not; for there are seven abominations in his heart*.¹¹

footnotes:
¹⁰ An envious nature.
¹¹ Prov. 26, 25.



## Chapter 7

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:1)


שבעה דברים בגולם ושבעה בחכם. חכם אינו מדבר בפני מי שגדול ממנו בחכמה ובמנין ואינו נכנס לתוך דברי חבירו ואינו נבהל להשיב שואל כענין ומשיב כהלכ׳ ואומר על ראשון ראשון ועל אחרון אחרון ועל מה שלא שמע אומר לא שמעתי ומודה על האמת וחילופיהן בגולם:


There are seven characteristics in an uncultured man¹ Cf. Aboth V, 10 (Sonc. ed., V, 7, pp. 64f.). and seven in a wise man. A wise man does not speak before one who is greater than he in wisdom and in number,² does not enter into the midst of the words of his fellow,³ is not hasty to answer; he asks in accordance with the subject-matter and answers in accordance with the accepted decision, speaks on the first [point] first and on the last [point] last, concerning what he has not heard he says, ‘I have not heard it’,⁴ and acknowledges the truth.⁵ The reverse of these are in an uncultured man.

footnotes:
¹ Heb. golem.
² Of years.
³ i.e. does not interrupt.
⁴ Cf. above, p. 571, n. 4.
⁵ He does not consider it inconsistent with his dignity to admit when he is in the wrong.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:2)


ת״ח צריך שיהא צנוע באכילה ובשתייה ברחיצה ובסיכה ובנעילת הסנדל בהליכתו ובעטיפתו ובקולו וברוקו ובמעשיו הטובים. מה כלה זו כל זמן שהיא בבית אביה מצנעת עצמה וכשהיא יוצאת מפרסמת עצמה ואומרת כל מי שיודע בי עדות יבא ויעיד. כך ת״ח צריך שיהא צנוע במעשיו ומפורסם בדרכיו. רודף אחר האמת ולא אחר השקר. אחר האמונה ולא אחר הגזל. אחר ענוה ולא אחר הגסות. אחר השלום ולא אחר המלחמה. אחר עצת זקנים ולא אחר עצת הילדים. אחר הארי ולא אחר האשה:


A scholar must be modest in eating, drinking, washing, anointing,⁶ putting his shoes on, walking, his attire, [the modulation of] his voice, expectorating⁷ and good works.⁸
As a bride keeps herself secluded all the time she is in her father’s house and only makes herself known when she goes out⁹ [as if] to say, ‘Anyone who can testify anything against me,¹⁰ let him come and testify’, so must a scholar be modest in his [good] deeds but renowned for his conduct. He must seek truth and not falsehood, honesty and not robbery, meekness and not haughtiness, peace and not conflict, the counsel of the Elders and not the counsel of the young.¹¹ He should rather walk behind a lion than behind a woman.¹²

footnotes:
⁶ i.e. rubbing with oil after a bath.
⁷ i.e. clearing his throat.
⁸ He should perform them unostentatiously.
⁹ Leaves her father’s house for the wedding ceremony.
¹⁰ Against her virtue.
¹¹ Cf. Meg. 31b (Sonc. ed., p. 192): ‘If old men say to you “Throw down” and young men say to you “Build up”, do the former’.
¹² To avoid unchaste thoughts.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:3)


איזהו מכבד מאכיל ומשקה מלביש ומנעיל מכניס ומוציא אחד הרב ואחד החכם. ואיזהו המבזה לא ישב ולא ידבר במקומו ולא סותר את דבריו.


He honours the wise¹³ [and does not show disrespect towards them.] What is meant by ‘honours the wise’? He gives him food and drink, dresses him and puts his shoes on for him, leads him in and out. This applies to both a teacher¹⁴ and a Sage.¹⁵ What is meant by ‘showing disrespect’? He must not sit in his [accustomed] place, speak¹⁶ in his stead or contradict his words.

footnotes:
¹³ Added by GRA.
¹⁴ A variant is ‘a father’ in agreement with Ḳid. 31b (Sonc. ed., p. 154).
¹⁵ Although he is not his teacher.
¹⁶ In Ḳid. ‘stand’; cf. also Midrash Rabbah, Num., XV, 17 (Sonc. ed., p. 660).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/7:4)


(תני ר' חייא) יפה שתיקה לחכמים ק״ו לטיפשים וכן אמר שלמה [גם] אויל מחריש חכם יחשב [משלי יז] ואין צ״ל חכם מחריש:


R. Ḥiyya taught: Silence is good for the wise and how much more so for fools; and so did Solomon say, *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise*.¹⁷ It is not necessary to say, ‘When a *wise man* holdeth his peace’.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁷ Prov. 17, 28.
¹⁸ Because a wise man knows when to be silent.



## Chapter 8

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:1)


הוי רך כקנה שהרוח נושבת בו לכל רוח שתרצה שאין התורה מתקיימת אלא במי שרוחו נמוכה עליו למה נמשלה תורה למים לומר לך מה דרכו של מים אינן הולכין למקום גבוה אלא למקום נמוך כך אין התורה מתקיימת אלא במי שרוחו נמוכה עליו:


Be pliable like the reed upon which the wind can blow from every direction it chooses;¹ for the Torah can only endure with him who is humble in spirit.
Why is the Torah likened to water?². It is to teach you that as water does not flow [from a lower] to a higher level but [from a higher level] to a lower, so the Torah endures only with him who is humble in spirit.³

footnotes:
¹ Cf. DER IV, p. 545.
² Cf. Isa. 55, 1, Ho, everyone that thirsteth, come ye for water
³ It flows away from him who is haughty; cf. Ta‘an. 7a (Sonc. ed., p. 27).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:2)


הרחק מן הכיעור ומן הדומה לו וקרב לדבר המתקבל ולכל הדומה לו והוי זהיר מהיועצך לפי דרכו


Keep aloof from anything hideous and from whatever resembles it,⁴ and draw near to what [59*a*] is becoming and all that resembles it. Beware of one who counsels you in his own interest.⁵

footnotes:
⁴ Cf. Ḥul. 44b (Sonc. ed., p. 239) and ARN II, 2, p. 18.
⁵ lit. ‘in his own way’; cf. Sanh. 76b (Sonc. ed., p. 517).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:3)


וכל המעביר על מדותיו מעבירין לו על כל פשעיו שנאמר (מיכה ז׳:י״ח) מי אל כמוך נושא עון ועובר על פשע למי נושא עון למי שעובר על פשע:


Who waives his right to retribution⁶ is forgiven all his sins, as it is stated, *Who is a God like unto Thee, that pardoneth the iniquity, and passeth by the transgression*,⁷ [which means,] who is forgiven iniquity? He who passed by transgression [against himself].⁸

footnotes:
⁶ lit. ‘passes by his measures’, i.e. forgoes his right to exact punishment.
⁷ Micah 7, 18.
⁸ Cf. R.H. 17a (Sonc. ed., p. 67).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:4)


כל המתנבל בדברי תורה סופו להתנשא בה שנאמר (משלי ל׳:ל״ב) אם נבלת בהתנשא. אם נבלת בדברי תורה בהתנשא


Whoever abases [*mithnabbel*] himself in connection with words of Torah⁹ will in the end be exalted on its account, as it is stated *If thou hast done foolishly* [*nabalta*] *in lifting up thyself*,¹⁰ [which means,] if you have abased yourself for words of the Torah, in the end you will be exalted.

footnotes:
⁹ i.e. is not ashamed to ask questions which may at first sound foolish; cf. Ber. 63b (Sonc. ed., p. 402).
¹⁰ Prov. 30, 32.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:5)


שכל המתנבל על ד״ת מוסיפין לו חכמה על חכמתו שנאמר (שם ט) תן לחכם ויחכם עוד.


He who seeks [knowledge of] the Torah, added wisdom will be given to him,¹¹ as it is stated, *Give to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser*.¹² IX, 9.

footnotes:
¹¹ Following the emended text of GRA.
¹² ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:6)


כל זמן שאדם חוטא מורא הבריות עליו וכל זמן שאינו חוטא מוראו על הבריות.


So long as a person is a sinner he has fear of his fellow-creatures; but so long as he is not a sinner his fellow-creatures have fear of him.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ They are afraid of his knowing about their guilt.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:7)


וכל המזלזל בדבר אחד בד״ת חייב כרת שנ׳ (במדבר טו) כי דבר ה׳ בזה.


Whoever makes light of a single point of the Torah is liable to *kareth*, as it is stated, *Because he hath despised the word of the Lord … that soul shall utterly be cut off*.¹⁴ And he who makes light of the [precept of] washing the hands will be uprooted from the world.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁴ Num. 15, 31.
¹⁵ Added by GRA. Cf. Soṭah 4b (Sonc. ed., p. 16).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:8)


כל שאין לו בושת פנים במהרה [הוא] חוטא. שנא׳ (ישעיהו ג׳:ט׳) הכרת פניהם ענתה בם. וכל שיש לו בושת פנים לא במהרה [הוא] חוטא שנאמר (שמות כ׳:י״ז) ובעבור תהיה יראתו על פניכם לבלתי תחטאו:


Whoever is not shamefaced will readily sin, as it is stated, *The show of their countenance doth witness against them;*¹⁶ but he who experiences shame¹⁷ will not readily sin, as it is stated, [*And Moses said unto the people: ‘Fear not; for God is come to prove you*] *and that His fear may be before you, that ye sin not*.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁶ Isa. 3, 9.
¹⁷ i.e. who is not callous, but is self-conscious when he is doing wrong.
¹⁸ Ex. 20, 17; cf. Ned. 20a (Sonc. ed., p. 57).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:9)


(כל ת״ח המזלזל בנט״י ה״ז מגונה. מגונה ממנו) האוכל לפני האורח . מגונה ממנו אורח מכניס אורח. מגונה ממנו האוכל לפני ת״ח. אורח המטריח אורח מגונה משלשתן. ר״מ אומר הנוטל מלפניו ונותן לבן בעל הבית. מעשה היה והרג בעל הבית את בנו.


It is unbecoming for a host to eat in the presence of his guest [without inviting him to join him]; it is more unbecoming for one guest to bring in another guest;¹⁹ it is still more unbecoming when one eats in the presence of a scholar. More unbecoming than these three is for a guest to cause trouble to another guest.²⁰ R. Meir said: [Most unbecoming of all is] he who takes [food] set before him and gives it to the host’s child; for it once happened that [through such an action] a host killed his child.²¹

footnotes:
¹⁹ Cf. B.B. 98b (Sonc. ed., p. 410), a saying attributed to Ben Sira.
²⁰ GRA reads ‘his host’.
²¹ Cf. DER IX, 3, p. 559.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:10)


כל המשפיל את עצמו מכוין את שמועתו וכל העובר על דברי חכמים חייב כרת וכל הפוסל פסול. אר״ע כך היה תחילת תשמישי לפני חכמים פעם אחת הייתי מהלך בדרך ומצאתי מת מצוה ונטפלתי בו בארבע׳ מילין עד שהבאתיו למקום בית הקברות וקברתיו וכשבאתי והרציתי דברים לפני ר״א ור' יהושע אמרו לי כל פסיעה ופסיעה שפסעת מעלה עליך כאילו היית שופך דמים אמרו להם למה בשעה שנתכוונתי לזכות נתחייבתי כרשע בשעה שלא נתכוונתי על אחת כמה וכמה באותה שעה לא זזתי מלשמש לחכמים הוא היה אומר דלא שימש לחכמים קטלא חייב:


He who humbles himself will understand his instruction and whoever transgresses the words of the Sages deserves *kareth*.²² Whoever [continually] declares [others] unfit is [himself] unfit.²³
R. ‘Aḳiba said: The beginning of my attendance upon the Sages²⁴ was this. I was once on a journey when I came across a *meth miẓwah* which I carried about four *mil* until I brought it to a cemetery and buried it there. When I appeared before R. Eliezer and R. Joshua and told them what had happened, they said to me, ‘Every step you took is reckoned against you as if you had shed blood’.²⁵ I said to them, ‘If, in a case where I intended to perform a meritorious act I have made myself liable like a wicked person, how much more [will I deserve punishment] when I have no [meritorious] intention! From that moment I did not let an opportunity pass to minister to the Sages’.²⁶ He used to say: One who does not minister to the Sages deserves death.

footnotes:
²² GRA reads: ‘He who attends upon scholars comprehends his instruction, and whoever does not comprehend his instruction deserves death’.
²³ Cf. DER I, 12, p. 535.
²⁴ Cf. Semaḥoth IV, 16, above p. 342.
²⁵ He should have buried the corpse where he found it.
²⁶ He learned by associating with scholars.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:11)


הכניסן למרחץ בתחילה מעביר מסוהב ואח״כ מעביר את המנעלים ואח״כ מעביר את המכנסיים ואח״כ מפשיט את החלוק:


He who enters a bath-house should first remove his cloak, then the shoes, then the trousers and then the shirt.²⁷

footnotes:
²⁷ This rendering is in accordance with GRA and H. V reads: ‘If [the pupil] brought [the Sages] into a bath-house, he should first remove the cloak’, etc., referring to the duty to minister to the learned.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 8:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/8:12)


הנכנס למרחץ נותן כבוד ליוצא. והיוצא מן בית הכסא נותן כבוד לנכנס: 
 עד כאן מן המחזור וויטרי


He who is about to enter a bath-house should respect²⁸ the one who is about to leave,²⁹ and the one who is about to leave a privy must respect the one who is about to enter.³⁰

footnotes:
²⁸ By giving way.
²⁹ By not hurrying him unduly
³⁰ He must hurry so as not to keep the other waiting; cf. DER X, 2, p. 561.



## Chapter 9

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:1)


רבי אליעזר הקפר אומר התרחק מן התרעומת. שאם תתרעם על אחרים תוסיף לחטוא.


R. Eliezer Ha-Ḳappar said: Keep aloof from making complaints, because if you complain against others you will be led to further sin.²

footnotes:
² To hatred, quarrel and slander; cf. above I, 15, p. 569.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:2)


הוי אוהב את המוכיחך [כדי שתוסף חכמה על חכמתך] ושנא את המכבדך כדי שלא תתמעט מחכמתך:


Love him who reproves you so that you may increase knowledge; and hate him who flatters³ you so that your knowledge may not decrease.

footnotes:
³ lit. ‘honours, praises’. Praise may discourage one from further study.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:3)


הוי אוהב את בית הכנסת כדי שתטול שכרך בכל יום.


Love the Synagogue that you may receive your reward daily.⁴

footnotes:
⁴ Cf. Ber. 8a (Sonc. ed., p. 39).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:4)


הוי אוהב את בית המדרש כדי שיבואו בניך לת״ת.


Love the House of Study that your children may come to study the Torah.⁵

footnotes:
⁵ Copying the example of their parents.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:5)


הוי אוהב את העניים כדי שלא יבואו בניך לידי אותה מדה:


Love the poor that your children may not come to that condition.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:6)


הוי אוהב את הענוה כדי שתמלא את ידיך:


Love meekness that you may complete [the number of] your years.⁶ for *yadeka*.

footnotes:
⁶ So GRA. V reads ‘fill your hands’; H ‘your days’, reading yameka


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:7)


הוי אוהב את החסידים כדי שתנצל ממלאך התשחורת.


Love the pious⁷ that you may be saved from the Angel of Darkness.⁸

footnotes:
⁷ By emulating them.
⁸ According to NY he is so called because the Angel of Death makes the face of man black. H reads ‘Angel of Death’.

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:17

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:24)


ואם יכבדוך אחרים בין בישיבה בין במסבה עשה עמהם שלום [כדי שיבוא וינוח] על משכבך. וכן היה ר״א הקפר אומר [אהוב את] השלום ושנוא המחלוקת. גדול השלום שאפי׳ עובדין ע״א ויש שלום ביניהן כביכול אין שכינה יכולה לנגוע בהן שנאמר (הושע ד) חבור עצבים אפרים הנח לו: אם יש ביניהן מחלוקת מה נאמר בהן (שם י) חלק לבם עתה יאשמו. (הא כיצד) בית שיש בו מחלוקת סופו ליחרב וחכ״א מחלוקת בבית הכנסת סופה להתגזר: ב׳ ת״ח הדרים בעיר אחת והם בתי דינין וביניהן מחלוקת סופן למות:


Should people strive²⁷ with you, whether it be in the House of Study or at a social gathering,²⁸ make peace with them, so that when you leave them²⁹ they may speak well of you, as was spoken of Phinehas the son of Eleazar.³⁰ And so used R. Eleazar Ha-Ḳappar to say: Love peace and hate dissension. Great is peace, for even if [Israel] were to practise idolatry but maintained peace among themselves, the Divine Presence, as it were, would be unable to do them harm, as it is stated, *Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone*.³¹ But if there is dissension between them, what is stated of them? *Their heart is divided; now shall they bear their guilt*.³²
A house in which is dissension will ultimately be destroyed. A Synagogue [in which is dissension] will ultimately be turned into a place of idolatry.³³ If two scholars reside in the same city who have set up separate Courts of Law and dissension occurs between them, they will ultimately die [prematurely].³⁴ Abba Saul said: Dissension between separate Courts of Law is the ruination of the world.

²⁸ lit. ‘in a sitting [for study] or in a reclining [at a meal]’.
²⁹ lit. ‘on your return [home]’.
³⁰ Cf. Num. 25, 10-13. The translation follows GRA instead of V’s senseless ‘so that he may come and rest upon your bed’.
³¹ Hos. 4, 17. Cf. Midrash Rabbah, Num., XI, 7 (Sonc. ed., p. 441) where the reading is: ‘The Holy One, blessed be He, as it were, says: Satan shall not touch them’. In Midrash Rabbah, Gen., XXXVIII, 6 (Sonc. ed., p. 306) the version is: ‘The Holy One, blessed be He, says: I have no dominion over them’.
³² Hos. 10, 2.

³⁴ Cf. Soṭah 49a (Sonc. ed., p. 263).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 9:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/9:25)


אבא שאול אומר מחלוקת בתי דינין חורבן העולם: אבא איסי בן יוחנן משום שמואל הקטן אומר העוה״ז דומה לגלגל עינו של אדם. לבן שבו זה אוקיינוס שמקיף את כל העולם. שחור שבו זה העולם. קומט שבשחור זה ירושלים. פרצוף שבקומט זה בית המקדש שיבנה במהרה בימינו ובימי כל ישראל אמן:


Abba Isi b. Joḥanan said in the name of Samuel the Small: This world is likened to a person’s eyeball: the white of the eye [corresponds to] the ocean which surrounds the whole world; the iris to the [inhabited] world; the pupil of the eye to Jerusalem; the face in the pupil to the Temple. May it be rebuilt speedily in our days and in the days of all Israel, Amen.



## Chapter 10

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:1)


רבי שמעון בן יוחי אומר שבוע שבן דוד בא שנה ראשונה מתקיימת והמטרתי על עיר אחת וגו׳ (עמוס ד׳:ז׳). שניה חצי רעב משתלחין. שלישית רעב גדול ומתים בו אנשים ונשים וטף וחסידים ואנשי מעשה מתמעטים ותורה משתכחת מלומדיה. רביעית שובע ואינו שובע. חמישית שובע גדול אוכלים ושותים ושמחים . בששית קולות. בשביעית מלחמות. במוצאי שביעית בן דוד בא: רבן גמליאל אומר דור שבן דוד בא בית הועד יהיה לזנות. הגליל יחרב. ואנשי הגליל יסובבו מעיר לעיר ולא יחוננו. וחכמת סופרים תסרח. ויראי חטא ימאסו פני הדור כפני הכלב והאמת נעדרת וסר מרע משתולל: רבי נהוראי אומר דור שבן דוד בא. נערים ילבינו זקנים זקנים יעמדו לפני נערים. בת קמה באמה. כלה בחמותה. ואין הבן מתבייש מאמו: ר׳ נחמיה אומר דור שבן דוד בא עזות תרבה והיוקר יעוות. והגפן (לא) תתן פריה. והיין יהיה ביוקר. והמלכות תהפך למינות. ואין תוכחת


R. Simeon b. Joḥai said: As for the seven-year cycle in which the son of David will come, in the first year will be fulfilled *And I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city;*¹ in the second, the arrows of hunger will be sent forth;² in the third there will be a severe famine in the course of which men, women and children will die, pious men and miracle workers become scarce, and the Torah will be forgotten by its students;³ in the fourth, there will be partial plenty;⁴ in the fifth, great plenty when men will eat, drink and rejoice and the Torah will be restored to its disciples;⁵ in the sixth [there will be heard heavenly] sounds;⁶ cf. Isa. 27, 13. in the seventh, wars [will be waged]; and at the expiration of the septennate the son of David will come.⁷
Rabban Gamaliel said: In the generation when the son of David comes, the house of assembly⁸ will be a brothel, Galilee will be in ruins, and the inhabitants of Gablan⁹, ‘Galilee’, as in Sanh., *loc. cit.* (Sonc. ed., p. 655, n. 4). will wander about [begging] from city to city without experiencing pity; the wisdom of scribes will be in disfavour and God-fearing men despised, the leaders of the people¹⁰ will be dog-faced;¹¹ truth will be lacking, and he that departs from evil will be regarded as demented.
R. Nehorai said: In the generation when the son of David comes, young men will insult the old, the aged will stand up before youth,¹² a daughter will rise up against her mother and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,¹³ and a son will not be abashed in his father’s¹⁴ presence.
R. Nehemiah said: In the generation when the son of David comes, impudence will increase, esteem will be perverted,¹⁵ the vine will yield its fruit yet wine will be dear,¹⁶ and the government will be converted to heresy¹⁷ By ‘the kingdom’ the Roman Empire is meant, and the statement is a remarkable forecast by R. Nehemiah (100 C.E.) of the conversion of Rome to Christianity under Constantine the Great in 313 C.E. Cf. however, Herford, *Christianity in Talmud and Midrash*, pp. 207ff., Sanh., *loc. cit.* (Sonc. ed., p. 656, n. 4). with none to reprove.

footnotes:
¹ Amos 4, 7. There will be famine in one place and plenty in another.
² i.e. not actual famine, but the first signs of it, nobody being completely satisfied.
³ Through lack of food.
⁴ lit. ‘plenty and no plenty’.
⁵ ‘And the Torah’, etc., is added by GRA.
⁶ Either heavenly voices announcing the advent of the Messiah or the blasts of the great shofar;
⁷ Cf. Sanh. 97a (Sonc. ed., pp. 654f.) for this and the following passages; also Midrash to Song of Songs 2, 13 (Sonc. ed., p. 126).
⁸ Where scholars gather.
⁹ The Jews living along the borders of the Land of Israel. Gablan is to be read for Galil
¹⁰ lit. ‘the face of the generation’.
¹¹ Shameless.
¹² To do them honour.
¹³ Cf. Micah 7, 6.
¹⁴ So GRA and H. V has ‘mother’s’.
¹⁵ No one will esteem another. Or, even the nobility and most honoured will degenerate.
¹⁶ Drunkenness will increase so that in spite of the abundant yield there will be a scarcity.
¹⁷ Heb. minuth.

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:4
