###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:5)


ארבע פרוטות אין בהם סימן ברכה . ואלו הם שכר כותבין. שכר מתורגמינן. ושכר הבא ממדינת הים. והנושא אשה לשום כתובה שאין מורישין לבניהם ולבני בניהם.


Four *peruṭoth*²⁶ are without a sign of blessing.²⁷ They are: the wages of scribes,²⁸ and *mezuzoth;* if they become wealthy they would no longer write them. the wages of interpreters,²⁹ money that came from overseas,³⁰. and he who marries for the sake of a dowry.³¹ These will not be able to bequeath anything to their children or grandchildren.

footnotes:
²⁶ i.e. the monies earned from the four occupations enumerated.
²⁷ It is therefore not advisable to engage in them.
²⁸ Cf. Pes. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 246) where the reference is to writers of Torah-scrolls, tefillin
²⁹ Officials who delivered the Sabbath lectures of the Rabbi to the congregation. The Rabbi whispered his statement to the interpreter, who elaborated it to the people. It includes the translators of the weekly lections of the Torah on the Sabbath in the Synagogue. The reason given in Pes. is that it appears like wages for Sabbath work.
³⁰ Danger attended the transport of freights by sea and one might suffer loss
³¹ Pes. has instead ‘the profit of orphans’, i.e. derived by trading with trust money.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:6)


יש נושא אשה לשום זנות. ויש נושא אשה לשום ממון ויש נושא אשה לשום גדולה. יש נושא אשה לשם שמים: הנושא אשה לשום זנות עליו הכתוב אומר (הושע ה׳:ז׳) בה׳ בגדו בי בנים זרים ילדו עתה יאכלם חדש את חלקיהם. חדש נכנס וחדש יוצא וממונן כלה. והנושא אשה לשום גדולה. לסוף שמורידין אותו מגדולתו. והנושא אשה לשם שמים סוף שיוצאין ממנו בנים שמושיעין את ישראל.


There are some who marry for sexual indulgence, and there are some who marry for money. There are some who marry for social advancement³² and there are some who marry with sincere intention.³³ Of him who marries for sexual indulgence Scripture declares, *They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, for they have begotten strange children*.³⁴ meaning ‘strange from the ways of decency’. Of him who marries for money Scripture declares, *Now shall the new moon devour them with their portions*,³⁵ [implying] a month comes and a month goes and their money is gone. He who marries for social advancement will ultimately be deposed from his high position; but he who marries with sincere intention will ultimately have children who will be saviours of Israel.

footnotes:
³² lit. ‘greatness’.
³³ lit. ‘for the sake of heaven’, to fulfil the command to procreate.
³⁴ Hos. 5, 7. In Ḳid. 70a (Sonc.ed., p.354) the verse is applied to one who marries for money and it states that ‘he will have unworthy children’, the word strange
³⁵ ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:7)


הדר אלהים בני אדם. הדר בני אדם כסותן. הדר תורה (הדר) חכמה. הדר זקנה שיבה. הדר בחורים יראת חטא. הדר עם הארץ מארה.


The adornment of God is mankind; the adornment of mankind is the Torah;³⁶ the adornment of the Torah is wisdom; the adornment of old age is grey hair; the adornment of youth is the fear of sin; the adornment of an *‘am ha-’areẓ* is a curse.³⁷

footnotes:
³⁶ So GRA. V has ‘their garments’; cf. Shab. 113b (Sonc. ed., p. 556).
³⁷ The opposite of ‘blessing’ which he deserves for the neglect of the Torah. The meaning is obscure. Two possibilities suggest themselves. 1) That he deserves nothing more than a curse (and this reflects the reciprocal hostility we find elsewhere between the ע״ה and the scholar. 2) That a curse comes most readily to the lips of an ע״ה.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:8)


קרא ולא שנה הרי [זה] בור. שנה ולא קרא עם הארץ. קרא ושנה ולא פירש חכם. קרא ושנה ופירש נבון. לא קרא ולא שנה נוח לו שלא נברא.


He who learnt Scripture but not Mishnah is a boor; he who learnt Mishnah and not Scripture is an *‘am ha-’areẓ;*³⁸. he who learnt Scripture and Mishnah but has not expounded them is a scholar; he who learnt Scripture and Mishnah and expounded them is an intelligent man; and as for him who learnt neither Scripture nor Mishnah, better for him if he had not been born.

footnotes:
³⁸ The reading in Ber. 47b (Sonc. ed., p. 287) and Soṭah 22a (Sonc. ed., p. 110) is: ‘Even if he learnt Scripture and Mishnah but did not attend upon Rabbinical scholars, he is an ‘am ha-’areẓ’


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 10:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/r/10:9)


חכמה ואין יראה בזויה. אין חכמה ואין יראה רשע גמור. חכמה ויראה צדיק גמור:


One who has wisdom but no fear [of God] is contemptible;³⁹ [one who has] fear [of God] but no wisdom is poor;⁴⁰ [one who has] neither wisdom nor fear [of God] is thoroughly wicked; [one who has] wisdom and fear [of God] is thoroughly righteous.

footnotes:
³⁹ Or his knowledge is contemptible, because he does not use it for a good purpose.
⁴⁰ The clause is added by GRA. He lacks what is essential; or, his fear of God is of poor quality.



## Section on Peace

###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/1)


אמר ריב״ל גדול הוא השלום שהשלום לארץ כשאור לעיסה אלמלא שנתן הקב״ה שלום בארץ היתה החרב והחיה משכלת את האדם. מה טעם דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ו:ו׳) ונתתי שלום בארץ. ואין ארץ אלא ישראל שנאמר (מלאכי ג׳:י״ב) ואשרו אתכם כל הגוים כי תהיו אתם ארץ חפץ ואומר (זכריה א) (והנה כל הארץ יושבת ושוקטת). דור הולך ודור בא והארץ לעולם עומדת (קהלת א׳:ד׳) . מלכות באה ומלכות הולכת וישראל לעולם קיימים. אבל שלמה אע״פ שדור הולך ודור בא מלכות הולכת ומלכות באה. גזירה הולכת גזירה באה ומתחדשת על שונאי ישראל. הארץ לעולם עומדת. ישראל לעולם עומדין לא עזבן ולא מיעזבן לא כלין ולא מיכלין שנאמר (מלאכי ג׳:ו׳) כי אני ה׳ לא שניתי ואתם בני יעקב לא כליתם. כשם שאני לא שניתי ולא אני עתיד להשנות כך אתם בית יעקב לא כליתם ולא עתידין אתם ליכלות אלא (דברים ד׳:ד׳) ואתם הדבקים בה׳ אלהיכם חיים כולכם היום:


R. Joshua b. Levi said: Great is peace, for peace is to the world as leaven is to dough. Had not the Holy One, blessed be He, given peace to the earth, the sword and the beast would have robbed the world¹ of its children. Whence² [do we know this]? From what is written, *And I will give peace in the land … and I will cause evil beasts to cease out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land;*³ and *land* is the same. and *land* means nothing else than Israel, as it is stated, *And all nations shall call you happy; for ye shall be a delightsome land*.⁴ with Israel is here evident. V and H add: ‘And it states, *And, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest*’. [And so Solomon declared,] *One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh; and the earth abideth for ever*:⁵ Solomon said:⁶ Although a generation passes away and another generation comes, one kingdom goes and another kingdom comes, one decree passes away and a new decree is imposed upon Israel,⁷ *the earth abideth for ever*, i.e. Israel will abide for ever,⁸ refers to Israel. [Cf. Midrash *ad loc.*, Sonc. ed., p. 15.] they are not forsaken nor will they be forsaken, they are not destroyed nor will they be destroyed, as it is stated, *For I the Lord change not; and ye, O sons of Jacob are not consumed*⁹—as I have not changed nor will I change, so you, the House of Jacob, are not destroyed and will not be destroyed, but [as it is stated], *But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day*.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹ So H; V reads ‘man’.
² So GRA; V reads ‘why is it written?’
³ Lev. 26, 6. The Heb. for earth
⁴ Mal. 3, 12. The identification of land
⁵ Eccl. 1, 4.
⁶ So GRA. V reads: ‘A kingdom comes and a kingdom goes, but Israel endures for ever. But Solomon, although’.
⁷ lit. ‘upon the enemies of Israel’, a euphemism.
⁸ Earth
⁹ Mal. 3, 6.
¹⁰ Deut. 4, 4.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/2)


תמן תנינן רשב״ג אומר על ג׳ דברים העולם קיים על הדין ועל האמת ועל השלום. א״ר מונא ושלשתן דבר אחד הן נעשה הדין נעשה אמת נעשה שלום. ושלשתן בפסוק אחד נאמרו שנאמר (זכריה ח׳:ט״ז) אמת ומשפט שלום שפטו בשעריכם. כל מקום שיש משפט יש שלום (וכל מקום שיש שלום יש משפט):


There¹¹ they taught: Rabban Simeon b. Gamaliel used to say: By three things does the world endure: justice, truth and peace.¹² R. Muna said: The three are one, because if justice is done, truth has been effected and peace brought about; and all three are mentioned in one verse, as it is stated, *Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates*,¹³ [indicating that] wherever justice is done peace is to be found.

footnotes:
¹¹ In Babylon.
¹² Cf. Aboth I, 18 (Sonc. ed., p. 10).
¹³ Zech. 8, 16.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/3)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום שבשעה שעמדו ישראל ואמרו כל אשר דבר ה׳ נעשה ונשמע (שמות כ״ד:ז׳) שמח בהן הקב״ה ונתן להם תורתו וברכם בשלום שנאמר (תהילים כ״ט:י״א) ה׳ עוז לעמו יתן ה' יברך את עמו בשלום: (חזקיה אמר תורת ה׳ תמימה משיבת נפש) (שם יט):


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, for when Israel stood [at Sinai] and declared, *All that the Lord hath spoken we will do, and obey*,¹⁴ [59*b*] the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoiced in them and gave them His Torah and blessed them with peace, as it is stated, *The Lord will give strength*¹⁵ *unto His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace*.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁴ Ex. 24, 7.
¹⁵ Here taken as a synonym of Torah.
¹⁶ Ps. 29, 11.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/4)


אמר חזקיה גדול הוא השלום. שכל מצוה שבתורה כתוב בהן (שמות כג) כי תראה (שם) כי תפגע (דברים כב) כי יקרא (שם) כי תבנה כשבאה המצוה לידך אתה זקוק לעשות אבל השלום מה כתיב בו (תהילים ל״ד:ט״ו) בקש שלום ורדפהו. בקשהו ממקומך ורדפהו במקום אחר.


Hezekiah said: Great is peace, for in connection with all other precepts in the Torah it is written, *If thou see*,¹⁷ etc., *If thou meet*,¹⁸ 4. *If there chance*,¹⁹ *If thou buildest*,²⁰ 8, E.V. *when thou buildest*. [implying,] if a precept comes to your hand, you are bound to perform it;²¹ but what is written in connection with peace? *Seek peace, and pursue it*,²² [meaning,] seek it in your place and follow it to another place.²³

footnotes:
¹⁷ Ex. 23, 5.
¹⁸ ibid.
¹⁹ Deut. 22, 6.
²⁰ ibid.
²¹ But if not, you are not bound to perform it.
²² Ps. 34, 15.
²³ If your presence can help to bring about peace there.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/5)


(חזקיה אמר) גדול הוא השלום. שבכל המסעות כתיב ויסעו ויחנו. נוסעין במחלוקת וחונין במחלוקת. בזמן שבאו לסיני חנו חנייה אחת. ויחן שם ישראל (שמות י״ט:ב׳). אמר הקב״ה הואיל ושנאו ישראל את המחלוקת ואהבו את השלום ונעשו חנייה אחת הרי השעה שאתן להם את תורתי: אדניה לא נהרג אלא בשביל שהיה בעל מחלוקת ומותר לומר לשון הרע על בעל מחלוקת שכן נתן הנביא אמר לבת שבע (מלכים א א׳:י״ד) ואני אבוא אחריך ומלאתי את דבריך. וא״ר כל השקרים אסורים ומותר לשקר בשביל להטיל שלום בין אדם לחבירו:


Hezekiah said: Great is peace, for with regard to all the journeyings [of Israel] it is written, *And they journeyed … and they pitched*,²⁴ [the plural number implying that] they journeyed in dissension and encamped in dissension. When, however, they came to Mount Sinai, they all became one encampment, [as it is stated,] *And there Israel encamped*²⁵ *before the mount*.²⁶ The Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘Since Israel hate dissension and love peace and became one encampment, this is the time when I will give them My Torah’.
Adonijah was slain only because he was a quarrelsome person,²⁷ and it is permissible to slander a quarrelsome person; for thus did Nathan the prophet say to Bathsheba, *I also will come in after thee, and confirm thy words*.²⁸ And Rabbi [Judah the Prince] said: All falsehoods are prohibited, but it is permissible to utter a falsehood for the purpose of making peace between a man and his fellow.¹

footnotes:
²⁴ Num. 33, 5 ff.
²⁵ The verb is singular in the Heb.
²⁶ Ex. 19, 2.
²⁷ Although the kingdom was promised by David to Solomon, Adonijah tried to usurp it, knowing that it would cause strife and bloodshed.
²⁸ 1 Kings 1, 14.
¹ (28a) [Cf. the procedure adopted by Aaron, below §18, ARN XII, p. 71ff.]


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/6)


אמר בר קפרא גדול השלום שכן מצינו שדברה תורה לשון בדאי כדי להטיל שלום בין אברהם לשרה. שנאמר (בראשית י״ח:י״ב) ותצחק שרה בקרבה לאמר וגו' ואדני זקן ולבסוף כתיב ואני זקנתי.


Bar Ḳappara said: Great is peace, for we find that the Torah modified a statement in order to maintain peace between Abraham and Sarah. It is stated, *And Sarah laughed within herself, saying … my lord being old*;²⁹ but in the sequel³⁰ it is written, *I who am old*.³¹ 13. God concealed from Abraham that Sarah called him ‘an old man’.

footnotes:
²⁹ Gen. 18, 12.
³⁰ When God repeated this to Abraham.
³¹ ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/7)


אמר בר קפרא גדול השלום שכן מצינו שדברו הנביאים לשון בדאי כדי להטיל שלום בין מנוח לאשתו. דמעיקרא כתיב (שופטים י״ג:ג׳) הנה נא את עקרה ולבסוף כתיב ( הנך הרה) ולא אידכר שום עקרה.


Bar Ḳappara said: Great is peace, for we find that in the prophets, too, Scripture modified a statement for the purpose of maintaining peace between Manoaḥ and his wife. At first³² it is written, *Behold, now, thou art barren … but thou shalt conceive and bear a son;*³³ but in the sequel³⁴ it is written, *Behold thou shalt conceive and bear a son*,³⁵ 7. and there is no mention of the words *behold thou art barren*.

footnotes:
³² When the angel spoke to Manoaḥ’s wife.
³³ Judg. 13, 3.
³⁴ When she reported her encounter with the angel to her husband.
³⁵ ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/8)


אמר בר קפרא גדול הוא השלום שהמלאכים אין ביניהם לא איבה ולא קנאה ולא שנאה ולא מינות ולא תגרות ולא מחלוקת שהקב״ה עושה עמהן שלום. מה טעם המשל ופחד עמו עושה שלום במרומיו (איוב כ״ה:ב׳) המשל זה מיכאל. ופחד זה גבריאל. לא זה מחזיק את זה. ומהן מן אש ומהן מן מים. בני אדם שיש ביניהן כל המדות האלו על אחת כמה וכמה:


Bar Ḳappara said: Great is peace, for even the angels among whom there is no enmity, jealousy, hatred, strife, rivalry or dissension [have need for] the Holy One, blessed be He, to make peace among them; as it is stated,³⁶ *Dominion and fear are with Him; He maketh peace in His high places*³⁷—*dominion* alludes to Michael and *fear* to Gabriel, one being of fire and the other of water³⁸ and yet they do not injure one another;³⁹ how much more so then do mortal beings, among whom all these dispositions exist, [have need of peace] !

footnotes:
³⁶ The emended text of GRA is followed.
³⁷ Job 25, 2.
³⁸ Cf. Midrash Rabbah, Numbers, XII, 8 (Sonc. ed., p. 472), where Gabriel is said to be made of fire and Michael of snow.
³⁹ Because God makes peace between them.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/9)


א״ר ישמעאל גדול הוא השלום שמצינו שויתר הקב״ה על שמו שנכתב בקדושה שימחה על המים כדי להטיל שלום בין איש לאשתו.


R. Ishmael said: Great is peace, for we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, permitted His Name, though written in holiness, to be blotted out in water,⁴⁰ for the purpose of restoring peace between husband and wife.

footnotes:
⁴⁰ Cf. Num. 5, 6ff., especially verse 23.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/10)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום שברית כהנים כרותה בשלום. שנא׳ (במדבר כ״ה:י״ב) הנני נותן [לו] את בריתי שלום:


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, for the covenant with the priests was made with [the word] ‘peace’, as it is stated, *Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace*.⁴¹ XXV, 12.

footnotes:
⁴¹ ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/11)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום ששמו של הקב״ה נקרא שלום. שנאמר (שופטים ו׳:כ״ד) ויקרא לו ה׳ שלום: (א״ר חייא בר אבא מכאן שאסור לשאול בשלום חבירו במקום מטונף מה טעם (שם) ויבן שם גדעון מזבח ויקרא לו ה׳ שלום) מה מזבח שאינו אוכל ולא שותה ולא מריח ולא נבנה אלא לכפרתן של ישראל נקרא שלום. מי שהוא אוהב שלום ורודף שלום ומקדים שלום ומשיב שלום ומטיל שלום בין ישראל לאביהם שבשמים על אחת כמה וכמה. רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר אף שמו של משיח נקרא שלום: שנאמר (ישעיהו ט׳:ה׳) אבי עד שר שלום.


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, for the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is called ‘peace’, as it is stated, *And he called it*⁴² *‘Adonai-shalom’*.⁴³ ⁴⁴R. Ḥiyya b. Abba said: Hence it can be deduced that a person may not extend a greeting of peace to his fellow in a place of filth, because it is stated, *And Gideon built an altar there unto the Lord and called it ‘Adonai-shalom’*. Now if an altar which does not eat, drink or smell and was erected only to make an atonement for [the sins of] Israel is called ‘peace’, he who loves peace and pursues peace, who welcomes people with the greeting of peace⁴⁵ and responds with peace, and who maintains peace between Israel and their Father in heaven, how much more so! R. Jose the Galilean said: Even the name of the Messiah is called ‘peace’, [as it is stated,] *And his name is called … Abi-ad-sar-shalom*.⁴⁶

footnotes:
⁴² The altar erected by Gideon.
⁴³ Judg. 6, 24, i.e. ‘the Lord is peace’; cf. Shab. 10b (Sonc. ed., p. 37) and Midrash Rabbah, Leviticus, IX, 9 (Sonc. ed., p. 117) where the rendering is ‘And he called Him Lord, Peace’, which is described in n. 1 as ‘a very bold Midrashic rendering’.
⁴⁴ This sentence is omitted by GRA.
⁴⁵ lit. ‘who is first with [the greeting of] ‘Peace [upon you]’; cf. Ber. 17a (Sonc. ed., p. 102) where it is reported by Rabban Joḥanan b. Zakkai that never did anyone anticipate him with the salutation of peace, not even a heathen in the market-place.
⁴⁶ Isa. 9, 5, i.e. ‘the Everlasting Father, the Ruler of peace’.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/12)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום שישראל נקראין שלום: שנאמר (זכריה ח׳:י״ב) כי זרע השלום . למי השלום לזרע השלום.


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, for [the children of] Israel are called ‘peace’, as it is stated, *For as the seed of peace, the vine shall give her fruit*.⁴⁷ To whom will peace [be given]? To *the seed of peace*.

footnotes:
⁴⁷ Zech. 8, 12.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/13)


רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר גדול הוא השלום שבשעה שמלך המשיח נגלה לישראל אין פותח אלא בשלום. שנאמר (ישעיהו נ״ב:ז׳) מה נאוו על ההרים רגלי מבשר משמיע שלום.


R. Jose the Galilean said: Great is peace, seeing that when king Messiah will reveal himself to Israel, his first message will be peace, as it is stated, *How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger of good tidings, that announceth peace*.⁴⁸

footnotes:
⁴⁸ Isa. 52, 7.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/14)


רבי יוסי הגללי אומר גדול הוא השלום שבשעת מלחמה אין פותח אלא בשלום. שנאמר (דברים כ׳:י׳) כי תקרב אל עיר להלחם עליה וקראת אליה לשלום:


R. Jose the Galilean said: Great is peace, since even in a time of war one should begin [by attempting to arrange] peace, as it is stated, *When thou drawest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it*.⁴⁹

footnotes:
⁴⁹ Deut. 20, 10.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/15)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום שעתיד הקב״ה לסמוך צדיקים בשלום שנאמר (ישעיהו כ״ו:ג׳) יצר סמוך תצר שלום:


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, since the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the hereafter support the righteous with peace, as it is stated, *The mind stayed on Thee Thou keepest in perfect peace*.⁵⁰.

footnotes:
⁵⁰ Isa. 26, 3. The preceding verse speaks of the righteous nation


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/16)


א״ר יהושע גדול הוא השלום שהיא תלויה לחיים ותלויה למתים. לחיים מנין ויאמר יתרו למשה לך לשלום (שמות ד׳:י״ח). למתים מנין ואתה תבוא אל אבותיך בשלום (בראשית ט״ו:ט״ו)


R. Joshua said: Great is peace, for it is given [as a blessing] to the living and the dead. Whence to the living? [As it is stated,] *And Jethro said to Moses: ‘Go in peace’*.⁵¹ And whence to the dead? [As it is stated,] *But thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace*.⁵²

footnotes:
⁵¹ Ex. 4, 18.
⁵² Gen. 15, 15.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/17)


רשב״ג אומר גדול הוא השלום שמצינו שדברו השבטים דברי בדאות כדי להטיל שלום בין יוסף לאחיו. שנאמר (בראשית נ׳:ט״ז) ויצוו אל יוסף לאמר אביך צוה וגו׳. אין אנו מוצאין שצוה להם כלום.


Rabban Simeon b. Gamaliel said: Great is peace, for we find that the tribes⁵³ reported an untrue statement in order to maintain peace between Joseph and his brethren; as it is stated, *And they sent a message unto Joseph, saying: Thy father did command before he died, saying: So shall ye say unto Joseph: Forgive, I pray thee now, the transgression of thy brethren and their sin*,⁵⁴ L, 16. but we do not find that [Jacob] had given them any such command.⁵⁵

footnotes:
⁵³ i.e. the sons of Jacob.
⁵⁴ ibid.
⁵⁵ Cf. Yeb. 65b (Sonc. ed., p. 437).


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/18)


רשב״ג אומר גדול הוא השלום שהרי אהרן הכהן לא נשתבח אלא בשביל השלום שהיה אוהב שלום ורודף שלום ומקדים שלום ומשיב שלום שנאמר (מלאכי ב׳:ו׳) בשלום ובמישור הלך אתי (מה כתיב בתריה ורבים השיב מעון.אלא) מלמד כשהיה רואה שני בני אדם שונאין זה את זה הולך אצל אחד מהן ואמר לו למה שונא אתה את פלוני כבר בא אלי לביתי ונשתטח לפני ואמר לי חטאתי לפלוני לך ופייס עליו ומניח לזה והולך אצל השני ואומר לו כראשון והיה משים שלום ואהבה וריעות בין אדם לחבירו ורבים השיב מעון: א״ר יהושע הנביא נקרא מלאך והחכם נקרא מלאך. הנביא נקרא מלאך שנאמר (חגי א׳:י״ג) ויאמר חגי מלאך יי׳. והחכם נקרא מלאך שנאמר (מלאכי ב׳:ז׳) מלאך יי׳ צבאות הוא: יכול יהא כהן עם הארץ ת״ל (שם) ותורה יבקשו מפיהו :


Rabban Simeon b. Gamaliel said: Great is peace, for Aaron the [High] Priest was praised only for peace; for he loved peace, pursued peace, greeted with the salutation of peace and responded with it, as it is stated, *He walked with Me in peace and uprightness*.⁵⁶ It teaches that when he noticed two persons at enmity one with the other, he used to go first to one of them and say to him, ‘Why do you hate So-and-so? He has already come to my house, prostrated himself before me and said to me, “I sinned against So-and-so”. Go and pacify him’. When he left this one, he went to the other and spoke to him similarly, and so made peace, love and friendship between a man and his fellow. What is written subsequently? *For he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts*.⁵⁷ 7. The text of GRA has been followed. [Cf. above, p. 599.]
R. Joshua said: The prophet is called ‘messenger [of the Lord]’ and the priest⁵⁸ is called ‘messenger [of the Lord]’. The prophet is called ‘messenger [of the Lord]’, as it is stated, *Then spoke Haggai the Lord’s messenger;*⁵⁹ and the priest is called ‘messenger [of the Lord]’, as it is stated, *For he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts*.⁶⁰ Lest you think that this applies even to a priest who is an *‘am ha-’areẓ*, the text declares, *And they should seek the law at his mouth*.⁶¹

footnotes:
⁵⁶ Mal. 2, 6.
⁵⁷ ibid.
⁵⁸ So GRA. V and H read ‘a Sage’.
⁵⁹ Hag. 1, 13.
⁶⁰ Mal. 2, 7.
⁶¹ ibid.


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/19)


ר׳ יהושע דסכנין בשם רבי לוי אמר גדול השלום שכל הברכות והתפלות חותמין בשלום. ק״ש חותמין בשלום ופרוס סכת שלומיך. ברכת כהנים חותמין בשלום וישם לך שלום (במדבר ו׳:כ״ו) (כל הברכות חותמים בשלום עושה השלום):


R. Joshua of Siknin said in the name of R. Levi: Great is peace, for all benedictions and prayers conclude with ‘peace’. In the case of the benedictions of the *Shema‘*⁶² and one benediction follows it; in the evening service two precede and two follow it (P.B., pp. 37ff., 96). one concludes with ‘peace’: ‘[Blessed art Thou, O Lord,] Who spreadest the tabernacle of peace’;⁶³ in the evening services on Sabbaths and Festivals (P.B., p. 114). in the case of prayers⁶⁴ (P.B., pp. 44-54). one concludes with ‘peace’: ‘[Blessed art Thou, O Lord,] Who makest peace’.⁶⁵ concludes with “peace” in *and give them peace* (Num. 6, 26)’.

footnotes:
⁶² In the morning service two benedictions precede the Shema‘
⁶³ The conclusion of the second benediction after the Shema‘
⁶⁴ i.e. the ‘Amidah
⁶⁵ P.B., p. 54, where this formula is now used only during the penitential season, though originally said on all occasions. V and H include, but GRA deletes, ‘The benediction of the kohanim


###### Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta, Section on Peace 20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Derekh%20Eretz%20Zuta/s/Section%20on%20Peace/r/20)


אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי אמר להם הקב״ה לישראל אתם גרמתם להחריב את ביתי ולהגלות את בניי. היו שואלים בשלומה ואני מוחל לכם מה טעם שאלו שלום ירושלים (תהילים קכ״ב:ו׳) (ואומר (ירמיהו כ״ט:ז׳) ודרשו את שלום העיר). ואומר (תהילים קכ״ב:ז׳) יהי שלום בחילך. (ואומר למען אחי ורעי וגו׳ ומי בחילך) ואומר (שם קכב) למען אחי ורעי וגו׳ ומי שהוא אוהב שלום ורודף שלום ומקדים שלום ומשיב שלום הקב״ה מורישו לחיי העולם הזה והעולם הבא (שם לז) וענוים יירשו ארץ והתענגו על רוב שלום:


R. Joshua b. Levi said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, ‘You have brought about the destruction of My Temple and the dispersion of My children; pray, therefore, for the peace [of Zion] and I will give you peace’;⁶⁶ as it is stated, *Pray for the peace of Jerusalem*,⁶⁷ and it also declares, *Peace be within thy walls*,⁶⁸ 7. and it is also stated, *For my brethren and companions’ sakes, I will now say: Peace be within thee*.⁶⁹ 8.
As for him who loves peace, pursues peace, and gives the greeting of peace and responds with peace, the Holy One, blessed be He, will cause him to inherit life in this world and life in the World to Come, as it is stated, *But the humble shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in the abundance of peace*.⁷⁰ XXXVII, 11. [60*a*]

footnotes:
⁶⁶ So GRA. V and H read, ‘I will forgive you’.
⁶⁷ Ps. 122, 6.
⁶⁸ ibid.
⁶⁹ ibid.
⁷⁰ ibid.

# Tractate Gerim

מסכת גרים

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim)

תהליך הגיור, מעמד הגר ודיני גר תושב.

Converts to Judaism, the conversion process, and non-Jewish residents of Israel who observe the seven laws of Noah.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 34, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 34)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Gerim 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:1)


הרוצה להתגייר אין מקבלין אותו מיד אומרים לו מה לך להתגייר והלא אתה רואה את האומה הזאת נמוכה וכפופה ושפילה מכל האומות וחולאים ויסורים באים עליהן וקוברין בנים ובני בנים ונהרגין על המילה ועל הטבילה ועל שאר כל המצות ואינם נוהגים בפרהסיא כשאר כל האומות:


If a man wishes to become a proselyte he is not accepted at once but they¹ say to him, ‘Why do you want to become a proselyte? Do you not see that this people are debased, oppressed and degraded² more than all other peoples, that diseases and chastisements come upon them and they bury their children and children’s children, that they are slaughtered for [observing] circumcision, immersion³ and the other precepts [of the Torah] and cannot hold up their heads⁴ like other peoples?’

footnotes:
¹ The Rabbis who consider his application.
² ‘Debased’ in themselves, ‘oppressed’ by others, and ‘degraded’ in consequence. MS.K. and H read ‘lowly and persecuted’.
³ To purify themselves after ritual defilement.
⁴ lit. ‘behave in public’.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:2)


אם אמר איני כדאי פוטרין אותו והולך לו:


If he says, ‘I am not worthy’, they dismiss him and he goes his way.⁵

footnotes:
⁵ MS.K. and H read: ‘If he says, “I am not worthy to place my neck under the yoke of Him Who spoke and the world came into being, blessed be He”, they receive him forthwith, and if not he is dismissed and goes his way’. In Yeb. 47a. (Sonc. ed., p. 311), the reading is ‘I know and yet am unworthy’ of the privilege of membership of Israel.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:3)


קבל עליו הורידהו לבית הטבילה וכיסהו במים עד מקום הערוה. ואומרים לו מקצת דקדוקי מצות על מנת שהוא נותן בשכחה ובלקט ובפיאה ובמעשר:


If, however, he undertakes [to become a proselyte], they take him down to the place of immersion, cover him in water up to his middle,⁶ and tell him some of the details of the precepts. [He is informed that he is accepted only] on condition that he will give gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field and tithes.⁷

footnotes:
⁶ The place of nakedness.
⁷ Cf. Lev. 19, 9; Deut. 24, 19; Num. 18, 26ff.; Deut. 14, 22ff.; XXVI, 12ff.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:4)


כשם שאומרים לאיש כך אומרים לאשה ע"מ שתהא זהירה בנדה ובהדלקת הנר:


As they say this to a man, so they say to a woman that [she is accepted] on condition that she will be particular in regard to *niddah, ḥallah*⁸ and the kindling of the Sabbath lamp.

footnotes:
⁸ Added by MS.K. and H.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:5)


טבל ועלה אומרים לו דברים טובים ונכונים במי נדבקת אשריך במי שאמר והיה העולם שלא נברא העולם אלא בשביל ישראל ולא נקראו בנים למקום אלא ישראל ואין חביבין לפני המקום אלא ישראל כל אותם דברים שדברנו לך לא אמרנו לך אלא להרבות שכרך:


When he has bathed and come up [out of the water], they speak to him words of kindness and comfort⁹ [saying], ‘To Whom are you cleaving? Happy are you! [You are cleaving] to Him Who spoke and the world came into being, blessed be He; for the world was created only for the sake of Israel;¹⁰ only Israel are called “sons of God”,¹¹ and only Israel are [described as] “beloved of God”.¹² All the things we have said to you¹³ we have said only to increase your reward’.

footnotes:
⁹ So MS.K. and H, V ‘appropriate words’.
¹⁰ [Cf. Midrash Rabbah, Leviticus, XXXVI, 4 (Sonc. ed., p. 461): ‘The heaven and earth were only created for the sake of Israel’, because God foresaw that they alone would accept the Torah, without which the universe could not endure.]
¹¹ [Cf. Deut. 14, 1.]
¹² [To be understood in the light of the dictum, ‘Beloved are Israel, for unto them was given the desirable instrument’, i.e. the Torah (Aboth III, 18, Sonc. ed., III, 14, p. 37).] MS.K. omits the clause.
¹³ viz. at the beginning, ‘Why do you want to become a proselyte?’


###### Tractate Gerim 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:6)


גר שמל ולא טבל טבל ולא מל הכל הולך אחר המילה דברי ר"א רע"א אין טבילה מעכבת:


If a proselyte has been circumcised but has not yet bathed [he is a proselyte]; if he has bathed but not yet been circumcised [he is not yet a proselyte]; everything depends on the circumcision. This is the view of R. Eliezer, but R. ‘Aḳiba said: Also¹⁴ with MS.K. and H instead of *’en* (not) in V. [Cf. the discussion on the subject in Yeb. 46a, b (Sonc. ed., pp. 302ff.).] [the lack of] bathing is a bar.

footnotes:
¹⁴ Reading ’af


###### Tractate Gerim 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:7)


כל המתגייר משום אשה משום אהבה משום יראה אין זה גר וכן היו ר׳ יהודה ור׳ נחמיה אומרים כל אותם שנתגיירו בימי מרדכי ואסתר אינם גרים שנא׳ ורבים מעמי הארץ מתיהדים כי נפל פחד היהודים עליהם וכל שאינו מתגייר לשם שמים אינו גר:


Anyone who becomes a proselyte for the sake of [marrying a Jewish] woman, or out of fear, or love¹⁵ is not a proselyte. Similarly R. Judah and R. Nehemiah said: All [the Gentiles] who were converted in the days of Mordecai and Esther were not genuine proselytes, as it is stated, *And many from among the peoples of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews was fallen upon them*.¹⁶ Anyone who is not converted from purely religious motives¹⁷ is not a proselyte. [60*b*]

footnotes:
¹⁵ [Of the Jews, perhaps deriving material advantage from his conversion.]
¹⁶ Esth. 8, 17.
¹⁷ lit. ‘to the name of Heaven’.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:8)


האיש מטביל לאיש והאשה מטבלת לאשה אבל לא את האיש:


A man gives immersion to a man, and a woman to a woman but not to a man.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:9)


גר שנתגייר והיו לו יינות ואמר בריא לי שלא נתנסך מהם מותר לו ואסורים לאחרים רע"א מה אם לאחרים אסורים אוסר לעצמו אם אמר אף גבי כל חבר נעשו בטהרה הרי זה נאמן:


If a man became a proselyte who had vessels of wine¹⁸, ‘wine of libation’, and is forbidden to Jews on the suspicion that it may have been used in idolatrous rites.] in his possession and he says, ‘I am positive that none of it has been poured out as a libation’, the wine is permitted to him and forbidden to others. R. ‘Aḳiba said: ¹⁹If it is forbidden to others, surely it is forbidden to himself! If he says, ‘[The wine has been made] in a state of purity in the presence of So-and-so who is a *ḥaber*, he is believed’.
Similarly should an *‘am ha-’areẓ* take upon himself to become a *ḥaber*, and he had food which should be in a state of ritual purity and said, ‘I am positive that it has been prepared in ritual cleanliness’, it is permitted to him and forbidden to others. R. ‘Aḳiba said: If it is forbidden to others, all the more it is forbidden to himself! But if he said, ‘It was prepared in ritual cleanliness in the presence of So-and-so who is a *ḥaber’*, he is believed.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁸ [Wine in the possession of a Gentile is termed yayin nesek
¹⁹ A comparison with Tosiftha Ṭohoroth sec. 9 shows that there is a lacuna in the text and that R. ‘Aḳiba is speaking of the case where the wine had not been made by the proselyte himself but by another Gentile.
²⁰ This paragraph is omitted in V and inserted in MS.K. and H.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:10)


ישראל שהלוה לעובד כוכבים ועובד כוכבים שהלוה לישראל ואח"כ נתגייר גובה את הקרן ואינו גובה את הרבית ר' יהודה אומר אם מתחלה זקפן עליו במלוה גובה את הכל:


If an Israelite lends money to a Gentile or a Gentile lends money to an Israelite and he became a proselyte, he collects the principal but not the interest.²¹ R. Judah said: If before conversion he turned the whole into a loan,²² he collects the whole.

footnotes:
²¹ MS.K. reads: ‘One (i.e. the proselyte) takes the capital only (because being now a Jew he may not take interest from a Jew [cf. Lev. 25, 36f.], and the other (the Jew) takes the interest as well’. The reason is that if this were not done, it might be suspected that the Gentile became a convert to escape paying the interest.
²² i.e. added the interest to the principal and wrote a fresh contract for the whole sum as a loan.


###### Tractate Gerim 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/1:11)


הא כיצד נולד לבן אדם בן בכור עד שלא נתגייר פטור משנתגייר חייב ואם ספק פטור. היו לו עיסה לעשות ושדה לקצור עד שלא נתגייר פטור משנתגייר חייב ואם ספק פטור:


How [is the law]? If a first-born son was born to him before he was converted, he is exempt;²³ but if after he was converted he is liable; in case of doubt he is exempt. If he had dough ready for baking and a field ready for reaping, until he is converted he is exempt²⁴ and the tithe. but from the time he is converted he is liable. If there is doubt he is exempt.

footnotes:
²³ From his redemption (cf. Ex. 34, 20). MS.K. and H read: ‘If a son were born to him or his cow calved or his cow were slaughtered before he was converted, he is exempt’ from the priestly dues.
²⁴ From ḥallah



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Gerim 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:1)


גר נימול לעולם לח׳ הא כיצד עד שלא טבלה אמו נולד בן נימול בן יומו משטבלה אמו נולד נמול לח׳:


There is a proselyte who is circumcised at eight days old¹. How is this? If he was born before his mother [who became a convert] underwent immersion he is circumcised at a day old,² but if after his mother underwent immersion at eight days old.³

footnotes:
¹ So MS.K. and H. V wrongly, ‘a proselyte is always circumcised at eight days old’.
² i.e. he is made a proselyte at the earliest moment.
³ Like a child of a Jewish mother.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:2)


גר שנתגייר מהול או ספק שנולד מהול צריך להטיף ממנו דם ברית כדברי ב"ש ובה"א א"צ:


If a proselyte was already circumcised, or if a child was born circumcised, it is necessary to draw from him blood of the covenant,⁴ according to Beth Shammai; but Beth Hillel say that it is not necessary.

footnotes:
⁴ A slight incision is made to draw a drop of blood.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:3)


א"ר מתיא בן חרש משום ר"ש לא נחלקו ב"ש וב"ה על גר שנתגייר מהול ועל תינוק שנולד מהול על מה נחלקו על תינוק שנולד מהול ביום השבת שבש"א דוחין עליו את השבת להטיף ממנו דם ברית ובה"א א"צ:


R. Mathia b. Ḥeresh said in the name of R. Ishmael:⁵ Beth Shammai and Beth Hillel did not differ on the question of a proselyte who was already circumcised or a child who was born circumcised. On what did they differ? On a child who was born circumcised on the Sabbath. Beth Shammai said: We override the Sabbath on his account to draw from him blood of the covenant, and Beth Hillel said that this is not necessary.⁶

footnotes:
⁵ So MS.K. and H. V has ‘Samuel’.
⁶ To set the Sabbath aside, and the blood should be drawn on another day. Both Schools agreed that it was necessary to draw the blood of the covenant.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:4)


עבד שטבל לפני רבו הרי הוא בן חורין מעשה בברוריא המלכה שטבלו מקצת עבדיה לפניה ומקצת עבדיה לאחריה. ובא מעשה לפני חכמים ואמרו אלו שטבלו לפניה בני חורין ולאחריה משועבדין:


If a slave underwent immersion before his master⁷ he becomes free. It is related of Queen Valeria⁸ that some of her slaves underwent immersion before her and some after her, and when the case came before the Sages they said that they who underwent immersion before her were free, but they who underwent immersion after her were still enslaved.

footnotes:
⁷ A Gentile who was being made a convert.
⁸ [In Yeb. 46a (Sonc. ed., p. 299) ‘Queen’ is omitted. R.H. 17b (Sonc. ed., p. 70) mentions ‘Valeria the proselyte’.] Some of her slaves became Jewesses while she was still a heathen.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:5)


כשם שישראל נכנסין לברית בג׳ מצות כך גרים נכנסין למילה ולטבילה ולקרבן ב׳ מעכבין וא׳ אינו מעכב רא"א גר שנתגייר צריך שיפריש רביעית לקנו רש"א א"צ:


Just as Israel were initiated into the covenant by three precepts, so proselytes are initiated by circumcision, immersion and a sacrifice. [The omission of] the first two debars him [from becoming a proselyte], but [the omission of] the third does not debar him. R. Eliezer [b. Jacob] said: The omission of the sacrifice is also a bar.⁹ This was the ruling of R. Eliezer b. Jacob: A proselyte who becomes a convert is required to set aside a fourth part [of a *dinar*] for his sacrifice of birds;¹⁰ (Sonc. ed., p. 67, n. 12). but R. Simeon says that he is not required to do so.

footnotes:
⁹ Omitted by V but added by MS.K. and H. Cf. Kerith. 9a (Sonc. ed., p. 66).
¹⁰ To be offered when the Temple will be rebuilt; Kerith. loc. cit.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:6)


נפרעין מן הגרים כדברי ר׳ יוסי ר׳ יהודה אומר אין נפרעין ממנו אלא הרי הוא כבן יומו:


Proselytes are punished [for their sins before conversion] in the opinion of R. Jose; R. Judah said: He is not punished [61*a*] but is like a new-born child.


###### Tractate Gerim 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/2:7)


א"ר חנינא בר גמליאל מפני מה גרים מעונין מפני שהם מחשיבין קודם לשנה וקודם לשתים שאגבה את חובי ואעשה את צרכי אלו ממון הן כדבריך אלא שהם קוברים בנים ובני בנים וחלאים רעים ויסורין באין עליהם מפני מה מעונים מפני ז׳ מצות שנצטוו עליהם בני נח:


R. Ḥanina b. Gamaliel said: Why are proselytes afflicted?¹¹ Because they calculate a year before or two years before [their conversion], saying, [‘I shall become a proselyte] when I have collected my debts and when I have finished what I have to do’. R. Jose said to him,¹² ‘If they were to lose money [only as a punishment] you would be right; but they [sometimes] bury their children and grandchildren and sore diseases and chastisements befall them. Why are they afflicted? Because of their [transgression¹³ of] the seven commandments which were given to the descendants of Noah’.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹¹ By God.
¹² ‘R. Jose … him’ added by MS.K. and H.
¹³ While they were still Gentiles.
¹⁴ [The practice of equity, and prohibitions against blasphemy, idolatry, immorality, bloodshed, robbery and eating a limb torn from a live animal; Sanh. 56a (Sonc. ed., pp. 381f.).]



## Chapter 3

###### Tractate Gerim 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:1)


איזהו גר תושב כל שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד ע"ז דברי רבי מאיר רבי יהודה אומר כל שקבל עליו שלא להיות אוכל נבילות:


What is a ‘resident proselyte’?¹ as distinguished from *ger ẓedeḳ*, ‘a righteous proselyte’. Whoever undertakes to abstain from idolatry, in the view of R. Meir; R. Judah said: Whoever undertakes not to eat flesh that has not been ritually slaughtered.² is defined as one who undertook to keep all the commandments except the prohibition against eating flesh not ritually slaughtered, and perhaps that should be the reading here.

footnotes:
¹ Heb. ger toshab
² According to ‘A.Z. 64b (Sonc. ed., p. 314) a ger toshab


###### Tractate Gerim 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:2)


רוקו ומושבו ומשכבו ומי רגליו טמאין עיסתו ושמנו ויינו טהורים ועובר על בל תונה ובל תעשוק ובל תלין פעולת שכיר.


His spittle, his seat, his couch and his urine are unclean; his bread,³ his oil and his wine are clean. The prohibitions *thou shalt not do him wrong*,⁴ *thou shalt not oppress*⁵ and *the wages of a hired servant shall not abide with thee all night*⁶ apply to him.

footnotes:
³ So MS.K. and H; V ‘his dough’.
⁴ Lev. 19, 33.
⁵ Deut. 24, 14.
⁶ Lev. 19, 13.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:3)


אין משיאין לו ולא נושאין ממנו נשים ולא מלוין אותו ולא לוין ממנו ברבית:


We do not marry him [to a Jewess] or take to wife women from him.⁷. We do not lend to him or borrow from him on interest.

footnotes:
⁷ Those within the category of ger toshab


###### Tractate Gerim 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:4)


אין מושיבין אותו בספר ולא בנוה רע אלא בנוה יפה באמצע א"י במקום שאמנותו יוצאת שנאמר (דברים כ״ג:י״ז) עמך ישב בקרבך במקום אשר יבחר וכו׳:


We do not settle him on the frontier⁸ or in an unhealthy district, but in a pleasant district in the centre of the Land of Israel,⁹ where he can find scope for his occupation, as it is stated, *With thee he shall dwell in thy midst, in a place which he shall choose in one of thy gates, thou shalt not wrong him*.¹⁰

footnotes:
⁸ [Where he would be exposed to attack, or by intercourse with foreign neighbours lapse into heathenism.]
⁹ The words ‘in the centre of the Land of Israel’ are superfluous and should perhaps be omitted.
¹⁰ Deut. 23, 17.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:5)


כל ערוה שישראל מצווין עליה מיתת ב"ד אין הגרים מצווין עליה:


Every incestuous marriage which is forbidden to Israel under pain of death at the hands of a *Beth Din* is¹¹ forbidden to proselytes.

footnotes:
¹¹ So MS.K. V and H insert ‘not’. [The question is debated in Sanh. 57b-58a (Sonc. ed., p. 393).]


###### Tractate Gerim 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:6)


הא כיצד היה נשוא אחות אמו ואת אחותה (אמו) מאם רמ"א יוציא וחכ"א יקיים א' מהן:


How is this? If he was married to the sister of his mother and her sister from the [same] mother, R. Meir says that he must dismiss her, but the Sages say that he may keep one of them.¹² it is adduced as an illustration of the statement that ‘a proselyte whose conception was not in holiness, but whose birth was in holiness (i.e. after his mother’s conversion) is forbidden to his mother’s relatives but not to his father’s’. In that case, however, we should certainly have to read here, ‘if he had married his father’s sister from the same father he may keep her, but if from the same mother, R. Meir says’, etc.

footnotes:
¹² This is the lit. rendering of V, which is hopelessly corrupt. MS.K. and H read: ‘How is this? If he was married to the sister of his father from the same father or the sister of his father from the same mother, R. Meir says that he must dismiss her, but the Sages say that he may keep her. [If he has married] two sisters from the same mother, R. Meir says that he must dismiss both, but the Sages say that he must dismiss one of them’. The instance here adduced has nothing to do with the statement which precedes. In Sanh. loc. cit.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:7)


ישראל שבא על בת עובד כוכבים ידון כדיני עובד כוכבים ועובד כוכבים שבא על בת ישראל ידון כדיני ישראל:


An Israelite¹³ who has had intercourse with the daughter of a Gentile is to be tried according to the non-Jewish law, but a Gentile who has had intercourse with the daughter of an Israelite is to be tried according to Jewish law.

footnotes:
¹³ This is an obvious mistake for ‘a Gentile’. [Cf. Sanh. 57b (Sonc. ed., p. 393) where it is explicitly stated.]


###### Tractate Gerim 3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:8)


גר שמת והניח בן ובת שנתגיירו עמו נכסיו ועבדיו ב"ח אם היו העבדים פקחין נקנין במשיכה מפני שאמרו נכסים שאין להם אחריות נקנין בחזקה:


If a proselyte died leaving a son or daughter who became a convert with him, his property is ownerless¹⁴ and his slaves regain their freedom. If the slaves were minors¹⁵ they are acquired by ‘drawing’,¹⁶ because [the Sages] said that movable property is acquired by ‘drawing’ and immovable property by seizure.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁴ [There is nothing in V corresponding to ‘is ownerless’ which is required by the context. MS.K. and H insert ‘is like the deer’, i.e. free, ownerless.]
¹⁵ [This is the reading suggested by N.Y.; V, MS.K. and H have ‘shrewd’. This version agrees with Ḳid. 23a (Sonc. ed., p. 110): ‘If a proselyte dies [without heirs] adult slaves acquire their freedom, but as for minors, whoever takes possession of them gains a title to them’.]
¹⁶ [‘Taking possession by drawing towards one’s self the object to be acquired’ (Jastrow).]
¹⁷ [This is the correct reading as against V’s ‘the Sages said that movable property is acquired by seizure’. Cf. Ḳid. I, 5 (Sonc. ed., p. 124). ‘Movable property’ is lit. ‘property which has no security’, i.e. on which a creditor cannot distrain if sold; ‘immovable property’, on the other hand, like real estate, can be mortgaged for the owner’s debts.]


###### Tractate Gerim 3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:9)


ר׳ אליעזר אומר לא זו בלבד אלא אפילו היה מטייל בתוך שדהו ובא אחד ואמר שדה שלי שדה שלו וחכמים אומרים לא קנה עד שיחזיק:


R. Eliezer said: [Immovable property] is acquired only by seizure; but if someone was walking in the field [of a proselyte who died] and a man came up to him to whom he said, ‘The field is mine’, the field is his; but the Sages say that he does not acquire the property until he has taken possession of it.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁸ [By performing some act such as levelling, etc. Cf. B.B. 100a (Sonc. ed., p. 418, n. 7).]


###### Tractate Gerim 3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:10)


זה בא מן הדרום וזה בא מן הצפון זה זכה במקום הלוכו וזה זכה במקום הלוכו דברי רבי אליעזר וחכמים אומרים זה וזה לא קנה עד שיחזיק:


If one man comes from the south and another from the north, each one acquires the part which he traverses. This is the view of R. Eliezer; but the Sages said: Neither acquires until he has taken possession.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:11)


היו עליו כתובת אשה ובע"ח ואמרה האשה אלו שלי ואלו כתובתי זכתה אלו כתובתי ואלו שלי אין לה אלא כתובתה:


[If a proselyte died] while liable for his wife’s *kethubah* and [the claim of] a creditor and she says, ‘This part of the property belongs to me and this part is due to me under my *kethubah*’, she is entitled [to the whole]. If she says, ‘This part is due to me under my *kethubah* and this part belongs to me’, she is entitled only to her *kethubah*.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:12)


וכן בעל חוב שאמר אלו שלי ואלו חובי זכה אלו חובי ואלו שלי אין לו אלא חובו:


Similarly, if a creditor says, ‘This part belongs to me and that part is for my debt’, he is entitled [to the whole]; but if he says, ‘This part is for my debt and that part belongs to me’, he is entitled only to his debt.


###### Tractate Gerim 3:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/3:13)


היו לו ב׳ עבדים רועי בקר ובא אחד ואמר עבדים הללו והצאן שלי הרי אלו שלו ואם העבדים פקחין אומרים אנו ב"ח והצאן שלפנינו שלנו :


If he had slaves pasturing a flock¹⁹ and someone came and said, ‘These slaves and the flock are mine’, they are his; but if the slaves are shrewd they can say, ‘We are free men and the flock belongs to us’.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ Following the text of MS.K. and H.
²⁰ By declaring themselves freemen they can inherit their master’s property.



## Chapter 4

###### Tractate Gerim 4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:1)


(שמות כ״ב:כ׳) וגר לא תונה ולא תלחצנו לא תונה לו בדברים ולא תלחצנו בממון אל תאמר לו אמש היית עובד הבל ואתה מקודם עד עכשיו חזיר בין שיניך אתה עומד ומדבר עמי ומניין להונאתו (נ"א שאם הוניתו) שהוא יכול לומר כי גרים הייתם מכאן היה ר׳ נתן אומר מום שבך אל תאמר לחבירך:


*And a stranger* [*ger*] *shalt thou not wrong, neither shalt thou oppress him:*¹ you shall not *wrong* him in speech or *oppress* him in money dealings. Do not say to him,² (קרס), *Nebo stoopeth*, alluding to Babylonian deities. ‘Yesterday you were worshipping Bel, Ḳores and Nebo, and till now pig’s flesh was between your teeth, and now you stand up and speak with me!’ And whence [do I learn] [not] to *wrong* him? He can retort, *For ye were strangers in the land of Egypt?*³ [The more correct version is found in Mekilta *ad loc.*: ‘If you wrong him he is able to wrong you? Therefore there is a saying, *For ye were strangers*, etc.’ Hence R. Nathan used to say: Do not taunt your neighbour with the blemish which you yourself have.⁴

footnotes:
¹ Ex. 22, 20.
² What follows is according to MS.K. For Bel, etc., cf. Isa. 46, 1, Bel boweth down
³ Ex. loc. cit.
⁴ [Cf. B.M. 59b (Sonc. ed.,p. 356).]


###### Tractate Gerim 4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:2)


ראב"י אומר לפי שסורו רע הזהיר עליו הכתוב במקומות הרבה [וגר לא תונה ולא תלחצנו] (שם כג) וגר לא תלחץ (וגר לא תונה) ואתם ידעתם את נפש הגר הוא שסורו רע הזהיר עליו הכתוב במקומות הרבה:


R. Eliezer b. Jacob said: Because [the proselyte’s] original nature was evil,⁵ Scripture gave many warnings in connection with him, as it is stated, *And a stranger shalt thou not wrong, neither shalt thou oppress him; for ye know the heart of a stranger*.⁶ Hence because his original nature was evil, Scripture gave many warnings concerning him.

footnotes:
⁵ [When he was a heathen, and ill-treatment by an Israelite may have the effect of making him relapse.]
⁶ Ex. 23, 9.


###### Tractate Gerim 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Gerim/r/4:3)


חביבין הגרים שבכל מקום מכנה אותם כישראל שנא׳ (מלאכי א׳:ב׳) אהבתי אתכם אמר ה׳ (ישעיהו מ״א:ח׳) ואתה ישראל עבדי יעקב אשר בחרתיך ונאמר אהבה בישראל שנאמר אהבתי אתכם אמר ה׳ ונאמר אהבה בגרים (דברים י׳:י״ח) שנאמר ואוהב גר לתת לו לחם נקראו ישראל עבדים והגרים שנאמר (ישעיהו נ״ו:ו׳) להיות לו לעבדים נאמר רצון לישראל שנאמר (שמות כ״ח:ל״ח) והיה על מצחו תמיד לרצון ונאמר רצון בגרים שנאמר (ישעיהו נ״ו:ז׳) עולותיהם וזבחיהם לרצון על מזבחי נאמר שמירה בישראל שנאמר (תהלים קכא) ה׳ שומרך ונאמר שמירה בגרים שנאמר (שם קמו) ה׳ שומר את גרים נאמר שירות בישראל שנאמר (ישעיהו ס״א:ו׳) ואתם כהני ה׳ תקראו משרתי אלהינו [יאמר לכם] ונאמר שירות בגרים שנאמר (שם נו) ובני נכר הנלוים על ה׳ לשרתו חביבין גרים שלא מל א"א לא בן כ׳ ולא בן למ"ד אלא בן צ"ט שנה שאלו מל א"א בן כ׳ ובן למ"ד לא היה גר שנתגייר מן כ׳ שנה ומעלה או בן למ"ד שנה ומעלה אלא הקב"ה היה עמו ובא עד שהגיע לצ"ט שנה שלא לנעול דלת בפני הגרים א"א קרא עצמו גר שנאמר (בראשית כ״ג:ד׳) גר ותושב וגו׳ דוד מלך ישראל קרא עצמו גר שנאמר (תהילים ל״ט:י״ג) כי גר אנכי עמך וכן הוא אומר (ד"ה א כט) כי גרים אנחנו לפניך וגו׳ חביבה א"י שמכשרת גרים היה בא"י ואמר גר אני מקבלים אותו מיד ובחוצה לארץ אין מקבלין אותו אלא אם כן היו עדיו עמו וחביבה א"י שהיא מכפרת על עונות ופשעים שנאמר (ישעיהו ל״ג:כ״ד) ובל יאמר שכן חליתי וכן אתה מוצא בד׳ כיתות העומדים לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא שנאמר (שם מב) זה יאמר לה׳ אני זה שכלו למקום ולא נתערב בו חטא וזה יקרא בשם יעקב אלו גרי הצדק וזה יכתוב ידו לה׳ אלו בעלי תשובה ובשם ישראל יכנה אלו יראי שמים:


Beloved are proselytes [by God], for [Scripture] everywhere uses the same epithets of them as of Israel; [61*b*] as it is stated, *But thou, Israel, My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen*.⁷ is here interpreted as *ibid.* XLIV, 5, *And another shall call himself by the name of Jacob*—these are the proselytes of righteousness (cf. towards the end of this tractate). The order of the quotations in V is confused. The term ‘love’ is applied to Israel, as it is stated, *I have loved you, saith the Lord*,⁸ and the term ‘love’ is applied to proselytes, as it is stated, *And He loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment*.⁹ Israel are called ‘servants’, as it is stated, *For unto Me the children of Israel are servants*,¹⁰ and proselytes are called ‘servants’, as it is stated, *To be His servants*.¹¹ The term ‘acceptable’ is used of Israel, as it is stated, *And it shall be always upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before the Lord*,¹² and the term ‘acceptable’ is used of proselytes, as it is stated, *Their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices shall be acceptable upon Mine altar*.¹³ The term ‘keeping’ is applied to Israel, as it is stated, *The Lord is thy keeper, the Lord is thy shade upon thy right hand*,¹⁴ and the term ‘keeping’ is applied to proselytes, as it is stated, *The Lord preserveth the strangers*.¹⁵ CXLVI, 9. The term ‘ministering’ is applied to Israel, as it is stated, *But ye shall be named the priests of the Lord, men shall call you the ministers of our God*,¹⁶ and the term ‘ministering’ is applied to proselytes, as it is stated, *Also the aliens, that join themselves to the Lord, to minister unto Him*.¹⁷ LVI, 6.
Beloved are proselytes seeing that our father Abraham did not circumcise himself when he was twenty or thirty years of age, but when he was ninety-nine years old;¹⁸ since if he had circumcised himself when he was twenty or thirty years old, no Gentile would have become a proselyte when he had passed the age of twenty or thirty. The Holy One, blessed be He, kept putting it off¹⁹ until he had reached ninety-nine years, so as not to close the door in the face of proselytes, [and to allow more days and years so as to increase the reward of those who do His will, as it is stated, *The Lord was pleased, for His righteousness’ sake, to make the teaching great and glorious*].²⁰
Our father Abraham called himself a *ger*, as it is stated, *I am a stranger* [*ger*] *and a sojourner with you*.²¹ Similarly David, king of Israel, called himself a *ger*, as it is stated, *For I am a stranger* [*ger*] *with Thee*,²² and likewise it states, *For we are strangers before Thee*.²³
Beloved is the Land of Israel because it makes proselytes fit [to be received]. If a man says in the Land of Israel, ‘I am a proselyte’, he is accepted at once, but outside the Land of Israel he is not accepted unless his witnesses are with him. Beloved is the Land of Israel because it atones for iniquities and transgressions, as it is stated, *And the inhabitant shall not say: ‘I am sick’, the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity*.²⁴
And so you find in the four classes that stand before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is stated, *One shall say: ‘I am the Lord’s’; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel*.²⁵ XLIV, 5. *One shall say: ‘I am the Lord’s’*—this alludes to one who belongs wholly to the Omnipresent and has no admixture of sin. *Another shall call himself by the name of Jacob*—this alludes to the proselytes of righteousness.²⁶ *Another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord*—this alludes to those who repent. *And surname himself by the name of Israel*—this alludes to those who fear Heaven.

# Tractate Kallah

מסכת כלה

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah)

נישואין, יחסי אישות וכללי התנהגות מינית נאותה.

Marriage, intercourse, and proper sexual behavior.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 26, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 26)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Kallah 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:1)


כלה בלא ברכה אסורה לבעלה כנדה מה נדה שלא טבלה אסורה לבעלה (כנדה) אף כלה בלא ברכה אסורה לבעלה. ומניין לברכת חתנים מן התורה שנאמר (בראשית כ״ד:ס׳) ויברכו את רבקה. ומנין שאפילו אלמנה אסורה שנאמר (רות ד׳:י״א) ויקח (בועז) עשרה אנשים וגו' ויאמרו כל העם אשר בשער והזקנים עדים יתן ה׳ וגו' ויהי ביתך כבית פרץ וגו׳.


A bride¹) and marriage (*ḳiddushin*) denoted two stages different from what they are now. *’Erusin* took place in the bride’s home and *ḳiddushin* subsequently in the bridegroom’s home. It is important to note that the ceremony of *’erusin* was binding upon the bridal couple and could not be dissolved without a bill of divorce. Later the current custom prevailed whereby the two ceremonies were combined and performed at the same time (cf. P.B., pp. 298f., the benediction on the first of the pages being of *’erusin*). is forbidden to her husband without the [marriage] benediction² in the same manner as a *niddah*.³ Just as a *niddah*⁴ who has not immersed [in the ritual bath] is forbidden to her husband, so likewise is a bride forbidden to her husband without the [marriage] benediction. Whence is the benediction of bridegrooms derived from the Torah? As it is stated, *And they blessed Rebekah*.⁵ And whence do we derive that even a widow is so forbidden?⁶ As it is stated, *And he took ten men of the elders of the city … And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders said, We are witnesses. The Lord make the woman … and let thy house be like the house of Perez*.⁷

footnotes:
¹ Here used in the sense of a betrothed girl. In the Talmudic period betrothal (’erusin
² This consisted of seven benedictions. For the wording cf. K.R. I, 1, below p. 415f.; Keth. 7b-8a (Sonc. ed., pp. 31ff.); P.B., p. 299.
³ In Biblical law the period of menstrual impurity lasted seven days (Lev. 15, 19ff.) but was extended by the Rabbis to eleven days. At the end of the period immersion in a ritual bath was necessary.
⁴ Whose period of purification has ended.
⁵ Gen. 24, 60.
⁶ On remarriage without the benediction, cf. Keth. 7a (Sonc. ed., p. 26).

###### Tractate Kallah 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:2)


כלה שנבעלה יום ראשון אסורה כל שבעה ואסור ליטול הימנה כוס כל שבעה דברי רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע אומר עד שיבדוק הדבר אם היתה נדה בבית אביה אסורה ואם לאו מותרת. שאלו את ר״א מהו לשתות מיד הכלה כל זמן שבעלה מיסב עמה. אמר להם כל השותה מיד כלה כאילו שותה מיד זונה אמרו לו והלא כל בנות ישראל יש להם דרך ארץ. אמר להם חס ושלום כל מי שאין התורה עובר על פיו אין בו דרך ארץ. הכריז ר״א (בן עזריה) בשלש מאות שופרות ואמר כלה אחת בנות ת״ח ואחת בנות עמי הארץ השותה בכלה כשותה בזונה ועוד אמרו כל המקבל כוס מיד כלה ושותהו אין לו חלק לעולם הבא:


After the consummation of her marriage on the first day, a bride is forbidden⁸ for the whole of the succeeding seven days, and it is not permitted to take any object⁹ from her hand all the seven days. This is the view of R. Eliezer, but R. Joshua said: Not until the matter is examined—if she was *niddah* while still in her father’s house, she is forbidden [to her husband], but if not she is allowed to him.
R. Eliezer was asked, ‘Is it permissible to drink from the hand of the bride so long as her husband is sitting with her at the festive table?’ He replied, ‘Whoever drinks from the hand of a bride is as though he drinks from the hand of a harlot’. [His colleagues] said to him, ‘Are not all the daughters of Israel possessed of good manners?’¹⁰ He answered, ‘God forbid! Anyone who is not familiar with the Torah¹¹ cannot be possessed of good manners’. R. Eleazar b. Azariah made a public declaration accompanied by the sounding of three hundred *shofars*,¹²’. These were sounded to increase the solemnity of the declaration. ‘Whether a bride be of the daughters of a scholar or of an *‘am ha-’areẓ*, he who drinks from her hand is as though he drinks from the hand of a harlot’. He further said, ‘Whoever takes a cup from the hand of a bride and drinks from it has no share in the World to Come’.

footnotes:
⁸ To her husband; cf. Nid. 65b (Sonc. ed., p. 460).
⁹ lit. ‘a cup’.
¹⁰ And it is therefore usual for a bride to hand things to the guests.
¹¹ And since women are not usually learned in the Torah it cannot be assumed that they possess good manners.
¹² In K.R. I, 5, below p. 418 the reading is ‘four hundred shofars


###### Tractate Kallah 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:3)


הקורא פסוק משיר השירים ועשאו כמין זמר וכן הקורא פסוק מדברי תורה בבית המשתאות שלא בזמנו מביא מבול לעולם מפני שהתורה חוגרת שק ועומדת לפני הקב״ה ואומרת רבש"ע עשאוני בניך ככנור המנגנים בו ליצים. אמר לה בתי בשעה שהן שמחים מה יהיו עושים אמרה לו רבש״ע אם תלמיד חכם הוא יעסוק בתורה ובלימוד ובמעשים טובים ובאגדות ובעלי מקרא במקרא ובעלי משנה במשנה בהלכות הפסח בפסח ושל עצרת בעצרת ושל חג בחג. העיד ר״ש ואמר כל הקורא פסוק בזמנו מביא טובה לעולם [שנאמר] (משלי טו) ודבר בעתו מה טוב.


He who recites a verse from the Song of Songs¹³ rendering it as a [secular] song, and similarly whoever recites a verse from the Torah unseasonably at banqueting tables, causes the Flood to come upon the world; because the Torah clothes itself in sackcloth, stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and complains, ‘Sovereign of the universe! Thy children have made me as a harp upon which scorners play’. To this He replies, ‘My daughter, when they rejoice what should they do?’ She makes the rejoinder, ‘Sovereign of the universe! If he is a scholar let him occupy himself with the Torah, with study and good deeds and *’aggadoth;* let students of Scripture occupy themselves with Scripture, students of Midrash and Mishnah with the laws of Passover on Passover, the laws of Pentecost on Pentecost and the laws of Tabernacles on Tabernacles’. R. Simeon¹⁴ testified and said: Whoever reads a verse in season brings good to the world, as it is stated, *And a word in due season, how good is it!*¹⁵

footnotes:
¹³ Cf. Sanh. 101a (Sonc. ed., p. 684). GRA reads ‘evil’ instead of ‘Flood’.
¹⁴ GRA adds ‘b. Eleazar in the name of R. Joshua b. Ḥananiah’.
¹⁵ Prov. 15, 23.


###### Tractate Kallah 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/1:4)


המשגר כוס של ברכה לאשה שלא מדעת בעלה חייב מיתה מפני שדעתו רבה עליו. רבי אומר מפני שיצר הרע רבה עליו. וכן בני חבורה ששגרו כוס של ברכה לאשה שלא מדעת בעלה חייבים מיתה מפני שדעתן רבה עליהן. רבי אומר מפני שיצר הרע רבה עליהן.


One who sends the cup of benediction¹⁶ to a woman without the knowledge of her husband forfeits his life because his mind prevailed over him.¹⁷ Rabbi [Judah the Prince] said: Because the evil inclination has prevailed over him. Similarly the members of a company who send the cup of benediction to a woman without the knowledge of her husband forfeit their lives because their minds prevailed over them. Rabbi [Judah the Prince] said: Because the evil inclination has prevailed over them.

footnotes:
¹⁶ Used in the Grace after meals.
¹⁷ lit. ‘is great over him’. GRA emends: ‘over him’ to ‘over her’, i.e. he is attracted to her. Similarly in the next sentences.



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Kallah 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:1)


המרצה מעות לאשה מידו לידה בשביל להסתכל בה אפילו הוא כמשה רבינו שקבל תורה מהר סיני לא ינקה מדינה של גיהנם שנאמר (משלי י״א:כ״א) יד ליד לא ינקה רע. הרי הוא אומר (במדבר ל״א:נ׳) ונקרב את קרבן ה׳ איש אשר מצא כלי זהב אצעדה וגו׳ אצעדה זו בירית. וצמיד אלו השיראים. עגול זה דפוס של (בית) הדדים. כומז זה דפוס של בית הרחם. לכפר על נפשותינו לפני ה׳ א״ל משה לישראל שמא חזרתם לקלקלכם הראשון. אמרו לו (שם) לא נפקד ממנו איש אמר להם א״כ כפרה זו למה. אמרו לו אם מידי עבירה יצאנו מידי הרהור לא יצאנו. טבעת למה לפי שכל המסתכל באשה בכוונה כאילו בא עליה מכאן אמרו חכמים כל הנוגע באצבע קטנה של אשה כאילו נוגע באותו מקום.


He who pays money to a woman,¹⁸ counting from his hand into her hand in order to gaze at her, even if he be like Moses our teacher who received the Torah from Mount Sinai, will not be exempt from the penalty of Gehinnom; as it is stated, *Hand to hand, the evil man shall not be unpunished*.¹⁹
Behold Scripture declares, *And we have brought the Lord’s offering, what every man hath gotten, of jewels of gold, armlets, and bracelets, signet-rings, ear-rings, and girdles, to make atonement for our souls before the Lord*.²⁰ *‘Eẓadah* (*armlets*) means a garter; *ẓamid* (*bracelets*) silk cloaks; *‘agil* (*ear-rings*) a cast of the female breasts; *kumaz* (*girdles*) a cast of the womb. *To make atonement for our souls:* Moses said to Israel, ‘Perhaps you have returned to your former sinful lapse’.²¹ They replied to him, ‘*There lacketh not one man of us*’.²² 49. ‘If so,’ he retorted, ‘why this atonement?’ They replied, ‘We may have escaped sin, but we have not escaped sinful thoughts’. Why [did they offer] signet-rings? Because whoever gazes intentionally at a woman is as though he had intercourse with her. Hence the Rabbis declared: Whoever touches a woman’s little finger is as though he touched ‘that place’.²³

footnotes:
¹⁸ Cf. ‘Erub. 18b (Sonc. ed., p. 125).
¹⁹ Prov. 11, 21, E.V. My hand upon it!
²⁰ Num. 31, 50.
²¹ Their association with the women of Midian; cf. Shab. 64a (Sonc. ed., p. 305).
²² ibid.
²³ The pudenda; cf. Ber. 24a (Sonc. ed., p. 145). So GRA emending the text according to the Talmudic version.


###### Tractate Kallah 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:2)


(וכן) כל המסתכל בעקיבה של אשה הויין לו בנים בעלי מומין חגרין סומין אלמין חרשין. רבי אליעזר אומר מפני שתבעה למטה ואינה נתבעת. רבי יהושע אומר מפני שאמרה בשעת בעילה אנוסה אני רבי עקיבא אומר מפני שאומרת בשעת טהרתה טמאה אני.


He who gazes at a woman’s heel will have deformed children. [Why are children born] lame, blind, dumb or deaf? R. Eliezer said: Because [the husband] claimed marital rights but she refused. R. Joshua said: Because she declared at the time of cohabitation, ‘I have been forced’.²⁴ R. ‘Aḳiba said: Because she says, ‘I am unclean’ when she is clean.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁴ To cohabitate while she was impure and nevertheless submitted.
²⁵ To annoy him.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:3)


רבי נחמיה אומר בעון שנאת חנם אשתו מפלת נפלים ומריבה רבה בתוך ביתו ובניו ובנותיו מתים כשהם קטנים.


R. Nehemiah said: Because of the sin of causeless hatred a man’s wife suffers miscarriage, contention is rife in his house, and his sons and daughters die young.²⁶

²⁶ Cf. Shab. 32b (Sonc. ed., p. 149).


###### Tractate Kallah 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:4)


רבי נהוראי אומר כל המבייש פני חבירו סוף הוא מתבייש ולא עוד אלא שמלאכי חבלה דוחפין אותו וטורדין אותו מן העולם ומראין קלונו לכל באי עולם וכל מי שיש לו בושת פנים לא במהרה הוא חוטא שנאמר (שמות כ׳:י״ז) ובעבור תהיה יראתו על פניכם לבלתי תחטאו. וכל מי שאין לו בושת פנים בידוע שלא עמדו אבותיו תחת הר סיני.


R. Nehorai said: Whoever puts his neighbour to shame will in the end himself be put to shame; furthermore, the Angels of Destruction thrust and drive him out of the world and expose his shame before all mankind. But whoever is shamefaced will not speedily yield to sin; as it is stated, *And that His fear may be before you, that ye sin not*.²⁷ As regards anyone who is not shamefaced, it is certain that his forefathers did not stand at the foot of Mount Sinai.

²⁷ Ex. 20, 17.


###### Tractate Kallah 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:5)


אמר רבי יוחנן ארבעה דברים סחו לי מלאכי השרת ואלו הן חגרים סומים אלמים חרשים. חגרים מפני מה מפני שהופכים את שולחנם ועושים כמעשה בהמות. סומים מפני מה מפני שמסתכלין באותו מקום. חרשים מפני מה מפני שמספרין בשעת תשמיש. אלמים מפני מה מפני שנושקים באותו מקום. וחכמים אומרים [אין הלכה כרבי יוחנן אלא] כל מה שאדם רוצה לעשות באשתו [עושה כי אין הדבר דומה אלא למי שלקח בשר מטבח רצה אוכלו צלי רצה אוכלו מבושל רצה אוכלו ע״ג גחלים]:


R. Joḥanan said:²⁸ The Ministering Angels told me four things and they are related to the lame, the blind, the dumb and the deaf. Why [are children born] lame? Because [their parents] overturned their table²⁹ and behaved like animals. Why [are children born] blind? Because [their parents] gaze at ‘that place’. Why [are children born] deaf? Because [their parents] converse³⁰ during cohabitation. Why [are children born] dumb? Because [their parents] kiss ‘that place’. The Sages say that the *halakah* is not in agreement with R. Joḥanan, but a man may do with his wife as he desires;³¹ because the matter can be best compared to a man who purchased meat from the butcher: if he wishes he eats it raw, if he wishes he eats it boiled, if he wishes he eats it roasted over coals.

footnotes:
²⁸ Cf. Ned. 20a (Sonc. ed., p. 57).
²⁹ A euphemism for unnatural intercourse.
³⁰ i.e. they conduct themselves with levity while performing a religious command.
³¹ At the time of cohabitation.


###### Tractate Kallah 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:6)


שאלו את אימא שלום אשתו של רבי אליעזר אחותו של רבן גמליאל אמרו לה מפני מה בניך יפין ובשעת תשמיש מהו אצלך. אמרה להם לא היה מספר עמי לא במשמרה ראשונה ולא במשמרה אחרונה אלא בבינונית מגלה טפח ומכסה טפח ודומה כמי שכפאו שד. אמרתי לו כל כך למה. אמר לי שלא תעלה על דעתי באשה אחרת ונמצאו בניי באים לידי ממזרות:


Imma Shalom,³² the wife of R. Eliezer and sister of Rabban Gamaliel was asked, ‘Why are your children beautiful? And during intercourse how does [your husband] conduct himself towards you?’ She replied, ‘He does not converse³³ with me during the first or last watch, but only during the middle watch;³⁴ [and when he cohabits] he uncovers a handbreadth and covers a handbreadth, and it is as though he was urged on by a demon. And when I questioned him, “What is the reason for all this?”³⁵ he replied, “So that another woman should not come to my mind³⁶ and my children consequently come within the category of bastards” ’.

footnotes:
³² Cf. Ned. loc. cit.
³³ A euphemism for cohabitation.
³⁴ The night was divided into three equal periods called ‘watches’.
³⁵ For selecting the middle watch.
³⁶ During the first and last watches of the night women are to be found in the streets.


###### Tractate Kallah 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah/r/2:7)


מכאן אמרו עשרה הם כממזרים ואינם ממזרים ואלו הן בני אמה בני שפחה בני שנואה (בני נדה) בני נדוי בני תמורה בני מריבה בני שכורה בני גרושת הלב בני ערבוביא וי״א אף בני ישינה. והבועל ארוסתו בבית חמיו שלא בכתובה הויין לו בנים ויתקין חלשות אלו בועלי נדות. מכוערים אלו בני טהרות ספק.


Hence [the Sages] declared: Ten³⁷, II, p. 310, n. 3.] categories of people are like bastards but are not [legally] such, and they are: the children [born] of fear,³⁸ the children of a maidservant, the children of a hated wife, (the children of a *niddah*),³⁹ the children of one who is under a ban of excommunication, the children of a woman thought to be another,⁴⁰ the children of [a marriage characterized by] strife, the children of a drunken woman, the children of a wife divorced in the heart,⁴¹ the children of promiscuity, and some add, the children of a sleeping woman.⁴² One who has intercourse with his betrothed in her father-in-law’s house without the *kethubah* having been drawn up⁴³ having taken place, the drawing up of the *kethubah* forming part of the ceremony. Cf. the opening words of this tractate, ‘A bride is forbidden’, etc. N.Y. has another explanation based on *’Eben Ha‘ezer* LXVI, 3, viz. a man must not live with his wife without a *kethubah*. In the context this interpretation is wide of the mark. will have sickly children. Weak children are the issue of those who cohabit with women who are *niddah;* ugly children [are born] of women in a doubtful state of ritual purity.

⁴⁰ lit. ‘children of exchange’, i.e. when a man has two wives and cohabits with one under the impression that she is the other.
⁴¹ i.e. in the heart of her husband; he has the intention of divorcing her while yet cohabiting with her.
⁴² During the intercourse

###### Tractate Kallah 2:8
