###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:2)


**ברייתא** לא ישמח אדם בין הבוכים ולא יבכה בין השמחים לא יהא ער בין הישנים ולא יהא ישן בין הערים: **[גמ׳]** מאי איריא דתני לא ישמח ברישא ליתני לא יבכה. חדא דמידי דפורעונותא לא קתני ואדרבה דרבים עדיפא אלא כדשלמה נקיט ליה טוב ללכת אל בית אבל דיקא נמי דקתני לא ישמח ולא קתני לא ישחוק וקתני סוף לא יבכה ולא קתני לא יזעף. לעולם אל יהי אדם קפדן בסעודה בסעודתייהו הוא דלא להוי הא בדרשא ובישיבה ובדברים אחרים להוי. הא ב״ה קתני לה דקאמרי ליה לשמאי אף ע״ג דכביש לך קפדא להטיל אימא על הבריות בביתא מיהו לא ליקפד מר דלמא נמנע למעבד מצוה. מעשה בשלשה בני אדם שהמרו זה את זה ואמרו כל מי שילך ויקניט את הלל יטול ארבע מאות זוז ואותו יום ערב שבת היה וכו׳. מעשה בר׳ עקיבא שהיה מהלך בדרך וחד מן אתינא איקלע לגבי חד עכו״ם פרש לון ארבע ערשוון ועבד לון שירו סגיא ואשקי לון חמרא אמרי חזיין אנן דהדין חמרא דמייתא הוא אייתי לון בשרא אמרי הדין בשרא דכלבא הוה אייתי להון מורסא אמרי מי רגלים הוה בה אייתי לון חרדלא אמרי חפשושין הוה בה אזל לגבי ההיא קפילא א״ל מאי עובדיה דההוא חמרא א״ל ולא מידי א״ל אשתבעינך דתימא לי א״ל כרמא דאבא הוה והוה ביה קבריה. אזל לגבי טבחא וא״ל גדיא הוא דמיתא אימיה ואונקתיה מן כלבא. אזל לגבי מוריסא א״ל ליליא חד הוינא רוי ואחדוניה לבבא באנפוי וצריכנא למי רגלים ולא למסתגי לי פתחתי לה לדנא ורמאי ליה אזל לגבי חרדלא א״ל ליליא חד שבקתיה מגלי ועלון ביה. אזל ואטרח לון ועבד לון שירו אמרין דין לדין חזיין אנן כרעיה דמריה ביתא ככרעיה מימוס. שמע מארי ביתא א״ל דילמא קושטא אינון אמרין אזל עבד נפשיה מרע כתבין ליה כולי עלמא א״ל לאימיהא אילו אמרת לי שמא דאבא מסתינא אמרה ליה אמר לה משקרת. כיון דחזיתיה מסתער א״ל ברי זימנא חדא אייתי לי בעלי חד זמא ואיתבעלית ליה ועברתך. אזל גפף להון וסגיד להון ואמר קושטא אנתון עמא דאלהא קדישא והוא שאמר שלמה כי ברוב חכמה רב כעס ויוסיף דעת יוסיף מכאוב: עובדא הוה בחד גברא דאתא לבי כנשתא א״ל לינוקא סב הדין פריטי ואייתי מה נאכל ונשבע ונותר וניתי לביתין אייתי ליה מילחא א״ל מרי תיכול ותשבע ותותיר ותוביל:


BARAITHA. One should not be joyous when in the presence of those who weep, or weep in the presence of those who rejoice. One should not be awake among those who sleep or asleep among those who are awake.
GEMARA. On what grounds does the Baraitha first teach, ‘One should not be joyous’? Let it first teach, ‘Or weep’, etc.! Firstly, because one should not begin with unfortunate circumstances,²¹ but on the contrary, priority should be given to the majority.²² [The Baraitha] follows the teaching of Solomon [who wrote], *It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting*.²³ Here is an additional proof: [The Baraitha] reads, ‘One should not be joyous’ and not ‘One should not make merry’, and then ‘or weep’ and not ‘be serious’.²⁴
BARAITHA. One should not be impatient at meals.
GEMARA. One should not be [impatient] at meals; [is it then to be inferred from this] that in giving an exposition [of Torah], in studying and in other matters one may be [impatient]? Did not Beth Hillel cite this and say to Shammai, ‘Although you are hot-tempered and consequently overawe your fellow-beings, yet do not display impatience [towards the members of your household]²⁵ lest you hinder them from performing good deeds’?
²⁶It once happened that two²⁷ men made a wager with each other, saying, ‘He who goes and makes Hillel angry shall receive four hundred *zuz’*. Said one, ‘I will go and incense him’.²⁸ That day was the Sabbath-eve, and Hillel was washing his head. He went, passed by the door of his house and called out, ‘Is Hillel here, is Hillel here?’¹) He spoke rudely, without addressing Hillel by his title. Thereupon he robed and went out to him, saying, ‘My son, what do you require?’ ‘I have a question to ask,’ he said. ‘Ask, my son,’ he prompted. Thereupon he asked, ‘Why are the heads of the Babylonians²⁹ round?’ ‘My son, you have asked a great question,’ replied he; ‘because they have no skilful midwives.’ He departed, tarried a while, returned and called out, ‘Is Hillel here, is Hillel here?’ He robed and went out to him, saying, ‘My son, what do you require?’ ‘I have a question to ask,’ said he. ‘Ask, my son,’ he prompted. Thereupon he asked, ‘Why are the eyes of the Palmyreans bleared?’ ‘My son, you have asked a great question,’ replied he; ‘because they live in sandy places.’ He departed, tarried a while, returned and called out, ‘Is Hillel here, is Hillel here?’ He robed and went out to him, saying, ‘My son, what do you require?’ ‘I have a question to ask,’ said he. ‘Ask, my son,’ he prompted. He asked, ‘Why are the feet of the Africans wide?’ ‘My son, you have asked a great question,’ said he; ‘because they live in watery marshes.’³⁰ ‘I have many questions to ask,’ said he, ‘but fear that you may become angry.’ Thereupon he robed, sat before him and said, ‘Ask all the questions you have to ask’. ‘Are you the Hillel who is called the *Nasi’* of Israel?’ ‘Yes,’ he replied. ‘If that is so,’ he retorted, ‘may there not be many like you in Israel.’ ‘Why, my son?’ queried he. ‘Because I have lost four hundred *zuz* through you,’ complained he. ‘Be careful of your moods,’ he answered, ‘Hillel is worth it that you should lose four hundred *zuz* and yet another four hundred *zuz* through him, yet Hillel shall not lose his temper.’
³¹It once happened that R. ‘Aḳiba, accompanied by an Athenian, went on a journey and chanced to stay with a Gentile. He prepared for them four beds, laid an abundant meal before them and gave them wine to drink. They said, ‘We discern that this wine [has the flavour of]the dead’. He brought them meat and they said, ‘This meat is dog’s flesh’. He brought them pickle and they said, ‘It contains urine’. He brought them mustard and they said, ‘It contains beetles’. [The host] went to the tavern-keeper and asked, ‘What happened to the wine?’ He replied, ‘Nothing’. He said, ‘I adjure you to tell me’. He replied, ‘The wine comes from my father’s vineyard where he is buried’. He went to the butcher who told him, ‘It was the meat of a lamb whose dam died and I made her suck from a bitch’. He went to the pickle-maker who told him, ‘One night I was drunk and [my family] locked me in. I wanted to pass water but was unable to go out, so I opened this [jar of pickle] and poured the urine into it’. He went to the mustard-maker who told him, ‘One night I left [the mustard] uncovered and beetles got into it’. He then took the trouble to prepare [another] meal for them. They said one to another, ‘We notice that the host’s legs are like those of a clown’. The host overheard this and said [to himself], ‘Perhaps these men speak the truth’. So he pretended to be very ill and people came to visit him. He said to his mother, ‘If you disclose to me the name of my father I will recover’. She told him, but he said to her, ‘You are telling a lie’. Since she noticed that he was grieved she said to him, ‘My son, once my husband brought a clown to me; I misconducted myself with him and conceived you’. He went and embraced them, bowed to them and exclaimed, ‘In truth you are the people of the Holy God’. This is what Solomon said, *For in much wisdom is much vexation; and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow*.³²
³³A man once entered a school and said to a child, ‘Take this money and bring me something of which we can eat our fill and leave some over to take home’. He brought him salt and said to him, ‘Sir, you may eat your fill and leave some over to take home’.

footnotes:

²² And the majority rejoice rather than weep.
²³ Eccl. 7, 2. Here mourning is mentioned first.
²⁴ The wording of the Baraitha proves that, like Ecclesiastes, it does not deal with ordinary merry-making and seriousness, but with rejoicings at a marriage-feast and the anguish one feels in a house of mourning.
²⁵ On terrorizing one’s household, cf. Giṭ. 6b-7a (Sonc. ed., p. 21).
²⁶ For the story, cf. Shab. 31a (Sonc. ed., pp. 138f.).
²⁷ V has ‘three’.
²⁸ V has ‘etc.’ The anecdote is here reproduced in full from the Soncino version.
¹ (28a
²⁹ Hillel was a Babylonian, and so the question was intended as a personal insult.
³⁰ To enable them to walk with ease.
³¹ For a parallel to the story, cf. Midrash Rabbah, Lamentations, I, 1, §4 (Sonc. ed., pp. 74f.).
³² Eccl. 1, 18. The information which he obtained from his mother caused him sorrow.
³³ Cf. Midrash Rabbah, Lamentations, I, 1, §7 (Sonc. ed., p. 77).


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:3)


**ברייתא** לא יאכל אדם שום ובצל מראשו אלא מעליו ואם אכל הרי זה גרגרן. לא יאכל אדם בכל אצבעותיו מפני שנראה כגרגרן. ולא יכניס ידו לתוך פיהו: **[גמ׳]** אמר רבא לא שנו אלא בתוך אכילה אבל לאחר אכילה לא מ״ט משום אסתניס. ולא יתן בכוסו אלא כדי דעתו מ״ט משום שיורין דאמר מר כל שיורי כוסות מטפשין חוץ משיורי הבדלה. האי מאן דשתי שיורי ארבעין לא חיי לא יטול אדם את המקדא לשתות ופיהו מלא חיישינן לאניני הדעת לא יטול אדם את הכלי ביד ואצבעותיו מלוכלכות ברוטב. לא ינפח במים וישתה משום שתים ת״ר שלשה חייהם אינם חיין ואלו הם הרחמנים והרתחנין ואניני הדעת אמר רב יוסף וכלהו איתנהו בי. כל ימי עני רעים זה שדעתו רעה וטוב לב זה מי שדעתו יפה ד״א כל ימי עני רעים זה [רחמני וטוב לב זה] אכזרי. דרש רבא כל מי שיש בו שלש מדות הללו בידוע שהוא מזרעו של אברהם [אבינו] רחמן וביישן וגומל חסדים בשלמא גומל חסדים דכתיב חסד לאברהם בישן נמי כדדריש רבא הנה נא ידעתי [כי אשה יפת מראה את] ולא עד עכשיו. אלא רחמן הא אברהם לא רחים על בריה. היינו רבותיה דאברהם להודיעך חבתו בהקב״ה :


BARAITHA.³⁴ A man should not eat leek or onion from its top but from the leaves; and if he did eat [in that manner] he is a glutton. A man should not eat using all his fingers because he has the appearance of a glutton; nor should one put his hand into his mouth.
GEMARA. Raba said: This³⁵ applies only during the meal but not after it. Why? Because he may be delicate.³⁶
BARAITHA. He should only fill his cup with as much as it is his intention [to drink].
GEMARA. What is the reason? Because of the ‘remnants’.³⁷ For the master said: All the ‘remnants’ of cups make one dull except the ‘remnants’ of the *Habdalah*.³⁸ in section *Shabbath*, §299. One who drinks ‘remnants’ for forty [days] will not survive.
BARAITHA. One should not take a potsherd which is full to the brim and drink from it so as not to offend fastidious persons. One should not handle a vessel with greasy fingers; nor should one blow on water and drink it for two [reasons].³⁹
GEMARA. The Rabbis have taught:⁴⁰ There are three whose life is not life, viz. the [over-] compassionate, the hot-tempered and the fastidious. R. Joseph said: All these [qualities] are found in me.
[It is written,] *All the days of the poor are evil*—this refers to a discontented man. *But he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast*⁴¹—this refers to a contented man.⁴² Another explanation: *All the days of the poor are evil*—this refers to the compassionate. *But he that is of a merry heart*—this refers to the cruel.
Raba expounded:⁴³ Whoever is distinguished by the following three characteristics is certain that he is of the seed of our father Abraham: merciful, bashful and benevolent. This is all right with the benevolent, for it is written, *Thou wilt show faithfulness to Jacob, mercy to Abraham;*⁴⁴, i.e. benevolence, is associated with Abraham’s name. also bashful, as Raba interpreted: *Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon;*⁴⁵ but not until now; cf. B.B. 16a (Sonc. ed., p. 80). but why merciful? Abraham had no mercy upon his son!⁴⁶ Herein is to be found the greatness of Abraham, to make known how great was his love for the Holy One, blessed be He.⁴⁷

footnotes:

³⁵ Not to put one’s hand into his mouth.
³⁶ And he must remove the bits which stuck to his teeth.
³⁷ The wine left over in the cup.

³⁹ Blowing causes foam and drinking it brings on catarrh in the head. Further, if he blows away the foam, it leads to poverty because some of the liquid is lost in the process. Cf. Ḥul. 105b (Sonc. ed., p. 585).
⁴⁰ Pes. 113b (Sonc. ed., p. 584).
⁴¹ Prov. 15, 15.
⁴² B.B. 145b (Sonc. ed., p. 628); Sanh. 100b (Sonc. ed., p. 683).
⁴³ Cf. Yeb. 79a (Sonc. ed., p. 535); Beẓah 32b (Sonc. ed., p. 165).
⁴⁴ Micah 7, 20. Mercy
⁴⁵ Gen. 12, 11. Now
⁴⁶ Isaac, whom he was ready to sacrifice at God’s command.
⁴⁷ The episode has no relationship to the Patriarch’s mercy.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:4)


**ברייתא** לא יעבור אדם פרוסה בקערה ולא יקנח את הקערה בפרוסה ולא ישתה אדם מכוסו ויתן לחברו ולא ישוך אדם את פתו ויתננו לחברו אלא א"כ מחיש (אולי צ״ל מכיר) דעתו של חברו חמשה דברים נאמרו בפת אמר רבא אין פורסין לא את הפרוסה על הספר ולא את הספר על הפרוסה ואין סומכין לא את הספר בפרוסה ולא את הפרוסה בספר חישב עליו לקדש אסור לזורקו במקום מטונף:


BARAITHA.⁴⁸ One should not move a piece of bread across the plate or wipe the plate with it. He should not drink from his cup and pass it to his friend; nor should he bite into the bread and pass it to his friend unless he knows his friend’s mind [that he does not object]. Five things have been said in connection with bread:⁴⁹ [Raw meat should not be placed on bread, or a cup of wine on bread, or a plate on bread. Bread should not be thrown about, and one should not sit on articles of food].
GEMARA. Raba said: A piece of bread should not be placed on a book or a book on a piece of bread; a book should not be rested against a piece of bread or a piece of bread against a book. If it was his intention to recite *Ḳiddush* over it, he may not put it in an unclean place.

footnotes:
⁴⁸ Cf. DER IX, p. 558.
⁴⁹ Cf. Ber. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 305) where the reading is ‘four things’. The passage within brackets is inserted by H but omitted by V.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:5)


**ברייתא** לא ישלח אדם לחברו חבית של מים לשם שמן **[גמ׳]** מ״ט כל דבר של תקלה אסור לעשות דכתיב ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול איבעיא להו ירך שנתבשל בה גיד הנשה מהו לשלחו לעובד כוכבים. אבר מן החי לא מבעי לך דאמר מר בני נח מצווין על (הסירוס) [אבר מן החי] וקא עבר משום ולפני עור לא תתן מכשול. אבל הכא לא או דילמא לא שנא. ת״ש שולח [אדם] ירך לנכרי שגיד הנשה עמה:


BARAITHA. A man should not send to his fellow a cask of water⁵⁰ as oil.
GEMARA. What is the reason? It is forbidden to do anything which may give him offence; as it is written, *Nor put a stumbling-block before the blind*.⁵¹ The question was asked: May one send to a Gentile a thigh which has been cooked with the sinew?⁵² It is obvious that [one may not send to a Gentile] a limb cut from a living animal, for the master said:⁵³ The sons of Noah⁵⁴ were forbidden to eat a limb cut from a living animal; therefore [one who sent a Gentile meat with the sinew of the thigh would commit an offence] because of *Nor put a stumbling-block before the blind*. But here [with the sinew of the thigh] they were not [forbidden and a violation of the law would not arise]; or perhaps there is a difference between the two cases! Come and hear:¹) Ḥul. 93b (Sonc. ed., p. 525). A man may send to a Gentile a thigh wherein is the sinew.

footnotes:
⁵⁰ Instead of water it would be better to read ‘wine’ as in Ḥul. 94a (Sonc. ed., p. 528). There the story is related of a tragedy which followed as the consequence of such an act of deception.
⁵¹ Lev. 19, 14.
⁵² Contrary to the Law of Gen. 32, 33.
⁵³ Sanh. 56a (Sonc. ed., pp. 381f.). This is one of the seven Noachian laws.
⁵⁴ i.e. non-Jews.
¹ (54a


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:6)


**ברייתא** לא יאמר אדם לחבירו טול שמן מפך ריקן **[גמ']** גונב דעת הבריות כגונב דעת המקום שהרי אמרה תורה על הגזלן לשלם בראשו ועל הגנב פי שנים בכלים ותשלומי ד׳ בצאן וחמשה בבקר מ״ט דחש רחמנא אטרחיה:


BARAITHA.⁵⁵ 94a (Sonc. ed., p. 527). A man may not say to his fellow, ‘Take oil from the jar when it is [in fact] empty’.
GEMARA. He who steals the mind⁵⁶, pp. 58f. of his fellow is as though he deceived the All-present, because the Torah decreed that the robber must pay in full⁵⁷ for the theft, but the thief must pay twofold in the case of articles, fourfold in the case of sheep, but fivefold in the case of cattle.⁵⁸ XXI. 37. The thief had to carry the sheep off on his shoulders but he could ride on the ox. Cf. B.Ḳ. 79b (Sonc. ed., p. 452). Why [the difference]? Because the All-merciful showed consideration [to the thief for his trouble].

footnotes:
⁵⁵ Cf. ibid.
⁵⁶ Crafty deception, cf. I. Epstein, The Jewish Way of Life
⁵⁷ Ex. 22, 2.
⁵⁸ ibid.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:7)


**ברייתא** לא יאכל אדם עד ארבע שעות ולא ישתה עד ארבע שעות: **[גמ׳]** איני והא אמר ליה רבא לרבה בר מרי מנא הא דאמרי אינשי שיתין רהוטי רהוט ולא דוריה לגברא דמצפרא כרך ואמור רבנן השכם ואכול בקיץ מפני החמה ובחורף מפני הצנה. התם דפת שחרית הכא במאי עסקינן באכילה מרובה רוחץ אדם לארבע שעות לא צריך:


BARAITHA. A man should not eat [his breakfast] until four hours [of the day],⁵⁹ or drink until four hours.
GEMARA. But it is not so! Did not Raba say to Rabbah b. Mari:⁶⁰ Whence can the popular saying be derived, ‘Sixty runners may pursue him who has an early meal in the morning and will not overtake him’? And the Rabbis said: Have early breakfast in the summer because of the heat and in winter because of the cold! There it speaks of the morning meal [which is light], but here it deals with a heavy meal.
BARAITHA. A man should bathe at⁶¹ four hours.
GEMARA. This is an unnecessary statement.⁶²

footnotes:
⁵⁹ i.e. ten o’clock. The day began at 6 a.m. Cf. Shab. 10a (Sonc. ed., p. 36).
⁶⁰ B.Ḳ. 92b (Sonc. ed., p. 534).
⁶¹ H reads ‘until after four hours’. Cf. DER, p. 560f.
⁶² This is either a gloss or a printer’s error.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:8)


**ברייתא** מזגו לו את הכוס ישהה וישתהו וכמה ישהה בחמין ג' פעמים ובצונן ארבעה כדי ארבעה כוסות שנתנו לו. והא ארבעה קאמר ההוא לחמין. הנכנס לבית המרחץ כיצד יעשה אומר יהי רצון מלפניך ה׳ אלהי שתכניסני לשלום ותוציאני לשלום ותצילני מזו ומכיוצא בו לעתיד לבא ולא יארע בי קלקלה ואם יארע בי תהא מיתתי כפרתי על כל עונותי. קודם שיכנס מאחר שיתפלל פושט חלוקו ומתיר חגורו ומסלק את כובעו ואח״כ מסלק פרסקו התחתונה וכן לענין תפילין מסלק זה של ראש ואח״כ של יד שמעת מינה כובע לית בה משום קדושה וה״מ כובע אבל סודרא לא דכתיב סוד ה׳ ליריאיו מ״ט לא קתני מברך יהי רצון מלפניך ה׳ אלהי שתעלני מזו ומכיוצא בו לעתיד לבא ולכשיצא אומר מודה אני לפניך רבון העולמים שהצלתני משקיעת מים ומשריפת אש יהי רצון מלפניך ה׳ שתצילני מדומה לזו לעתיד לבא. מידי דדרך ארץ קתני דברכות לא קתני אלא הא דתנן לסוף פרקא הנכנס לבית הכסא אומר התכבדו ואמאי התם לאו ברכה היא דאמר מר היה מתעטף בטלית המצוייצת מניחו בקרן זוית ואינו צריך לומר אשר יצר למה לי איידי דתאנו הא תני הא:


BARAITHA. When his cup is filled,⁶³ he should pause in drinking it.⁶⁴ How many [pauses]? If [it is mixed] with warm water, he should pause three times; if with cold, four times, so that [it is equivalent to] his having been given four cups.
GEMARA. But it says four!⁶⁵ This refers to when the cup is mixed with warm water.⁶⁶
BARAITHA. When about to enter the bath-house how should a man act? He says,⁶⁷, p. 92. ‘May it be Thy will, O Lord my God, that Thou bring me in in peace and bring me out in peace. Do Thou save me from this and similar [dangers] in the future and may no mishap befall me; and if it does, may my death be an atonement for all my sins’. Before entering and after he has recited the prayer, he takes off his shirt, loosens his girdle, removes his hat and then slips off his undergarment. It is similar with the [removal of the] *tefillin:* first he removes the phylactery of the head and then the phylactery of the hand.⁶⁸
GEMARA. From this you may deduce that there is no sanctity attached to the hat.⁶⁹ This applies only to the hat but not to the turban,⁷⁰, i.e. *sudarium*, the distinctive headgear of Rabbinical scholars. Cf. Ḳid. 8a (Sonc. ed., p. 29, n. 5); Shab. 77b (Sonc. ed., p. 368) and S. Krauss, *Talmudische Archäologie*, I, pp. 166f. as it is written, *The counsel* [*sod*] *of the Lord is with them that fear Him* [*yere’aw*].⁷¹ to be a hybrid made up of *sod yere’aw*.
Why does the Baraitha use the verb ‘says’ and not ‘makes the benediction’:⁷² ‘May it be Thy will, O Lord my God, to deliver me from this and similar [dangers] in the future’; and when leaving he says, ‘Lord of the universe! I thank Thee for that Thou hast delivered me from sinking in the water⁷³ and from being burnt by fire.⁷⁴ May it be Thy will to deliver me from anything similar in the future’? [The Baraitha] is concerned with right conduct⁷⁵ and not with the benedictions [to be recited]. But what about the following which is learnt at the end of the chapter:⁷⁶ One who enters a privy says, “Be honoured [ye honoured and holy beings who minister to the Most High! Give glory to our God, remain in your place, be mindful, help me, guard me, wait for me until I shall have entered and left; for what I am doing is the way of men”]’? There it is not a case of a ‘benediction’, for the master said:⁷⁷ If he wrapped himself in a *ṭallith* with fringes attached, he leaves it in the corner and he has no need to recite a prayer. Why, then, [does it continue with: One who leaves a privy says,] ‘Blessed be … Who hast formed man in wisdom’?⁷⁸ While it deals with the one, it also [takes the opportunity] to deal with the other.

footnotes:
⁶³ lit. ‘mixed’, i.e. with water.
⁶⁴ He should not drink it in one draught; cf. Beẓah 25b (Sonc. ed., p. 130); Pes. 86b (Sonc. ed., p. 456).
⁶⁵ The question i: directed against the last words of the Baraitha. The assumption was that this clause is to be taken in connection with the one immediately before it: ‘If with cold, four times’. If there are four pauses, that would necessitate five draughts.
⁶⁶ In this case there are three pauses, making four draughts.
⁶⁷ Cf. DER X, p. 560. On the bath-house, cf. J. Rabbino-witz, Mishnah Megillah
⁶⁸ Men. 36a (Sonc. ed., p. 224).
⁶⁹ Seeing that the hat is not removed last.
⁷⁰ Sudra’
⁷¹ Ps. 25, 14, taking the word sudra’
⁷² The assumption is that ‘says’ implies a general meditation while ‘makes a benediction’ indicates a specific prayer in the form of a benediction. The reading in Tosiftha Ber. VII, 17, is ‘prays’, which is more appropriate.
⁷³ Drowning in the bath.
⁷⁴ Scalded by the vapour.
⁷⁵ i.e. expressing one’s sense of dependence on God.
⁷⁶ What follows does not occur in this tractate but is found in DER XI, p. 566.
⁷⁷ What follows is not found in the Talmudic sources.
⁷⁸ For the full form of the prayer, cf. P.B., p. 4.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:9)


**ברייתא** הנכנס לבית המרחץ אין מתעמל ואין מתגרד על השיש (ואין משתבר): **[גמ׳]** מאי מתעמל כגון האי דכיף רישיה ביני ברכיה. ואין מתגרד איני והא שמעיה דרבא הוה מגרד ליה כי אמרי׳ ביד:


BARAITHA. One who enters the bath-house should not exercise himself,⁷⁹ or scrape himself on the marble [slab], or have his limbs broken.⁸⁰
GEMARA. What is the meaning of ‘exercise himself’? For example, pressing his head between his knees. ‘Or scrape himself’: but it is not so! For [we are informed that] the servant of Raba scraped him! It speaks of scraping with the hand. ‘Or have his limbs broken’; Rabban Gamaliel said: Whoever has his limbs broken on the marble is the companion of an ass.⁸¹ [*garem*] *ass* (Gen. 49, 14) and homiletically read the word as גרום, ‘with bones broken’. Hence the association of ‘the breaking of the bones’ with the ass.

footnotes:
⁷⁹ Have massage. In V this clause is attached to the next Baraitha but is more appropriate here.
⁸⁰ A form of massage; cf. DER X, p. 560f. All these forms of exercise should not be undertaken in the public bath-house out of modesty.
⁸¹ Rabban Gamaliel must have had in mind the phrase a large-boned


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:10)


**ברייתא** ואין משתבר אמר ר״ג כל המשתבר על השיש חברו של חמור. בית המרחץ נותן מקום זה שהוא נכנס לזה שהוא יוצא לא ישאל אדם שלום לחברו בבית המרחץ ואם ישאל לו יאמר לו בית המרחץ הוא. האוכל בשוק חברו של כלב: **[גמ']** וה״מ בנהמא ומידי דרעבתנותא אבל מידי אחרינא לא:


BARAITHA. In the bath-house, one who enters gives way to the one who is leaving.⁸² A man should not greet his friend in the bath-house,⁸³ and if he greets him first he should say to him, ‘This is a bath-house’. One who eats in the street is the companion of a dog.⁸⁴
GEMARA. This applies to bread and foods which [are eaten to satisfy] one’s hunger, but not to other things.

footnotes:
⁸² Cf. j.B.Ḳ. III, 5, 3d: ‘One who enters a bath-house should show honour to him who leaves’.
⁸³ Cf. Shab. 10b (Sonc. ed., p. 37); Tosiftha Ber. II, 20.
⁸⁴ Ḳid. 40b (Sonc. ed., p. 203).


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:11)


**ברייתא** לא יניח אדם שמן בזכוכית מפני הסכנה: **[גמ']** מ״ט דילמא מיתבר ומסתכני ברייתא כדשמואל דאמר שמואל רחץ ולא סך ס״ד אימא לא סך מעיקרא :


BARAITHA. A man should not leave oil⁸⁵ in a glass because of danger.
GEMARA. What [danger] is there? Lest it be broken and endanger [the bathers]. As Samuel said:⁸⁶ If one bathes without anointing [he is like water poured over a barrel].⁸⁷ Say,⁸⁸ ‘And has not anointed himself previously’.

footnotes:
⁸⁵ The oil was used by the bathers to remove the sweat and dirt from the body.
⁸⁶ Cf. Shab. 41a (Sonc. ed., p. 191).
⁸⁷ The water pours around it but does not enter the barrel.
⁸⁸ Since a man does not bathe without anointing his body, read Samuel’s dictum in the following sense.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:12)


**ברייתא** ובכל מקום לא ירוק אדם בפני חברו ולא יניח רגלו על שפת האמבט ויהא קופץ בתוכו מפני שהוא דרך המיתה. הקורא שמע שני פעמים הרי זה מגונה. והטובל שני פעמים הרי זה מגונה דילמא דייב על אינשי ולא חזי ליה רחץ בחמין ולא נשתטף בצונן הרי זה גוזל את הרבים: **[גמ׳]** היכי דמי כגון דעייל לבני בני ומייתי ליה מחמימי ומשתטף ונפיק דהא קא גזל להו. ותיפוק לי דלא סליק ליה בדחמים לנפשיה בביתא אי נמי בדסמיך לנהרא:


BARAITHA. A man should not spit anywhere in front of his fellow or put his foot on the bath and jump into it, because it may lead to death. He who recites the *Shema‘*⁸⁹ twice is reprehensible. So, too, is he reprehensible who immerses twice.⁹⁰
GEMARA. Lest [the water from his head and beard] drip on to people without their noticing it.⁹¹
BARAITHA. If one bathes in hot water and does not slush himself with cold water he robs the public.
GEMARA. How is this? For example, he entered the bath and they brought him warm water, and he slushed himself with it and then went out; in such a case he has robbed the public!⁹² But should this not be excluded [from the category of robbery] seeing that his bathing is not beneficial to him?⁹³ He warms himself at home; or [the bath-house] is near a river.⁹⁴

footnotes:
⁸⁹ He is suspected of the heresy of believing in the existence of two Supreme Powers; cf. Ber. 33b (Sonc. ed., p. 210).
⁹⁰ One immersion immediately after the first.
⁹¹ After his first immersion they will avoid him to escape the drippings but not after the second. H reads דייק (for דייב), ‘press against’; cf. Y.D. CCI, §62.
⁹² By his using hot water for the shower, there will be less hot water for the other bathers.
⁹³ Cf. Shab. 41a (Sonc. ed., p. 191): ‘If one bathes in hot water and does not have a cold shower, he is like iron put into the fire but not into cold water’, to temper it.
⁹⁴ In which he can dip to cool himself.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:13)


**ברייתא** והגוזל את הרבים מה יעשה ילך ויחפור בורות שיחין ומערות ויתקן את הדרכים ואת האסטרטיות ונמחל לו: **[גמ׳]** מני ר׳ עקיבא היא דאמר לא זה הדרך מוציאתו מידי עבירה עד שישלם גזילה לכל אחד ואחד אפי׳ תימא ר׳ (שמעון) [טרפון] דהא מתנח קמייהו:


BARAITHA. If one has robbed the public, what should he do [to atone for his sin]?⁹⁵ He should dig wells, ditches and grottoes, or repair roads and streets; then he will be pardoned.⁹⁶
GEMARA. In accordance with whose view [is this Baraitha]? R. ‘Aḳiba’s, who said:⁹⁷ This is not the way that would absolve him from sin unless he pays [the full amount of the robbery] to each person. You might even say that it is in accordance with the view of R. Ṭarfon, because here [the amount] lies before them.⁹⁸

footnotes:
⁹⁵ Seeing that he does not know to whom to make restitution.
⁹⁶ His work for the welfare of the community is a form of restitution. Cf. Beẓah 29a (Sonc. ed., p. 150); B.Ḳ. 94b (Sonc. ed., p. 550).
⁹⁷ Cf. Yeb. 118b (Sonc. ed., p. 835). The case is where a man robbed one of five persons and does not know which was his victim, each declaring, ‘He robbed me’. There is a dispute between R. ‘Aḳiba and R. Ṭarfon. According to the former he has to leave the full amount of the robbery with every one of the persons involved; but R. Ṭarfon holds the view that he has to leave the amount of the robbery with the five claimants and withdraw.
⁹⁸ Every one of them can make use of the public facilities which the robber provided.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:14)


**ברייתא** כותבי ספרים תפילין ומזוזות הם ותגריהן ותגרי תגריהן אינם רואים סימן ברכה: **[גמ׳]** תוספתא סוף בכורים כותבי ספרים משום מחסרין ומשום מיתרין. תנן התם האומר אין תפילין לעבור על דברי תורה פטור חמש טוטפות להוסיף על דברי חכמים חייב מני ר׳ שמעון היא דאמר כי טובים דודיך מיין והכא נמי כיון דעקר לכוליה מילתא או לכוליה קרא מתרבש וכיון דעקר ליה לתלויה אי נמי לתגא מתרבש: ת״ר כותבי ספרים והמתורגמין ומעות הבאות ממדינת הים והחזנין אין רואין סימן ברכה לעולם. כותבי ספרים מאן נינהו ארבעה ועשרים ספרא דלא בדיק. והמתורגמין משום דנטלי שכר שבת. מעות הבאות ממדינת הים משום דמתרחיש בהו ניסא. והחזנין משום מלאכת ה׳. תנא כותבי ספרים תפילין ומזוזות אינם רואין סימן ברכה ואי עסוקין לשמה רואין:


BARAITHA.⁹⁹ As for them who write [Torah] scrolls *tefillin* and *mezuzoth*, they, their traders and their traders’ traders¹⁰⁰ do not see a sign of blessing.
GEMARA. ‘As for them who write scrolls’:¹⁰¹ because they may omit or add a letter.¹⁰²
We have learnt there:¹⁰³ If one says, ‘There is no precept of *tefillin* so that a Biblical law may be transgressed’, he is exempt [from punishment].¹⁰⁴. [But if he rules that the phylactery of the head must consist of] five compartments, thus adding to the words of the Sages, he is liable.¹⁰⁵ According to whom is this? It is according to R. Simeon who said: [It is written,] *For thy love is better than wine*:¹⁰⁶ is plural and interpreted by R. Simeon in the sense of ‘beloved men’, i.e. the scribes and scholars who are beloved of God. [these are the scribes]. Accordingly when the man¹⁰⁷. uproots a whole [commandment of the Torah] or a whole verse, he is not liable;¹⁰⁸ but where he uproots the law concerning a suspended letter¹⁰⁹ or crownlets on letters¹¹⁰ he is liable.¹¹¹
The Rabbis have taught:¹¹² The [earnings of] writers of scrolls, [the wages of] interpreters,¹¹³ money which comes from countries overseas,¹¹⁴ and [the payment of] *ḥazzanim*¹¹⁵ never see a sign of blessing. ‘The [earnings of] writers of scrolls’: what are these scrolls? The twenty-four books¹¹⁶, pp. 6ff. if not examined. ‘Interpreters’: because they receive pay for work on the Sabbath. ‘Money which comes from countries overseas’: because a miracle happened.¹¹⁷ ‘And [the payment of] *ḥazzanim’*: Because [they are engaged] in the work of the Lord. It has been taught:¹¹⁸ They who write scrolls, *tefillin* and *mezuzoth* do not see a sign of blessing; but if they engage [in this task] for its own sake,¹¹⁹ they do see [a sign of blessing].

footnotes:
⁹⁹ Pes. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 246).
¹⁰⁰ i.e. all who trade with them directly or indirectly.
¹⁰¹ V inserts: ‘Tosiftha, end of tractate Bikkurim’, a marginal note which was included in the text.
¹⁰² Cf. ‘Erub. 13a (Sonc. ed., p. 81), R. Ishmael’s injunction to R. Meir, who was a scribe, ‘Be meticulous in your work, because your occupation is sacred; should you perchance omit or add one letter, you would thereby destroy all the universe’.
¹⁰³ Sanh. 88b (Sonc. ed., p. 587).
¹⁰⁴ Since all people know that the Torah commands the donning of tefillin
¹⁰⁵ Because not everyone is aware of the rule that it must have four compartments.
¹⁰⁶ Cant. 1, 2. In the Heb. the word for love
¹⁰⁷ Who declared that there was no precept of tefillin
¹⁰⁸ This is the reading of H; the word in V is corrupt.
¹⁰⁹ Certain words in the Heb. text have a letter suspended above the line; cf. ARN, p. 164.
¹¹⁰ Cf. Men. 29b (Sonc. ed., p. 190): ‘Raba said: Seven letters in the Torah require each three crownlets’.
¹¹¹ Cf. j.Ber. I, 4, 3b: ‘The words of the scribes … are dearer than the words of the Torah’.
¹¹² For the parallels to these passages, cf. Pes. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 245).
¹¹³ Officials who delivered the Sabbath lecture to the congregation. The Rabbi whispered his statements to the interpreter, who explained them to the people. The term may also denote those who translated the reading of the Torah in the service into Aramaic for the understanding of the congregation.
¹¹⁴ Danger was involved in the transport of goods by sea and there was the risk of loss.
¹¹⁵ Functionaries who combined the offices of supervisor of children’s studies in the Synagogue, beadle, court crier and janitor. Cf. Shab. 11a (Sonc. ed., p. 41, n. 7).
¹¹⁶ On the number of the books of the Bible, cf. L. Blau, Zur Einleitung in die Heilige Schrift
¹¹⁷ And miracles do not happen every day; Pes. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 240).
¹¹⁸ Pes. loc. cit.
¹¹⁹ i.e. their aim is to be of service to the community, profit being a secondary consideration.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:15)


**ברייתא** המצפה לשכר חמורו ולשכר אשתו אינו רואה סימן ברכה **[גמ׳]** מ״ט דכתיב יודע צדיק נפש בהמתו בהמה [אינה] יודעת נפש צדיק. שכר אשתו דכתיב ללחמך ללחם ביתך למדה תורה [ד״א] שיהא לחמך קודם ללחם ביתך ואח״כ לנערותיך. אמר רבא כל הכופה אשתו ובני ביתו למלאכה יצר הרע מסתלק מהם שנאמר נסו ואין רודף רשע וצדיקים ככפיר יבטח אתיא כדתנן ר׳ שמעון [ב"ג] אומר המדיר אשתו מלעשות מלאכה יוציא ויתן כתובה לפי שהבטלה מביאה לידי שיעמום:


BARAITHA. He who looks to the earnings of his ass or to the earnings of his wife¹²⁰ (Sonc. ed., p. 245). does not see a sign of blessing.
GEMARA. What is the reason? Because it is written, *A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast:*¹²¹ a beast does regard the life of a righteous man. ‘The earnings of his wife’: for it is written, [*And there will be goat’s milk enough*] *for thy food, for the food of thy household; and maintenance for thy maidens*.¹²² XXVII, 27. The Torah teaches that your food comes before the food of your household,¹²³ and then comes the food of your maidens. Raba said: Whoever compels his wife or his household to work, the evil inclination departs from them;¹²⁴ as it is stated, *The wicked flee when no man pursueth; but the righteous are secure as a young lion*.¹²⁵ This conforms to what we learnt:¹²⁶ Rabban Simeon b. Gamaliel said: If a man forbade his wife under a vow to do any work, he must divorce her and give her her *kethubah*, because idleness leads to idiocy.

footnotes:
¹²⁰ Pes. loc. cit.
¹²¹ Prov. 12, 10.
¹²² ibid.
¹²³ In Rabbinic phraseology the Biblical term ‘house’ is equated with one’s wife; cf. Yoma 2a (Sonc. ed., p. 1).
¹²⁴ Being fully occupied, they will have no time to indulge in wrong.
¹²⁵ Prov. 28, 1.
¹²⁶ Keth. 59b (Sonc. ed., p. 353).


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:16)


**ברייתא** המשתכר בקנים ובקנקנים אינו רואה סימן ברכה לעולם: **[גמ']** משום דשלטא בהו עינא הלכתא בשמן ולא ביין:


BARAITHA.¹²⁷ He who trades in canes and jars will never see a sign of blessing.
GEMARA. Because [their bulk being large] the [evil] eye has power over them. Therefore¹²⁸ instead of V’s *hilketha’*. this applies only to [jars of] oil but not of wine.¹²⁹

footnotes:
¹²⁷ Pes. 50b (Sonc. ed., p. 245).
¹²⁸ Reading with H hilkak
¹²⁹ Presumably jars of wine were smaller than jars of oil.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:17)


**ברייתא** פעם אחת היה ר״ע יושב ודורש (על שולחנו מפני הסכנה) תחת הזית ואמר מגדלי בהמה דקה ומקצצי אילנות טובים ומלמדי תינוקות שאין עושין מלאכה לאמיתן אינם רואים סימן ברכה: **[גמ׳]** איני והא אמר ר׳ חנינא אם היה מעולה בדמים מותר. התם בשאר אילנות הכא בזית דיקא נמי דקתני היה יושב תחת הזית מ״ט משום דברכתא נפיש ואתא איהו וקצצה. אימא רישא מגדלי בהמה דקה ואי משום ברכה אמאי אין רואין שוחטי איתמר:


BARAITHA.¹³⁰ Once R. ‘Aḳiba was sitting and expounding beneath an olive-tree and said: They who breed small cattle,¹³¹ they who cut down beautiful trees,¹³² and they who teach young children but do not do their work conscientiously will not see a sign of blessing.
GEMARA. But it is not so! For R. Ḥanina said:¹³³ If the value [of the tree for other purposes] exceeds that [of its fruit] it is permissible [to cut it down]. There¹³⁴ it speaks of other kinds of trees and here of olive-trees. Deduce this from what [the Baraitha] teaches, ‘He was sitting beneath an olive-tree’. Why [an olive-tree]? Because the blessing [which it provides] is great and yet the man comes and cuts it down! [I quote against that reasoning] the first clause, ‘They who breed small cattle’! If it is because they are a blessing, why do they not see [a sign of blessing]? The text should read, ‘They who slaughter [small cattle]’.

footnotes:
¹³⁰ Pes. loc. cit.
¹³¹ e.g. sheep and goats.
¹³² To dispose of them for timber.
¹³³ B.Ḳ. 91b-92a (Sonc. ed., p. 530).
¹³⁴ In the statement of R. Ḥanina.


###### Tractate Kallah Rabbati 10:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kallah%20Rabbati/r/10:18)


**ברייתא** התיר מנעלו ויצא לשוק הרי זה מגסי הרוח: **[גמ׳]** אלא מאי ליעבד ה״ק נפל מנעלו כשיצא לשוק הרי זה מגסי הרוח. אמר רבא גס רוח אסור להכניסו בבית דאמרי רבנן כל אדם שיש בו גסות הרוח נכשל באשת איש דכתיב תועבת ה׳ כל גבה לב ואפילו גדול בתורה כמשה רבינו לא ינקה מדינה של גיהנם וכל מי שדעתו שפלה הקב״ה מצילו מן הפורענות שבעולם שנאמר [כי] כה אמר רם ונשא שוכן עד וקדוש שמו מרום וקדוש אשכון ואת דכא ושפל רוח להחיות רוח שפלים ולהחיות לב נדכאים:


BARAITHA.¹³⁵ If he loosened his shoe and went out into the street he is regarded as haughty.
GEMARA. What is he to do? This is what it means to say: If he put on¹³⁶ V has *nafal*, ‘fell off’. his shoe when he went out into the street he is regarded as haughty. Raba said: It is forbidden to bring a haughty man into one’s house; for the Rabbis said:¹³⁷ Any man in whom is haughtiness of spirit will in the end stumble through an [unfaithful] married woman, as it is stated, *Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord*.¹³⁸ Even if he be learned in the Torah like Moses our teacher, he will not be free from the judgment of Gehinnom. As for everyone who is lowly of spirit, the Holy One, blessed be He, will save him from [evil] visitations that come upon the world; as it is stated, *For thus saith the High and Lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is holy: I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones*¹³⁹ [55*b*].

footnotes:
¹³⁵ Cf. DER XI, p. 565. The reading in the Baraitha must have been originally ‘if his shoe fell off and he went out’. Hence the point of the question in the Gemara: ‘What is he to do?’ His haughtiness is displayed in his desire to be different from others.
¹³⁶ Reading with H na‘al;
¹³⁷ Soṭah 4b (Sonc. ed., p. 16).
¹³⁸ Prov. 16, 5.
¹³⁹ Isa. 57, 15.

# Tractate Kutim

מסכת כותים

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim)

מעמדם הדתי של השומרונים והקשרים האסורים והמותרים עימם.

The religious status of Samaritans, permitted and prohibited interactions with them.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 21, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 21)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Kutim 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:1)


דרכי כותים פעמים כעובדי כוכבים פעמים כישראל ורובן כישראל.


The Samaritans in some of their ways resemble the Gentiles and in some resemble Israel, but in the majority they resemble Israel.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:2)


אין מביאין מהן לא קיני זבין ולא קיני זבות ולא קיני יולדות ולא חטאות ולא אשמות אבל מקבלין מידן


We do not accept from them for offering [in the Temple] sacrificial birds brought by males with a flux,¹ or sacrificial birds brought by females with a flux,² 29. or sacrificial birds brought by women after childbirth,³ XII, 6, 8. or sin-offerings or trespass-offerings, but we receive from them vows and free-will-offerings.⁴

footnotes:
¹ Lev. 15, 14.
² ibid.
³ ibid.
⁴ The words ‘vows and free-will offerings’ have dropped out of the printed text and MS.K., but are added by H in agreement with Shek. I, 5 (Sonc. ed., p. 3).


###### Tractate Kutim 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:3)


אין מקנין אותם במחובר לקרקע ולא מוכרין להם רחלים לגוז ולא תבואה לקצור ולא עצים מחוברים לקרקע אלא מה שישחוט.


We do not transfer to them anything attached to the soil,⁵ or sell to them sheep to shear, or crops to reap⁶ or trees attached to the soil,⁷ but we sell them animals to slaughter.

footnotes:
⁵ Lest they should transfer it to Gentiles to whom such ownership is forbidden. [In ‘A.Z. 20b (Sonc. ed., p. 107) this rule is stated in connection with Gentiles. As with several other rulings which follow it was subsequently applied to Samaritans.]
⁶ The correct reading is probably ‘unripe produce (for cattle food) to clip’.
⁷ The words ‘to be cut down’ should certainly be inserted.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:4)


אין מוכרין להם בהמה גסה ואף על פי שהיא שבורה ולא סייחים ולא עגלים. אבל מוכרין להם שבורה שאינה יכולה להתרפאות.


We do not sell them large cattle even if they are mutilated, or foals or calves;⁸ but we may sell them a mutilated animal which can never recover.⁹

footnotes:
⁸ [From the fear that the owner will not allow them to rest on the Sabbath; cf. ‘A.Z. 15a (Sonc. ed., p. 75).]
⁹ [Because it will not be put to work and so the fear, previously stated, does not apply.]


###### Tractate Kutim 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:5)


אין מוכרין להם כלי זיין ולא כל דבר שיש בו נזק לרבים.


We do not sell them weapons of war or anything which can cause injury to the public.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:6)


אין משיאין אותם ולא נושאים מהם נשים אבל מלוין ולוין מהם ברבית.


We do not give to them [Israelite women] in marriage or take wives from them,¹⁰ but we lend to them and borrow from them on interest.¹¹

footnotes:
¹⁰ [For the reason, cf. below II, 7, n. 13.]
¹¹ [Either the text should be emended to ‘and we do not lend to them’, etc., or the clause is a later insertion at the time of the final repudiation of the Samaritans. Cf. Kirchheim ad loc.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:7)


נותנים להם לקט שכחה ופאה ויש להם שכחה ופאה והם נאמנים על הלקט ועל השכחה ועל הפאה בשעתן ועל מעשר עני בשעתו ופירותיהן טבל כפירות עובדי כוכבים ואוסרין את העירוב כעובדי עבודת כוכבים.


We give them gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field;¹² I, 3, n. 7. they too observe [gleanings], forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field,¹³ and their word can be taken in regard to gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field in their season and in regard to the tithe of the poor in its year.¹⁴ Their produce is reckoned as *ṭebel*¹⁵ like the produce of Gentiles, and they make the *‘erub* ineffective like Gentiles.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹² Cf. Gerim
¹³ And therefore no tithe need be given for them.
¹⁴ The tithe of produce was given to the poor in the third and sixth year of the seven-year cycle.
¹⁵ i.e. produce from which the heave-offering and tithe have not been separated.
¹⁶ Cf. ‘Erub. 61b (Sonc. ed., p. 433, n. 1).


###### Tractate Kutim 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:8)


בת ישראל אינה מילדת את הכותית ולא מניקה את בנה אבל הכותית מילדת בת ישראל ומניקה את בנה ברשותה.


An Israelite woman should not act as midwife to a Samaritan woman or suckle her child;¹⁷ but a Samaritan woman can act as midwife to an Israelite woman and suckle her child on her premises.

footnotes:
¹⁷ [Based on Mishnah ‘A.Z. II, 2 (Sonc. ed., p. 129) where it speaks of ‘a heathen woman’ and the reason given is ‘because she would be delivering a child to idolatry’. Since the Tosiftha ‘A.Z. III permits it in the case of a Samaritan, the text here is probably a later adaptation and] originally read ‘may act as midwife … and suckle’.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:9)


ישראל מוהל את הכותי והכותי מוהל את ישראל ר׳ יהודה אומר כותי לא ימול את ישראל שאינו מוהלו אלא לשם הר גריזים.


An Israelite may circumcise a Samaritan and a Samaritan can circumcise an Israelite. R. Judah said: A Samaritan may not circumcise an Israelite because he only circumcises him in the name of Mount Gerizim.¹⁸, pp. 170f.).]

footnotes:
¹⁸ The mountain sacred to the Samaritans as the Temple Mount in Jerusalem was to the Jews. [The phrase ‘seems to mean simply, “with the intention of attaching the person to the community of Gerizim” ’ (Montgomery, The Samaritans


###### Tractate Kutim 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:10)


מעמידין בהמה בפונדק כותי ושוכר כותי שילך אחר בהמתו. ומוסר בהמתו לרועה כותי ומוסר את בנו שילמדנו כותי אומנות ומתיחדים ומספרים עמהם בכל מקום משא״כ בעובדי כוכבים.


We may stall an animal in the inn of a Samaritan, and [an Israelite] may hire a Samaritan to follow his beast. He may also entrust his cattle to a Samaritan shepherd,¹⁹ and he may entrust his son to a Samaritan to teach him a trade.²⁰ We may associate with them and converse²¹ with them in any place, which is not so with Gentiles.²²

footnotes:
¹⁹ [Because a Samaritan is not suspected of perverted practices with an animal. Cf. ‘A.Z. 15b (Sonc. ed., p. 78).]
²⁰ [We do not fear that he will influence the boy against Judaism.]
²¹ The correct reading according to Kirchheim is מסתפרין, ‘may have the hair cut by them’, instead of מספרין [in agreement with Mishnah ‘A.Z. II, 3 (Sonc. ed., p. 135).
²² Who are suspected of murderous intent.


###### Tractate Kutim 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:11)


חולץ ליבמתו ונותן גט לאשתו ונאמן הכותי להביא גט ממדינת הים לישראל.


He performs *ḥaliẓah* for his sister-in-law and gives a *geṭ* to his wife, and a Samaritan may be relied on to bring a *geṭ*²³. from foreign countries to Israel.

footnotes:
²³ i.e. his word is taken that he witnessed the signing and sealing of the geṭ


###### Tractate Kutim 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:12)


אלו דברים שאין מוכרין להם לא נבלות ולא טריפות ולא שקצים ולא רמשים. ולא סנדל של בהמה ולא שמן שנפל לתוכו עכבר ולא שליל אע״פ שישראל אוכלים אותו כוס כוס ושליל אין מוכרין להם מפני ממכר טעות. וכשם שאין מוכרין להם כך אין לוקחין מהם שנא׳ (דברים י״ד:ב׳) כי עם קדוש אתה לה׳ אלהיך


These are the things which we do not sell them: animals which died of themselves or have been improperly slaughtered, animals forbidden [to an Israelite] as food,²⁴ reptiles,²⁵ a shoe made from the skin of an animal which died of itself,²⁶ explains that the leather of an animal which died of itself is inferior to that of a healthy animal, and to sell shoes from this leather is false pretences. oil into which a mouse has fallen,²⁷ or [the flesh of] a *koskos*²⁸ or of an embryo. Although Israelites eat a *koskos* and an embryo we do not sell them to the Samaritans, because such a sale would be under false pretences. And just as we do not sell these to them so we do not buy these from them, as it is stated *For thou art a holy people unto the Lord thy God*²⁹—since thou art holy, thou must not make another people holier than thyself.³⁰

footnotes:
²⁴ Lest they should sell them to Israelites as fit for consumption.
²⁵ Lest they should mix them with things sold to Israelites.
²⁶ Cf. Ḥul. 94a (Sonc. ed., p. 528, n. 4): ‘The animal may have died through the bite of a serpent and the hide of the animal may thereby have become contaminated’. Rashi ad loc.
²⁷ [The oil would thereby become unclean, and in this matter the Samaritans were scrupulous.]
²⁸ ‘A כוס כוס’ is added by MS.K. and H. It is the term for an animal which has been hurriedly slaughtered because otherwise it would soon have died naturally.
²⁹ Deut. 14, 21.
³⁰ ‘Since thou art holy’, etc., is omitted in V. [Kirchheim explains that the underlying principle is that which is laid down in Pes. 50b-51a (Sonc. ed., p. 247): ‘Things which are permitted, yet others treat them as forbidden, you may not permit it in their presence’. It is there expressly applied to Samaritans.]


###### Tractate Kutim 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/1:13)


נאמן הכותי לומר אם קבר אם לא קבר ובבהמה אם בכרה או לא בכרה. נאמן הכותי על נטע רבעי ועל הערלה ועל הציונות אבל לא על הסככות ולא על הפרעות ולא על ארץ העמים ולא על בית הפרס מפני שנחשדו בהם. זה הכלל דבר שנחשדו בו אין נאמנין עליו:


A Samaritan may be trusted if he says that he has buried [a miscarriage] or not buried it,³¹ and, with regard to an animal, that it has brought forth its first-born³² or not brought forth. A Samaritan may be trusted with regard to the plantation of the fourth year and uncircumcised fruit³³ and grave-signs,³⁴ but not with regard to overhanging boughs, protruding stones,³⁵ land of the peoples,³⁶ or a *beth peras*,³⁷ because they are suspected [of carelessness] in these matters. The general principle is that in regard to matters in which they are suspected [of carelessness] they are not trusted.

footnotes:
³¹ [Cf. Nid. 56b (Sonc. ed., p. 397). If the foetus was buried in a room, any person entering it would be rendered ritually unclean.]
³² [Then the subsequent birth would not come under the law of the firstling, which was a priestly due.]
³³ Cf. Lev. 19, 23f.
³⁴ If he says that there is no grave in a place which is not marked.
³⁵ Which form a ‘tent’ for communicating ritual defilement. [Cf. Nid. Sonc. ed., p. 399, n. 2.]
³⁶ [i.e. countries outside the Holy Land in matters which concern ritual purity.]
³⁷ [Cf. Jast. p. 1233.]



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Kutim 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:1)


אין לוקחין בשר מטבח כותי אלא ממה שהוא אוכל ולא דקריות של צפורים אא״כ נתנם לתוך פיו לא שיתן הוא לישראל שכבר נחשדו שמאכילין את ישראל נבלות.


We do not buy meat from a Samaritan butcher except that of which he is prepared himself to eat, nor [do we buy from him] baskets of birds unless he first puts them in his mouth.¹ He must not give them to an Israelite to eat, since the Samaritans have from of old been suspected of giving Israelites carrion to eat.

footnotes:
¹ [Ḥul. 4a (Sonc. ed., p. 10) reads: ‘[The Israelite] cuts off the head of one of the birds and gives it to the Samaritan; if he ate it, then we may eat of his slaughtering’.]


###### Tractate Kutim 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:2)


שוה הכותי לישראל לכל נזיקין שבתורה ישראל שהרג את הכותי וכותי שהרג את ישראל שוגג גולה מזיד נהרג שור של ישראל שנגח שור של כותי פטור ושור של כותי שנגח שור של ישראל אם תם הוא משלם חצי נזק ואם מועד משלם נזק שלם [ר״מ אומר שור של כותי שנגח שור של ישראל בין תם בין מועד משלם נזק שלם] ומשלם מן העליה.


The Samaritan is on the same footing as an Israelite in regard to all damages mentioned in the Torah. Whether an Israelite kills a Samaritan or a Samaritan kills an Israelite, if he did it by inadvertence he goes into exile [to a City of Refuge], if wilfully he is put to death. If the ox of an Israelite gored the ox of a Samaritan he is exempt from damages;² but should the ox of a Samaritan have gored the ox of an Israelite, if the ox is *tam* he pays half the damage and if it is *mu‘ad*³ (warned) one which had done so and the owner had been warned. he pays the whole damage. R. Meir said: If an ox of a Samaritan gores the ox of an Israelite, whether it is *tam* or *mu‘ad* the owner pays the whole damage and pays from his best possessions.⁴

footnotes:
² i.e. if it was not known to have a tendency to be a gorer.
³ תם (innocuous) denotes an ox which had not previously gored, mu‘ad
⁴ [Cf. B.Ḳ. 38b (Sonc. ed., p. 217).]


###### Tractate Kutim 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:3)


הגבינים שלהם מותרות רשב״א אומר אם של בעלי בתים מותרות ואם של סיטונים אסורות השלקין והכבשין שלהם שדרכן לעשות בהן יין וחומץ אסורים


Their cheeses are permitted. R. Simeon b. Eleazar said: Those of private persons are permitted, but those of wholesalers⁵ are forbidden. Their cooked and preserved vegetables, into which they usually put wine or vinegar,⁶ I, 9, n. 18.] are forbidden.

footnotes:
⁵ H reads ‘those of the villages’. [The reason is that these cheeses are made for sale, and the makers are not particular to enclose them in skins of ritually clean animals.]
⁶ [Cf. Gerim


###### Tractate Kutim 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:4)


חולקים כהני ישראל וכהני כותים במקומם מפני שהם כמצילין מידם אבל לא במקום ישראל שלא יחזיקנו בכהונה. כהן כותי שהוא אוכל ומאכיל לישראל בטומאה מותר בטהרה אסור.


Israelite priests⁷ share with Samaritan priests in the latters’ districts because they, as it were, rescue [the produce] from their hands, but not in Israelite districts lest [Jews appear to] confirm their priesthood. If a Samaritan priest offers from what he is eating to an Israelite, should [the priest] be unclean it is permissible, but if clean it is forbidden.⁸, and therefore the Israelite may eat what he was eating.

footnotes:
⁷ About the time of Alexander the Great, the Samaritans built a temple on Mount Gerizim and a number of priests from Jerusalem, including a High Priest, went and ministered there. They were disowned by the Judeans.
⁸ The Samaritan priest, if unclean, would not eat terumah


###### Tractate Kutim 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:5)


אין לוקחים מנחתום כותי במוצאי פסח אלא לאחר ג׳ תנורים ולא מבעלי בתים אלא לאחר ג׳ שבתות ולא מן הכפרים אלא לאחר שלשה עסיות אימתי בזמן שלא עשו מצה עם ישראל או שהקדימו יום אחד אבל אם עשו מצה עם ישראל או שאחרו יום אחד חמצן מותר ור״ש אוסר לפי שאינם יודעים לשמור מצה כישראל.


We do not buy [bread] from a Samaritan baker on the outgoing of Passover until after three bakings [have been made], or from private persons until three weeks have passed, or from the villages until after three bakings.⁹] When does this apply? When they have not prepared their unleavened bread together with Israelites or they observed Passover one day earlier; but if they baked their unleavened bread together with Israelites or observed Passover one day later, their leaven is permitted. R. Simeon forbids it because they do not know how to observe the law of unleavened bread like the Israelites.

footnotes:
⁹ H reads ‘makings’ which has the same meaning as ‘bakings’. [As the continuation indicates, the ruling was made because the Samaritan Passover did not always coincide exactly with the Jewish Festival. Cf. Kirchheim ad loc.


###### Tractate Kutim 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:6)


בראשונה אמרו יינה של גדוד אסור מפני יינה של כפר חזרו לומר כ״מ שנחשדו המעורבים בעובדי כוכבים פתוחה אסורה סתומה מותרת רבי מאיר אומר כל יינם מותר חוץ מן הפתוחה שבשווקים וחכ״א פתוחה בכ״מ אסורה סתומה מותרת נקובה וסתומה כסתומה. הקנקנים שלהם חדשות מותרות וישנות אסורות.


At first they said: The wine of Gedor is forbidden on account of the wine of Kfar Paggasha.¹⁰ Later they revised this rule and said: Wherever [Samaritans] are suspected because of their mingling with Gentiles, if [their wine is] in an open [vessel] it is forbidden,¹¹ and if in a closed [vessel] it is permitted. R. Meir said: All their wine is permitted except that which is in open [vessels for sale] in the markets; but the Sages said: In an open [vessel] it is everywhere forbidden and in a closed [vessel] permitted, while [a vessel] which has been pierced and then sealed is like one which is sealed. Their jars when new are permitted but when old are forbidden.¹²

footnotes:
¹⁰ For Gedor there is a variant ‘Kador’ and for Paggasha (the text in V is corrupt) ‘Pansha’. Apparently Gedor was a Samaritan village and Kfar Paggasha a heathen village near by with whose inhabitants the Samaritans freely mingled. Hence the doubt about the wine.
¹¹ Because some of it may have been used in heathen worship.
¹² [Cf. ‘A.Z. 29b (Sonc. ed., p. 146); another instance of a law relating to Gentiles which was later applied to Samaritans. An old jar may have contained the wine of a heathen.]


###### Tractate Kutim 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:7)


מפני מה הכותים אסורים לבוא בישראל מפני שנתערבו עם כהני הבמות. רבי ישמעאל אומר גרי צדק היו מתחילתן מפני מה אסורים מפני הממזרות ושאינן מיבמים את הנשואה.


Why are Samaritans forbidden to enter the Jewish community? Because they have become mixed up with the priests of the high places. R. Ishmael said: They were originally genuine proselytes. Why, then, are they forbidden? Because of the illegitimate females¹³ and because they do not perform the levirate duty to a married woman.¹⁴ instead. Cf. I, 11.

footnotes:
¹³ [Since they are a mixed people, they include females who may not have been born to Israelite mothers and in turn their offspring are non-Israelite since their status in this respect depends upon that of the mother.]
¹⁴ But perform ḥaliẓah


###### Tractate Kutim 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Kutim/r/2:8)


מאימתי מקבלין אותם משכפרו בהר גריזים והודו בירושלים ובתחית המתים מכאן ואילך הגוזל את הכותי כגוזל את ישראל:


When may they be received into the Jewish community? When they have renounced Mount Gerizim and acknowledged Jerusalem and the resurrection of the dead.¹⁵ From then onwards one who robs a Samaritan is like one who robs an Israelite. [62*a*]

footnotes:
¹⁵ [That the Samaritans denied the doctrine of resurrection is recorded in Sanh. 90b (Sonc. ed., p. 606, n. 1).]

# Tractate Mezuzah

מסכת מזוזה

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah)

כתיבת פרשיות קריאת שמע על מגילת קלף וקביעת המגילה על מזוזת הדלת.

Writing the mezuzah, a scroll of parchment containing the Shema, and hanging it on the doorpost.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 23, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 23)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:1)


אין כותבין מזוזות לא על גבי עורות בהמה טמאה ולא על גבי עורות חיה טמאה אבל כותבין על עורות נבלות ועל עורות טרפות ואין חוששין שמא עורות לבובין הם


It is not permitted to write *mezuzoth* on the skins of ritually unclean cattle or on skins of ritually unclean wild animals. It is permitted, however, to write them on skins of *nebeloth* and *ṭerefoth*, and there is no need to consider the possibility of their having been pierced at the animal’s heart.¹

footnotes:
¹ There was a heathen practice to remove the heart from an animal while it was still alive and offer it as a sacrifice. Rabbinic law regards such an animal as an idolatrous offering (cf. Mishnah ‘A.Z. 29b, Sonc. ed., p. 145) and forbids its entire use, including the skin.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:2)


צריך להניח שיטה אחת לכל צד כדברי רשב״א


It is required to leave [a space of] one line on every side [of the text of the *mezuzah*], according to R. Simeon b. Eleazar.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:3)


נקבה במקום [הכתב פסולה במקום] הריוח כשרה עשא הווין זיינין זיינין ווין כפופים פשוטים פשוטים כפופים פתוחים סתומים סתומים פתותים או ששנה אותיותיה או שנכתבה עברית הרי זו פסולה


If a hole was made in the place of the script it is unfit for religious use; but if it occurred in the margin it remains fit.
If the letter *waw* [in a *mezuzah*] was shaped like a *zayin* or *vice versa*, curved letters like straight-lined letters² like the final *kaf.* or *vice versa*, open letters closed³ like the final *mem.* or *vice versa*, or if the shape of its letters had been altered [in any other way], or if it was written in [obsolete] Hebrew, it is unfit for religious use.

footnotes:
² e.g. an ordinary kaf
³ An ordinary mem


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:4)


בית התבן בית העצים בית האוצר הרי אלו פטורים רפת הבקר פטור אם היו הנשים נאותות בו חייב הצריפים והבורגנין והלקטיות והבורסקיות הרי אלו פטורים מן המזוזה


A magazine for straw, a wood-shed [and any] storage room are exempt [from the *mezuzah*].⁴ A stable for cattle is exempt, but if women make use of it⁵ it is liable. Cone-shaped huts,⁶, I, p. 6.] travellers’ stations, field sheds⁷, p. 226, and *Talm. Arch.* I, p. 276, n. 81, reads *hilaḳṭiyoth*. Maimonides understood the term to mean ‘summer-house’, thatched on top and open on the four sides. More probably it was used for stacking hay, etc., where it was dried by the wind.] and tanneries are exempt from *mezuzah*.⁸

footnotes:
⁴ Only dwelling-houses are subject to the obligation.
⁵ In which to adorn themselves; but if they use any of the structures for bathing it is exempt (cf. Yoma 11a, Sonc. ed., p. 48; Y.D. CCLXXXVI, §2).
⁶ [Used by watchers in a field or by hunters; Krauss, Talmudische Archäologie
⁷ [Krauss, Lehnwörter
⁸ They are not dwelling-houses.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:5)


בית המרחץ פטורה אם יש לה בית דירה פתח החיצון חייב


A bath-house is exempt, but if a dwelling-house adjoins it the outer doorway is liable.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:6)


פתח שבזוית אין בו אלא מזוזה אחת פתח שהוא עשוי בנסרים אין בו אלא מזוזה אחת חייב ר׳ אליעזר בן יעקב פוטר


A corner doorway that has only one doorpost, [or] a doorway made in [a structure of] boards which has only one doorpost is liable. R. Eliezer b. Jacob declares it exempt.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:7)


הכיפין פטורות ר׳ מאיר ור׳ יהודה מחייבין אבל הכל שוין שאם היה הבנין מלמטה והכיפין מלמעלה הרי אלו חייבות במזוזה


Arched doorways are exempt, but R. Meir and R. Judah declare that they are liable. All, however, agree that if they have the [usual] structure below⁹ and the arched section above they are liable to *mezuzah*.

footnotes:
⁹ Being four handbreadths wide and reaching to a height of ten handbreadths (cf. ‘Erub, 11b, Sonc. ed., p. 69).


###### Tractate Mezuzah 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/1:8)


שערי העיר שערי הרחובות שערי העזרות הרי אלו פטורים ושל הלשכות שהיו במקדש היו פטורות מן המזוזה והלשכה של בית הפרוה שהיתה בית דירה לכהן גדול ז׳ ימים בשנה וסוכות היוצרים הרי אלו חייבות במזוזה ור׳ יוסי פוטר:


City gates, the gates of open places¹⁰ and the gates of Temple Courts are exempt.¹¹.] [The doorways of] chambers in the Temple were exempt from *mezuzah*, but the Chamber of the Counsellors,¹², one of the Temple chambers, in agreement with Yoma 10a (Sonc. ed., p. 45). V and H read: *lishkath shel beth happarwah*, ‘the chamber of the Parwah house’, Parwah being the name of its Persian builder (cf. *ibid.* 35a, Sonc. ed., p. 161, n. 6). which served as a residence for the High Priest on seven days in the year,¹³ 2a, Sonc. ed., p. 1). and potters’ booths are subject to *mezuzah*. R. Jose declares them exempt.

footnotes:
¹⁰ Where people assemble for special prayers or to discuss public matters.
¹¹ [But according to Yoma 11a, Sonc. ed., p. 47, city gates require a mezuzah
¹² Reading lishkath parhedrin
¹³ Before the Day of Atonement (cf. ibid.



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:1)


המזוזה נכתבת על הימין בכניסתו מן השוק לבית שער וביציאתו מן החצר לבית שער


The *mezuzah* is placed¹ on the right-hand side of the entrance from the street into the lodge, and [on the right-hand side of] the exit from the courtyard into the lodge.²

footnotes:
¹ lit. ‘written’.
² It refers to where the lodge is in front of a courtyard and has two doorways, one facing the street and the other facing the courtyard.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:2)


גננא שיש לה פצים מן החצר נותן דרך יציאתו מן הגנה לחצר ואם יש לה בית שער נותן מכאן ומכאן


If a garden has a doorpost where it adjoins the courtyard, the *mezuzah* is placed [on the right-hand side of] the exit from the garden into the courtyard; and if a lodge is attached to it,³ *mezuzoth* are to be placed on both doorways [of the lodge].

footnotes:
³ Between the garden and the courtyard, with doorways leading to each of them.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:3)


קיטוניות שהן פתוחים לטרקלן נותן דרך הנעלה ואם היה רגיל על כולם נותן דרך כולם


Where small rooms open into a reception room,⁴ the *mezuzah* is placed on that doorway which is customarily used.⁵ If they are all customarily used, *mezuzoth* are placed on all the doorways.

footnotes:
⁴ Access to which is gained only through the small ones.
⁵ So according to H. V’s reading is corrupt.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:4)


בתים לפנים זה מזה נותן דרך כניסתו לכולם רבי יהודה אומר אם היה הסולם מטלטל לארבע רוחותיו


If a number of rooms have doorways leading from one room to the other,⁶ *mezuzoth* are placed at the entrance of each one of them. R. Judah says: If the ladder is movable on the four sides….⁷ is placed at every side’; but this also does not convey much sense.

footnotes:
⁶ lit. ‘rooms within one another’.
⁷ The sentence is obviously incomplete. H reads: ‘If the ladder is movable a mezuzah


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:5)


פתח שהוא פתוח מן הגג נותן דרך כניסתו מן הגג אמר ר׳ נתן בר׳ יוסי בזה ב״ש מחייבין וב״ה פוטרין


If a doorway leads from a roof [into a room], the *mezuzah* is placed [on the right-hand side of] the entrance from the roof. R. Nathan b. R. Jose said: In such a case Beth Shammai hold that the doorway is subject to *mezuzah* and Beth Hillel hold that it is exempt.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:6)


סוכה שהיא לפנים מן הגג נותן דרך יציאתו מן הסוכה לגג ר׳ יוסי אומר מן הגג לסוכה


In a booth that is set back⁸ from [the edge of] a roof the *mezuzah* is to be placed [on the right-hand side of] the exit from the booth to the roof. R. Jose says: [On the right-hand side of the entrance] from the roof to the booth.

footnotes:
⁸ lit. ‘within’.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:7)


אכסדרה שהיא לפנים מן הבתים ואין לה יציאה ממקום אחר נותן דרך יציאתו מן האכסדרה לבתים ר׳ יוסי אומר דרך כניסתו מבתים לאכסדרה


In the case of a portico that is set back from the rooms and has no other exit,⁹ the *mezuzah* is placed [on the right-hand side of] the exit from the portico into the rooms. R. Jose says: [On the right-hand side of] the entrance from the rooms to the portico.

footnotes:
⁹ Except through one of the rooms.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:8)


פתח שהיא משמשת שני פתחים וכותל רחב טפח נותן מזוזה אחת כדברי ר׳ יהודה יותר מכאן שני מזוזות


If an entrance serves as two doorways and a wall [of not more than] one handbreath in width [separates them], only one *mezuzah* is to be affixed, according to R. Judah. [If the wall was] wider than that two *mezuzoth* are required.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:9)


המזוזה ניתנה מן החצי ולמעלה דברי ר״מ ר׳ יהודה אומר מטפח ולמטה ומטפח ולמעלה


The *mezuzah* is placed in the upper half of the doorpost;¹⁰ so R. Meir. R. Judah says: [It should be placed] below the handbreadth [from the top of the doorpost] and above one handbreadth [from the bottom].

footnotes:
¹⁰ lit. ‘from the half and above’. Another reading is: ‘on the upper third’; cf. the ruling in the name of Samuel in Men. 33a (Sonc. ed., p. 208).


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:10)


חקק בכותל והרחיק טפח ונתנה הרי זו מזוזה כשרה יותר מכאן פסולה חקק במקל ונתנה הרי זו פסולה נתנה בשפופרת תלאה אחר הדלת אחר המזוזה ר׳ מאיר מכשיר ור׳ יהודה פוסל


If one made a groove in the wall at a distance of [not more than] one handbreadth [from the doorpost], and placed [the *mezuzah*] in it, the *mezuzah* is valid. [If the distance] was greater than that it is invalid.
If one made a groove in a stick and put the *mezuzah* in it, it is invalid. If one inserted [the *mezuzah*] in a tube and hung it up behind the door [or] behind the doorpost,¹¹ R. Meir declared it valid, but R. Judah declared it invalid.

footnotes:
¹¹ Hanging the stick on the doorpost.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:11)


בית חדש כיון שגמרו חייב במזוזה


A new house is subject to the obligation of *mezuzah* as soon as it is completed.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:12)


הדר בפונדק בארץ ישראל שלשים יום חייב במזוזה השוכר נותן מיד ובחוצה לארץ הרי זה פטור והשוכר נותן לאחר שלשים יום


One who lodges in an inn in the Land of Israel for thirty days is subject to the obligation of *mezuzah*, and if one rents [a house] he must affix [a *mezuzah*] forthwith. Outside the Land of Israel, [one who lives in an inn] is exempt, and one who rents [a house] must affix [a *mezuzah*] after thirty days.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:13)


השוכר בית מן הנכרי ומן הכותי נותן מזוזה מיד וכשיצא יטלנה והשוכר מישראל יתן מזוזה מיד ואם נתן לא יטול


[A Jew] who rents a house from a Gentile or from a Samaritan must affix a *mezuzah* forthwith, and when he quits he must remove it; but if one rents a house from an Israelite, he affixes the *mezuzah* forthwith and when he quits he must not remove it.


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:14)


הלוקח בית מן הנכרי ומן הכותי חייב במזוזה ומישראל הרי זו בחזקתו


One who buys a house from a Gentile or a Samaritan is under the obligation of putting a *mezuzah*, but [if he bought it] from an Israelite it is presumed [to have been provided with the necessary *mezuzoth*].


###### Tractate Mezuzah 2:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Mezuzah/r/2:15)


הלוקח מלבן מן הנכרי לא ידליק עד שיבדקנו שהמזוזה נבדקת אחת לכ״ה שנה דברי ר״ש ר׳ יעקב אומר עד זמן מרובה אבל הכל שוין שאם היה מעביר ממקום למקום שצריכה בדיקה כיוצא בה מוכנות מים שברשות הרבים נבדקת אחת בשבוע ושברשות היחיד אחת לכ״ה שנה דברי ר׳ מאיר וחכמים אומרים אחד זה ואחד זה זה הכלל כל מקום שהוא בת ראש נבדק אחת בשבוע ושאינו בת ראש נבדק אחת לכ״ה שנה:


If one buys a brick-mould from a Gentile, he should not heat it before he had examined it.
[The scroll in] the *mezuzah* should be examined once in twenty-five years, according to R. Simeon. R. Jacob says: A much longer time [may be allowed to intervene]. Both, however, agree that if it was transferred from one place to another it requires examination.
In like manner, water-tanks¹², ‘stores’. in a public domain must be examined once in seven years, but those situated in a private domain once in twenty-five years, according to R. Meir; but the Sages say: In either case the general rule is that wherever there is a top cover¹³ instead of V’s *bath*. the examination takes place once in seven years, and where there is no top cover the examination takes place once in twenty-five years.

footnotes:
¹² lit. ‘machines’. H has mogeroth
¹³ Reading with H beth
