# Tractate Sefer Torah

מסכת ספר תורה

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah)

כתיבת ספר תורה וכיצד יש לנהוג בו; זהה כמעט לתחילת מסכת סופרים.

Writing and treatment of a Torah scroll; almost identical to the beginning of Tractate Soferim.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 60, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 60)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:1)


אין כותבין ספר תורה לא על עורות בהמה טמאה ולא על עורות חיה טמאה ולא תופרין אותן בגידין ולא כורכין בשערן. הלכה למשה מסיני (אלא) שיהא כותבין על עורות בהמה טהורה ועל עורות חיה טהורה ותופרין בגידין טהורים וכורכין בשערות טהורים וכותבין בדיו שהרי יש לו סמך מן המקרא ואני כותב על הספר בדיו (ירמיהו ל״ו:י״ח):


It is not permitted to write a scroll of the Torah¹ on skins of ritually unclean cattle or on skins of ritually unclean wild animals, nor may they² be sewn with [their] sinews or [the parchment rolls of *tefillin*] be wound with their hair. It is an oral prescription delivered to Moses at Sinai that [these] shall be written on the skins of ritually clean cattle, or on skins of ritually clean wild animals, that they shall be sewn together with ritually clean sinews, [that the *tefillin* rolls] shall be wound with ritually clean hair, and that the writing be done with ink, because [this latter requirement] has support in Scripture, *And I wrote them with ink in the book*.³

footnotes:
¹ The scroll of the Pentateuch used for the lections in public worship.
² The parchment sheets of which the scroll is made up.
³ Jer. 36, 18.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:2)


כותבין על עורות נבלות ועל עורות טרפות ואין חוששין שמא עורות לבובות הן:


It is permitted to write [sacred scrolls] on skins of *nebeloth* and on skins of *ṭerefoth* and there is no need to consider the possibility of their having been pierced at the animal’s heart.⁴

footnotes:
⁴ It was a heathen practice to remove the heart from a live animal to offer it as a sacrifice, and this, in Rabbinic law (Mishnah ‘A.Z. 29b, Sonc. ed., p. 145) rendered the entire animal, including its skin, forbidden as an idolatrous offering.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:3)


לוקחין עורות מכל מקום לספרים ולתפילין ומזוזות ואין חוששין שמא עורות לבובין הן:


Skins⁵ for the [sacred] books, *tefillin* and *mezuzoth* may be bought anywhere, and one need not consider the possibility that they might be skins that were pierced at the animal’s heart.

footnotes:
⁵ Before they were dressed; but dressed skins may be bought only from trustworthy persons who can testify that the dressing had been done in accordance with the law.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:4)


כותבין על הקלף במקום בשר ועל הגויל במקום שער ואם שינה בזה ובזה אל יקרא בו:


The writing on *ḳelaf* must be on the side of the flesh, and on *gewil* it must be on the side of the hair; and if one changed the one for the other [the scroll] may not be used for the lection [in the statutory services].


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:5)


אין כותבין לא על גבי דיפתרא ולא על גבי פינקס ולא על גבי נייר מחוק לא בשחור ולא בשיחור ולא בקומוס ולא בקנקנתום ולא נותנים קנקנתום בדיו:


[Sacred texts]⁶ may not be written on *difthera*, a tablet or erased paper;⁷ nor with coal,⁸ shoe-black, or ink containing gum or vitriol. Vitriol may not be added to the ink.

footnotes:
⁶ Mentioned in Rule 1.
⁷ Others ‘palimpsest’. GRA in Sof. I, 5 omits ‘erased’.
⁸ Or, ‘black pigment’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:6)


אמר רבי יעקב משום רבי מאיר נותנין קנקנתום בדיו אמר רבי יהודה היה רבי מאיר אומר הוא מן התורה בקנקנתום חוץ מפרשת סוטה אמר רבי יעקב לא היה אומר חוץ מפרשת סוטה אלא שבמקדש מפני שהיא נמחקת:


R. Jacob said in the name of R. Meir: Vitriol may be added to the ink. R. Judah said: R. Meir’s statement about [writing with ink containing] vitriol applies to [the whole] Torah⁹ except the section dealing with a suspected wife.¹⁰ R. Jacob retorted: [R. Meir] said, ‘Except the section dealing with a suspected wife’, [by which he meant that] only in the special scroll¹¹ which [was used] in the Temple [must the ink contain no vitriol] because [the writing] had to be blotted out.¹² 23f.

footnotes:
⁹ Cf. ‘Erub. 13a [Sonc. ed., p. 82).
¹⁰ Num. 5, 11ff.
¹¹ A small scroll on which were written the curses that would befall an unfaithful wife.
¹² Cf. Num. ibid.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:7)


אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש משום רבי מאיר משום ר׳ ישמעאל שנותנים קנקנתום בדיו:


R. Simeon b. Laḳish said in the name of R. Meir, who had it from R. Ishmael, that vitriol may be added to the ink.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:8)


אין כותבין עברית ולא מדית ולא עילמת ולא יונית שבעים זקנים כתבו התורה לתלמי המלך כתיבה יונית והיה אותו היום קשה לישראל כיום שעשו את העגל שלא היתה תורה יכולה להתרגם כל צרכה:


[Sacred texts]¹³ may not be written in [obsolete] Hebrew characters or in the Median, Elamitic or Greek languages.¹⁴ and *mezuzoth*. Seventy Elders wrote the Torah for king Ptolemy¹⁵). in Greek, and that day was as ominous for Israel as the day on which the Golden Calf was made, since the Torah could not be adequately translated.

footnotes:
¹³ Mentioned in Rule 1.
¹⁴ According to Meg. 9a (Sonc. ed., p. 48) it is permitted to write the Torah in Greek, though this is not allowed in the case of tefillin
¹⁵ Assumed to be Ptolemy Philadelphus who reigned in Egypt, 285-247 B.C.E., and who arranged for the Greek Version, the Septuagint, to be made, as narrated in Sof. I, 8 (cf. the notes ad loc.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:9)


י״ג דברים שינו בה אלהים ברא בראשית. אעשה אדם בצלם ודמות ויכל בששי וישבות בשביעי. זכר ונקבה בראו (בראשית ה׳:ב׳) הבה ארדה (שם יא) ותצחק שרה בקרוביה לאמר (שם יח). כי באפם הרגו שור וברצונם עקרו אבוס (שם מט) ויקח משה את אשתו ואת בניו וירכיבם על נושא בני אדם (שמות ד׳:כ׳). ומושב בני ישראל אשר ישבו בארץ כנען ובארץ מצרים שלשים שנה ות׳ שנה (שם יב). לא חמד אחד מהם נשאתי (במדבר ט״ז:ט״ו). ואת צעירת הרגלים (ויקרא י״א:כ״ב). אשר חלק ה׳ אלהיך אתם לכל העמים להאיר בהם תחת כל השמים (דברים ד׳:י״ט). ומעלין (רשות) לשמש או לירח או לכל צבא השמים אשר לא צויתי לעבדם (שם יז):


They [all] introduced [the same] thirteen alterations:¹⁶ ‘God created in the beginning’; ‘I shall make a man in image and likeness’; ‘And He finished on the sixth [day] and rested on the seventh [day]’; ‘Male and female He created him’; ‘Come let Me go down’; ‘And Sarah laughed among her relatives, saying’; ‘For in their anger they slew oxen and in their self-will they digged up a stall’; ‘And Moses took his wife and his children and set them upon a carrier of men’; ‘Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in the land of Canaan and in the land of Egypt was four hundred and thirty years’; ‘I have not taken one desirable thing from them’; ‘And the [beast] with small legs’; ‘Which the Lord thy God hath allotted unto all the peoples to give light under the whole heaven’; ‘And they offer sacrifices to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven which I commanded should not be served’.

footnotes:
¹⁶ For a comparison of these variants with the Heb. text, cf. on Sof. I, 8.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:10)


אין כותבין בזהב מעשה בתורתן של אלכסנדרים שהיו כל אזכרותיה כתובים בזהב ובא מעשה לפני חכמים ואמרו תיגנז:


[Sacred scrolls] must not be written in gold. It is related that, in an Alexandrian scroll¹⁷ of the Torah, the divine names were written in gold, and when the matter came before the Sages they decided that it should be stored away.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁷ Cf. note to Sof. I, 9.
¹⁸ lit. ‘it shall be hidden’, i.e. not used for the lections.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:11)


עברית שכתבו תרגום תרגום שכתבו עברית האזינו שעשו רצוף או שעשו את המסורג שלא כהלכתו אל יקרא בו:


If Hebrew words were written in Aramaic or Aramaic words in Hebrew, if *Ha’azinu* was written in continuous lines,¹⁹ or if the breaking up [of the lines] was not done according to the rule, the scroll may not be used for the lections.

footnotes:
¹⁹ Cf. Sof. I, 10, n. 44, for the correct arrangement.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:12)


גמר כל הספר ושייר בו פחות מדף מסרגו ועושה אותו דף קטן ואינו נמנע:


If one finished [writing nearly] all the scroll [of the Torah] and less than a column of text remained, one need not hesitate to extend the writing so as to make of this a small column on its own.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ The extension of a short passage over a full column is done either by enlarging the characters or, according to others, by making each successive line shorter than the one preceding it.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:13)


פתוחה שעשאה סתומה וסתומה שעשאה פתוחה הרי זו תיגנז איזו היא פתוחה כל שהתחיל מראש השיטה כמה יהא בסוף השיטה ויתחיל מראש השיטה והיא נקראת פתוחה כדי לכתוב שם של שלש אותיות:


If an open section was written as a closed one or *vice versa*, the scroll must be stored away. What is an open section? One which commences at the beginning of a line. How much space must there be at the end of a line so that the section beginning at the next line may be called an open one? A space on which may be written a name of three letters.²¹

footnotes:
²¹ The opinion of Maimonides, which has been adopted, is that space must be left for three words, each of three letters (cf. Y.D. CCLXXV, §2).


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/1:14)


גמר כל הפרשה בסוף הדף אם שייר שיטה אחת ופרשה סתומה היא מתחיל באמצע השיטה ואם פתוחה היא מתחיל מלמעלה ומניח את השיטה ההיא:


Should an entire section be finished at the end of a column, if one [blank] line remained and [the next] section is a closed one, [the scribe] begins it in the middle of the line; but if it is an open section, he begins at the top [of the next column] and leaves that line [blank].²²

footnotes:
²² Cf. Sof. I, 14.



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:1)


מניחין בין שם לשם כדי שיהיו ניכרים ובאותיות כדי שלא יהיו מעורבין עירב את האותיות או שהפסיק באמצע השם אל יקרא בו:


Sufficient space must be left between words¹ so that they may be distinguished, and between letters so that they be not mixed. If the letters were mixed up or a break made in the middle of a word, the scroll must not be used for the lection in the statutory services.

footnotes:
¹ lit. ‘between name and name’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:2)


מביאין בין דפין שתי אותיות משם גדול אבל לא משם קטן ואם היה משם קטן בפני עצמו אסור:


[It is permitted] to insert between columns two letters from a long word, but not from a short one. If, however, [the part of a longer word forms] a short word on its own,² (he will reign) the last two letters can form an independent short word *lak* (to thee). it is forbidden [to insert it between the columns].

footnotes:
² e.g. in a word like yimlok


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:3)


מניחין תורה ריוח שתי אצבעות ובנביאים ובחומשין ריוח הגודל:


In a Torah scroll the space of two finger-breadths must be left [between columns], but in scrolls of the Prophets and in those of Pentateuchs³ a space of one thumb-breadth [only].

footnotes:
³ Intended for ordinary reading or study, and not for the public lections.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:4)


מניחין (מלמעלן) [מלמטן] בתורה ריוח טפח ומלמעלה שני חלקים בטפח ובנביאים ובחומשין שלש אצבעות מלמטן ושתים מלמעלן כן וכן אם רצה להוסיף מוסיף ובלבד שלא יהיו זה וזה מרובין מן הכתב:


In the lower margin of a Torah scroll the space of a handbreadth is left, and in the upper margin two-thirds of a handbreadth;⁴ the upper margin must be three finger-breadths wide. but in scrolls of the Prophets and Pentateuchs three finger-breadths in the lower margin and two finger-breadths in the upper. In all these cases⁵ if it is desired to extend [the margins] this may be done, provided they do not exceed [the space of] the written matter.

footnotes:
⁴ lit. ‘two parts of a handbreadth’. This is also the reading of V and M in Sof. II, 4. According to Men. 30a (Sonc. ed., p. 195) and H in Sof. loc. cit.
⁵ lit. ‘here and there’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:5)


מניחין בין ספר לספר בתורה ריוח ארבעה שיטין ובנביא של תרי עשר ג' שיטין מניחין בסוף הספר ובתחלתו כדי להקים ובתורה לא נתנו שיעור אלא עושה עמוד בסוף הספר ואינו צריך לעשות כן אלא בתחילתן:


Between the books in a Torah scroll a vacant space of four lines must be left, and in a scroll containing the Twelve Prophets three lines.
At the end of a scroll and at its beginning sufficient [parchment] must be left to wind⁶. V reads *lehaḳim* ‘to raise up’. [it round the scroll]. In a Torah scroll no limit has been prescribed, but a roller should be attached at the end of the scroll and there is no need to do this at its beginning.⁷

footnotes:
⁶ Reading with many authorities lehaḳḳif
⁷ This regulation does not agree with Sof. II, 5.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:6)


אין פוחתין ביריעה פחות מג׳ דפים ואין מוסיפין על שמונה ובקלפים לא נתנו שיעור אלא מוסיף כל מה שהוא רוצה ובלבד שלא יפחת מג' דפין:


A sheet of a Torah scroll must contain not less than three columns and not more than eight. In the case of *ḳelaf* parchments no limit was prescribed, [62*b*] and one may add [as many columns] as desired provided only there are not less than three columns [to the sheet].


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:7)


גמר כל הספר ושייר בו דף אחד עושה אותו יריעה קטנה בפני עצמה ואינו נמנע:


If one finished [writing nearly] all the book⁸ and one column of text remained, one need not hesitate to make of it a separate small sheet.

footnotes:
⁸ This refers either to one book of the Prophets or to several of them written in one scroll.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:8)


יריעה שבלתה לא יטול שנים ויחזיר שנים אלא נוטל ג׳ ומחזיר ג׳ ומה שהוא מחזיר כמדת כתב הראשון:


If a sheet [of a Torah scroll] is worn out, one may not remove two [columns only] and replace them by two new columns; but three columns should be removed and replaced by three new ones, and the new columns must be written in the same size as the original script.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:9)


שיעור הדף כדי שהוא רואהו ובקטן לא יפחות מטפח ר' יוסי בר יהודה אומר לא יפחות מג׳ אצבעות:


The width of a column [in a Torah scroll] must be such as to be recognizable at one glance,⁹ and in a small scroll not less than a handbreadth. R. Jose b. Judah says: It must not be less than the width of three fingers.

footnotes:
⁹ Accordingly, not more than three Hebrew words, each of ten letters, may be written in a line. If the column is wider, the reader experiences difficulty in passing from line to line.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:10)


לא יעשה ארכו יתר על רחבו ולא רחבו יתר על ארכו אבל ממציעו הוא ועושה אותו מן המובחר:


The height¹⁰ of [a scroll] must not be greater than its circumference,¹¹ nor its circumference greater than its height, but they must be exactly alike,¹² and this is the most correct procedure.

footnotes:
¹⁰ lit. ‘length’.
¹¹ When rolled up, so according to B.B. 14a (Sonc. ed., p. 67); lit. ‘its width’.
¹² lit. ‘takes the middle course’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:11)


לא יעשה גויל וחציו צבאים אע״פ שאינו מן המובחר:


A Torah scroll may not consist half of *gewil* [and half of *ḳelaf*, but it may consist half of *gewil*]¹³ If ‘although’ is altered to ‘because’, the text will make sense but will be contrary to the Rule in Sof. *loc. cit.* and half [of the *ḳelaf*] of deers, although this is not the best procedure.

footnotes:
¹³ The words of this Rule enclosed within square brackets are added from Sof. II, 10, q.v.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 2:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/2:12)


אין דובקין בדבק ולא כותבין על גבי מטלית ולא תופרין במקום הכתב אמר רבי שמעון בן אלעזר משום רבי מאיר דובקין בדבק וכותבין על גבי מטלית אבל אין כותבין במקום הכתב וספר שנקרע טולה עליו מטלית מבחוץ:


[A tear in a Torah parchment sheet] may not be joined with glue, nor is it permitted to write on a patch, nor may [the sheets] be sewn together on the written side. R. Simeon b. Eleazar said in the name of R. Meir: [A torn sheet] may be joined with glue and it is permitted to write on a patch, but it is forbidden to do the sewing¹⁴ on the written side. If a scroll¹⁵ is torn, a patch may be placed on the outside.

footnotes:
¹⁴ So according to GRA, H and M in Sof. II, 11. V reads here as in Sof. ‘the writing’.
¹⁵ Other than a Torah scroll.



## Chapter 3

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:1)


עושה אדם תורה ונביאים כאחת דברי ר׳ יהודה וחכמים אומרים תורה בפני עצמה ונביאים בפני עצמן:


It is permissible to join the Torah and the Prophets in one scroll, according to R. Judah; but the Sages say: The Torah and the Prophets must be written in separate scrolls.¹

footnotes:
¹ According to GRA (in Sof. III, 1) who adopted the reading of B.B. 13b (Sonc. ed., p. 66): ‘it is permissible to fasten the Torah, the Prophets and the Hagiographa together (in one scroll)’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:2)


לא יניח בין נביא לנביא כשם שהוא מניח בין ספר לספר בתורה אבל מניח לזה ריוח בפני עצמו ולזה ריוח בפני עצמו ומתחיל מלמעלן:


Between a book of the Prophets and another one should not leave the same [empty space] as between two books of the Torah; but in each case the space must be that which has been prescribed for it.² Furthermore [a book of the Prophets]³ must begin at the top.⁴

footnotes:
² i.e. four lines between books of the Torah and three between the books of the Prophets.
³ If the preceding book ended at the foot of a column.
⁴ Of the next column, the reason being that, if the books of the Prophets were separated one from the other, the beginning of each book would commence at the top of a column. This does not apply to Torah scrolls, which may never be cut up into separate books.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:3)


אין עושין ספר תורה חומשין שאין מורידן מקדושה חמורה לקדושה קלה אבל עושין חומשין תורה אימתי בזמן שמדתן ושטתן שוין. אין עושין שני חומשין כאחד ולא חומש ומחצה כאחד אבל אם עתיד להוסיף עליהם מותר:


A Torah scroll⁵ may not be made into [separate] books of the Pentateuch, because it is forbidden to reduce a major sanctity⁶ to a minor sanctity.⁷ From scrolls containing sections of the Pentateuch, however, it is permitted to make up a Torah scroll. When may this be done? When the measurements⁸ and the number of the lines⁹ are alike.
It is not permissible to join together two sections of the Pentateuch or one and a half of them to form a single scroll.¹⁰ But if it was intended¹¹ that additional scrolls be attached to them,¹² it is permissible.

footnotes:
⁵ Which contains all the five books of Moses.
⁶ The Torah scroll in its entirety.
⁷ A section of the Pentateuch.
⁸ Of all the scrolls that are to be joined together.
⁹ In each column.
¹⁰ Since it might be mistaken for a proper Torah scroll.
¹¹ When these were written.
¹² To complete a full Torah scroll.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:4)


ספר שנפסק או שנקד ראשי פסוקים אל יקרא בו. גלפו או שעירב אותיותיו אל יקרא בו:


If a Torah scroll has spaces or stops [to mark] the beginning of verses, it may not be used for the lections.¹³ [Similarly] if a letter has been engraved or joined to another, the scroll may not be used for the lections.

footnotes:
¹³ Because all proper Torah scrolls must conform to the original without any deviations.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:5)


ספר שנמחק אל יכתב בו רבי שמעון ב״א אומר אם היתה בבואה שלו ניכרת מותר:


A scroll [some of whose letters] are faded may not be used for the public lections.¹⁴ R. Simeon b. Eleazar says: If the outline [of the effaced letters] is distinguishable, it is permitted [to rewrite them].

footnotes:
¹⁴ So H and GRA in Sof. III, 8. V reads ‘one shall not rewrite [the letters] in it’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:6)


ספר שנמחק בו אות אחת על פני כולו אסור נמחק רובו ומיעוטו קיים מותר.


A scroll of the Torah in which a whole line¹⁵ is faded may not be used. If the greater part of a line is faded and the smaller part intact, the use of the scroll is permitted.

footnotes:
¹⁵ This is the reading in Sof. III, 9. V reads here ‘one letter’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:7)


אין פותחין בתורה יותר מארבעה דפין אבל קורין אפילו עשרה כאחת ואין נמנעין.


Not more than four¹⁶ columns of the Torah scroll may be unrolled [at one time during the reading of the lection] but there is no objection to the reading of ten [columns] in one [lection].

footnotes:
¹⁶ And not less than three (cf. Sof. III, 10).


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:8)


לא יניח כותב בין דין על וקולמוס על גבי הכתב ולא יאחז בקלפים ויתירן אלא יאחז בקלפים ויוציא כתב מבחוץ לא יוציאנו מתוכו ויחלצו וכולם במגיהים ספרים מותר.


A scribe may not put upon the written part [of a Torah scroll] a reed-pen with ink on it;¹⁷ nor may he take hold of the sheets of parchment and thereby unroll [the scroll]; nor may he¹⁸ grasp the parchments to extract the written sheets;¹⁹ nor may he remove a scroll from its [case] by shaking it out. All these [restrictions], however, are relaxed in the case of official revisers of Scriptural scrolls.

footnotes:
¹⁷ So according to Sof. III, 11. The text in V is meaningless.
¹⁸ This is the reading in Sof. III, 11. V reads ‘but he should’.
¹⁹ Which are rolled up; lit. ‘and bring forth the writing without’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:9)


לא יתננו על גבי הכסא ויתן אציליו עליו ויהא קורא בו כדברי רבי נחמיה לא יתננו על גבי הכסא ויהא (נוטלו) [תלוי] וקורא בו כשם שקוראין בשטרות שאין נוהגין בזיון בספרים:


It is not permissible to place a Torah scroll on a chair and to lean on it with one’s elbows while reading; so according to R. Nehemiah. It is not permissible to place it over a chair [with its sheets] hanging down while it is read in the manner of ordinary documents, because [sacred] books must not be treated with disrespect.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:10)


לא יתננו על גבי מטה ולא במרגלות המטה ולא תחת המטה שישב אדם על גבי המטה והספר עליה. מעשה ברבי אליעזר שישב לו על גבי המטה והספר עליה ועמד כאדם שנשכו נחש שנאמר את שבתותי תשמורו ומקדשי תיראו לא משבתות אתה ירא אלא ממי שצוה עליו שנא׳ זה אלי ואנוהו אתנאה לו כדברי רבי ישמעאל רבי עקיבא אומר אדבר בנאות שלו אבא שאול אומר אדמה לו מה הוא חנון ורחום אף אתה היה חנון ורחום:


A Torah scroll may not be placed on a bed and [certainly]²⁰ not at its foot or under it; nor may one sit²¹ on a bed while a [Torah] scroll rests on it. It is related that R. Eliezer²² once sat [unknowingly] on a bed on which a [Torah] scroll lay, and [when he realized it] he jumped up as if a snake had bitten him. [Such respect is shown for the Torah] because Scripture declares, *Ye shall keep My sabbaths, and reverence My sanctuary*²³—it is not the Sabbaths that one reverences but Him Who commanded [to observe them], for Scripture declares, *This is my God, and I will glorify Him*²⁴ [which means,]²⁵ (*I will glorify Him*) homiletically with *na’eh* (beautiful) and understanding it as ‘I will serve Him in a beautiful manner’. I will perform the commandment in a beautiful way to His glory.²⁶ Such is the interpretation of R. Ishmael. R. ‘Aḳiba expounds it: I will expatiate on His excellencies.²⁷, lit. ‘beauties’, excellent attributes. Abba Saul explains it: I will be like Him,²⁸ as the equivalent of *’ani wahu* (I and He). i.e. as He is gracious and merciful so be thou gracious and merciful.

footnotes:
²⁰ Cf. N.Y. on Sof. III, 13. The insertion of ‘certainly’ avoids an anticlimax.
²¹ lit. ‘that one may sit’.
²² In Sof. III, 13, ‘R. Eleazar’.
²³ Lev. 19, 30.
²⁴ Ex. 15, 2.
²⁵ Connecting we’anwehu
²⁶ lit. ‘before Him’.
²⁷ Heb. na’oth
²⁸ He explains we’anwehu


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:11)


אין נוהגין בזיון באוכלין לא ישב אדם על גבי קופה מלאה תמרים וגרוגרות אבל יושב הוא על גבי קופה מלאה קטניות ואף על גבי עיגול דבילה מפני שנהגו בו כן:


Foodstuffs may not be treated with disrespect. One may not sit on a basket containing dates or dried figs;²⁹ but he may sit on a basket that contains pulse and also on a cake of pressed figs, because it is customary to do so in such cases.³⁰

footnotes:
²⁹ Because they might be crushed and spoilt.
³⁰ Pulse and dried figs are not spoilt by sitting on them.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 3:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/3:12)


אין מכסין באוכלים ר׳ מאיר אומר כל שיש לו קליפה מותר ר׳ יהודה אומר כל שיש לו עוקץ או יד מותר אין אוכלין אוכלים באוכלים אלא אם כן אוכלן בבת אחת.


Foodstuffs may not be used as a covering. R. Meir says: Any fruit which has a husk may be [used as a covering]. R. Judah says: Any fruit which has a stem or a stalk³¹ may be [used as a covering].³² Foodstuffs may not be eaten with the aid of foodstuffs³³ unless they are consumed simultaneously.³⁴

footnotes:
³¹ Whereby it can be lifted if it should happen to fall into the contents of the vessel it covered.
³² Since it would not be necessary to throw it away after use.
³³ Using them, e.g., in place of a spoon.
³⁴ And would not be thrown away.



## Chapter 4

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:1)


אלו שמות שאין נמחקין הכותב אלהים אדני יוד הא ואו הא שדי צבאות אהיה אשר אהיה ר׳ יוסי אומר צבאות היו נוהגין בו חול:


The following divine names may not be erased, viz.¹ *Alef-lamed-he-yod-mem*,² *Alef-daleth-nun-yod*,³ *Yod-he-waw-he*,⁴ *Shaddai*,⁵ *Ẓeba’oth*,⁶ *‘Eheyeh-’asher-’eheyeh*.⁷ (Ex. 3, 14). R. Jose says: *Ẓeba’oth* is generally treated as a secular noun.⁸

footnotes:
¹ lit. ‘he who writes’.
² Meaning ‘God’.
³ Translated ‘Lord’.
⁴ Composing the Tetragrammaton.
⁵ i.e. ‘Almighty’.
⁶ Meaning ‘[Lord of] hosts’.
⁷ I am that I am
⁸ Which may therefore be erased.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:2)


הכותב אל ימחוק אל מאלהים יה מארבע אותיות אינן נמחקין מפני שיש שמות כיוצא בהם:


If one writes *’El*⁹ it may be erased;¹⁰ if *’El* of *Alef-lamed-he-yod-mem* or *Yod-he* of the four letters [of the Tetragrammaton],¹¹. they may not be erased, because there are divine names corresponding to them.

footnotes:
⁹ It can mean ‘to’ or ‘God’ so far as the consonants are concerned.
¹⁰ It is presumed to be the preposition ‘to’. This Rule is omitted in Sof. IV, 2.
¹¹ Which are Yod-he-waw-he


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:3)


כל אותיות המשמשות את השם בין מלמעלה בין מלמטה הרי אלו נמחקין:


All prefixes or suffixes connected with a divine name may be erased.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:4)


כל השמות ההדיוטות שאותיותיהם כאותיות השם מכנין בהם הרי אלו נמחקין:


All ordinary words the letters of which are the same as those of a divine name may be erased.¹²

footnotes:
¹² Because they possess no sanctity.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:5)


כי ה׳ אלהיכם הוא אלהי האלהים (דברים י׳:י״ז) הראשון קודש והשני חול ואדני האדנים (שם) הראשון קודש והשני חול אלהי אברהם (בראשית ל״א:נ״ג) קדש ואלהי נחור חול אלהי אביהם חול. אלהים לא תקלל (שמות כ״ב:כ״ז) משמש קודש וחול ר' ישמעאל אומר קודש:


In *For the Lord your God, He is God of gods*,¹³ the first [two]¹⁴. are sacred and the last¹⁵, signifying ‘judges’ or ‘princes’. is secular. In *Lord of lords*,¹⁶ the first is sacred and the second secular. In *the God of Abraham*¹⁷ it is sacred; in *the god of Nahor*¹⁸ Nahor did not worship the true God. it is secular, and in *the god of their father*¹⁹ Terah (*their father*) was an idolater. it is secular. In *Thou shalt not revile God*,²⁰ [the noun may bear] a sacred or a secular meaning.²¹ R. Ishmael²² maintains that the noun is sacred.

footnotes:
¹³ Deut. 10, 17.
¹⁴ i.e. your God He is God
¹⁵ Of gods
¹⁶ ibid.
¹⁷ Gen. 31, 53.
¹⁸ ibid.
¹⁹ ibid.
²⁰ Ex. 22, 27.
²¹ It may refer to God or judges.
²² In Sof. IV, 5, ‘R. Simeon’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:6)


כל שמות האמורים בתורה באברהם קודש חוץ מן הראשון ר׳ חנינא בן אחי ר׳ יהושע אומר קודש:


All nouns in the Torah [signifying God] that are mentioned in connection with Abraham are sacred except the first.²³ (Gen. 18, 3), because *my lord* was addressed to the leader of the three angels R. Ḥanina the son of R. Joshua’s brother holds that it is sacred.²⁴ was addressed to God.

footnotes:
²³ The verse, And he said: My lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight
²⁴ In his opinion my Lord


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:7)


כל שמות האמורים בתורה בלוט חול חוץ מן האחרון במיכה חול אפילו יה בנבות קודש אפילו אל:


All names in the Torah mentioned in connection with Lot are secular²⁵ except the last.²⁶ (Gen. 19, 18). Lot’s address to the angels is understood as ending at *not so*, and his petition to God then begins, *My Lord, behold*, etc. [So the Targum and Shebu. 35b, Sonc. ed., pp. 205f.] [All names] in the story of Micah²⁷ are secular, even [when they begin with] *Yod-he*.²⁸ In [the account of] Naboth²⁹ they are sacred even [when they begin with] *Alef-lamed*.³⁰

footnotes:
²⁵ There is only one secular name in the Lot passages, and the Tetragrammaton occurs twice. The word ‘all’ is not intended to be taken literally (cf. N.Y. on Sof. IV, 7).
²⁶ Viz. And Lot said unto them: ‘Oh, not so my Lord’
²⁷ Judg. 17f.
²⁸ The Tetragrammaton.
²⁹ 1 Kings 21.
³⁰ Meaning elsewhere ‘God’.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/4:8)


אלהים נצב בעדת אל בקרב אלהים ישפוט (תהלים פב) משמש קודש וחול יסגירני אל אל עויל (איוב ט״ז:י״א) הראשון קודש והשני חול כי אל אל האמור (שם לד) הראשון חול והשני קודש ואל יהי מקום לזעקתי (שם טז) חול ואלהים אמר לבהלני (ד״ה ב לה) קודש חדל לך מאלהים אשר עמי (שם) קדש כדברי ר׳ יוסי בר יהודה אלהים זדים קמו עלי (תהלים פו) קדש אלא שהקורא צריך להיות קורא ומפסיק:


In *God standeth in the congregation of God, in the midst of the judges*³¹ *He judges*,³² [the divine name] is used as sacred³³. and as secular.³⁴ In *God delivereth me to*³⁵ (to) which is the same consonants as the word for ‘God’. *the ungodly*,³⁶ the first is sacred and the second³⁷ in the sense of ‘to’. secular. In *For hath any said unto God*,³⁸ XXXIV, 31. the first [*’el*] is secular and the second sacred. [In the verse] *And let my cry have no*³⁹ *resting-place*,⁴⁰ XVI, 18. In Sof. IV, 9 the analysis is extended to the continuation of the verse. etc., [the words whose consonants are the same as those of a divine name] are secular. In *God hath given command to speed me*⁴¹ [the name] is sacred. In *Forbear thee from meddling with God, Who is with me*,⁴² the name is sacred, according to the view of R. Jose b. Judah. In *O God, the proud are risen up against me*,⁴³ the name is sacred but the reader must pause in his reading [after *God*].⁴⁴ might erroneously be taken as qualifying God.

footnotes:
³¹ The Heb. has the consonants of the divine name.
³² Ps. 82, 1.
³³ In God standeth
³⁴ The name bearing the meaning of judges.
³⁵ Heb. ’el
³⁶ Job 16, 11.
³⁷ ’el
³⁸ ibid.
³⁹ Heb. על, the same consonants as those of the name of God.
⁴⁰ ibid.
⁴¹ 2 Chron. 35, 21.
⁴² ibid.
⁴³ Ps. 86, 14.
⁴⁴ In the absence of the pause, the adjective proud



## Chapter 5

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/5:1)


הכותב שני שמות של קודש מקיים את הראשון ומחטיב את האחרון רבי יהודה אומר אם היה האחרון בסוף הדף מחטיב ומוחק את הראשון ומקיים את האחרון:


If [a scribe] wrote a sacred name twice,¹ he retains the first and erases the latter.² R. Judah says: If the latter occurred at the end of a column, he erases the first and retains the latter.³

footnotes:
¹ lit. ‘he who writes two sacred names’.
² The first is retained because it was properly written; the second is erased because it was written in error.
³ [In Sof. V, 1, the reading is: ‘R. Judah says: If the first occurs at the end of a column’. Here H reads: ‘If the latter occurs at the beginning of a column’. Either of these must be substituted for V because the idea is that] it spoils the appearance to leave a blank space at the beginning of the top line of a column.


###### Tractate Sefer Torah 5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Sefer%20Torah/r/5:2)


שני שמות של חול מקיים את הראשון ומוחק את האחרון רבי יהודה אומר אם היה האחרון בראש הדף מוחק את הראשון ומקיים את האחרון:


If [the scribe wrote] a secular noun twice,⁴ he retains the first and wipes away the latter.⁵ R. Judah says: If the latter was at the top of a column,⁶ he wipes away the first and retains the latter.

footnotes:
⁴ lit. ‘two secular names’.
⁵ While the ink is still wet.
⁶ [Cf. Sof. V, 2, n. 6.]

הכותב יהודה ולא כתב בו דלית יתלנו מלמעלה את השם כתב השם וכתב את יהודה עושה דלית הא ומוחק את ההא האחרונה (ויתלה את דלית):


If a scribe writes *Yehudah* and omits the *daleth* he inserts it above the line. If he intended to write the Tetragrammaton⁷. Lit. ‘the name, he wrote the name’, apparently a misprint. and wrote *Yehudah*⁸. instead, he alters the *daleth* to *he*⁹. and wipes away the final letter *he*.

###### Tractate Sefer Torah 5:4

היה צריך לכתוב את יהודה ונתכוין וכתב את השם אע״פ שנתן בו דלית מחטיבו וכותב יהודה אחר:


If it was required to write *Yehudah* but [the scribe] intended to write the Tetragrammaton, although he [inadvertently] inserted the *daleth*,¹⁰ he erases it and writes another *Yehudah*.¹¹

היה צריך לכתוב את השם ונתכוין וכתב יהודה אע״פ שנתן בו דלית מוחק את הא האחרונה ויכתוב דלית הא ר׳ יהודה אומר יחזור עליו הקולמוס ויחדשנו אמרו לו אין זה מן המובחר:


If it was required to write the Tetragrammaton but [the scribe] intended to write *Yehudah*, although he inserted the *daleth*¹² was not only intended but also written correctly, in the wrong place. [Cf. the variant reading in Sof. V, 3.] he wipes away the final *he* and alters [the preceding] *daleth* into *he*.¹³ R. הכותב את השם וטעה אות אחת יתלנו מלמעלה טעה את השם כולו יתלנו בין השיטין כדברי ר׳ יהודה ר׳ יוסי אומר מוחק מה שלפניו וכותב את השם וחוזר ותולה מה שמוחק ר׳ חנניה בן עקשיא אומר צריך לגנוז את כל היריעה:


If in writing the Tetragrammaton he made an error [by omitting] one letter he should suspend it above [the line]. If one erred [by omitting] all the name¹⁴ he should suspend it between the lines. If one wrote *Alef-lamed* by mistake three¹⁵ times in the clause *God delivereth me to the ungodly*,¹⁶ one retains¹⁷ the first and erases¹⁸ the latter.¹⁹ which, having been intended in error to stand for the divine name, is treated in accordance with Rule 1 above. הכותב שם על בשרו לא ירחץ ולא יסוך ר׳ יוסי אומר מותר ובלבד שלא ישפשף על קרן הפרה ועל כרעי המטה גוררן וגונזן על האבן שומטה וגונזה:


If a person writes a divine name on his body, he must neither bathe nor anoint himself.⁵⁰ R. Jose says: This is permitted provided only that he does not rub it off. המחתך בספרים בחדשים מותר בישנים אסור (במקום הספרים) במקק הספרים ובמקק התפילין ובמקק מטפחות מהספרים הרי אלו יגנזו אבל לא יניחם אלא במקום תורפה והם מרקבין מאליהם:


Should one cut off a strip of a scroll,⁵⁴ it may [be used for ordinary purposes] if it is a new one,⁵⁵ but if it is an old scroll⁵⁶ [the use of the strip] is forbidden. # Tractate Semachot

מסכת שמחות

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot)

דינים ומנהגים הקשורים למוות: רגע המוות, קבורה, אבלות וכללי התנהגות בבית הקברות.

Laws and customs relating to death: the moment of death, burial, mourning, and cemetery conduct.

Sections: Paragraph

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 231, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 231)


## Introduction

###### Tractate Semachot, Introduction 1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/s/Introduction/r/1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/s/Introduction/r/1)


(שמות י״ב:כ״ט) ויהי בחצי הלילה וה׳ הכה כל בכור בארץ מצרים וגו׳ וכתיב (במדבר ח׳:י״ז) כי לי כל בכור [וגו׳] ביום הכותי כל בכור וגו' (ואתה משיב) א״ר יוחנן אע״פ שהכה אותם מכת מות מחצי הלילה היתה נפשם מפרפרת בהם עד הבוקר משל הדיוט אומר נתת פת לנער הודע את אמו אף הקדוש ברוך הוא אמר אודיע לבני המיתה המשתקת הזאת ששונאיהם היאך מתים בה אלא תשמור נפשותם עד הבוקר כדי שיראו בני בשונאיהם:


*And it came to pass at midnight, that the Lord smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt*,² etc.; and it is written, *For all the first-born among the children of Israel are Mine, both men and beast; on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them for Myself*.³ R. Joḥanan said: Although He smote them with the plague of death at midnight, the souls writhed within them until morning. A common proverb says, ‘If you give a morsel of bread to a child, inform his mother’.⁴ Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘I will inform My children of the death by choking⁵ of which their enemies are dying. Let their souls await the morning [before expiring], so that My children shall look upon [the fate of] their enemies’.

footnotes:
² Ex. 12, 29.
³ Num. 8, 17.
⁴ Cf. Beẓah 16a (Sonc. ed., p. 81) where it is quoted, not as a proverb, but as a saying of Rabban Simeon b. Gamaliel.
⁵ GRA’s emendation of a verb in the text meaning ‘which silences’.



## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Semachot 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:1)


הגוסס הרי הוא כחי לכל דבר לעולם (זקוק) [זוקק] ליבום ופוטר מן היבום ומאכיל בתרומה ופוסל בתרומה ונוחל ומנחיל פרש ממנו אבר כאבר מן החי בשר כבשר מן החי וזורקין על ידו דם חטאתו ודם אשמו עד שימות:


A dying man¹, the term applied when the rattle in the throat indicates that a person is at the point of death. is regarded as a living entity in respect of all matters in the world: he holds [his brother’s wife] tied to the leviratical marriage,² he frees [his mother] from the obligation of a leviratical marriage³ and enables her to eat *terumah*,⁴, she may continue to eat *terumah* so long as he remains at the point of death. and he [may also] disqualify her from eating *terumah;*⁵ married to a lay-Israelite, she may not eat of the *terumah* belonging to her father which, on the death of her husband, she is permitted to eat when she returns to his home (cf. Lev. 22, 12f). The reason is that, since her son is regarded as living, it would be contrary to the stipulation in Lev. *and have no child*. he inherits and transmits;⁶ if one of his limbs is severed, it is regarded as a limb cut off from the living;⁷ if [part of his] flesh [is severed], it is regarded as flesh cut off from the living;⁸ and the blood of his sin-offering and guilt-offering is sprinkled for him until the time he dies.⁹

footnotes:
¹ Heb. gosēs
² Cf. Deut. 25, 5ff. Should the brother die while he himself is dying, the former’s widow is precluded from marrying until she is released by the latter from his obligation to wed her (cf. Ohol. I, 6, Sonc. ed., pp. 151f).
³ If his father died and left no other children, his mother is free to remarry because the dying man is regarded as living. Even a child who survives one day frees his mother from the levirate. Cf. Nid. 43b (Sonc. ed., p. 303).
⁴ If his mother is the daughter of a lay-Israelite married to a kohen
⁵ If she is the daughter of a kohen
⁶ i.e. an estate. On inheritance and transmission, cf. B.B. 108a (Sonc. ed., p. 448).
⁷ There is a legal difference if it is a limb severed from a living or dead body. If it was from a dead body, a piece of flesh from it, even the size of an olive, communicates defilement; but if from a living body it does not. Therefore, if one of the dying man’s limbs is severed, flesh from it does not defile because he is considered a living being.
⁸ Flesh not necessarily from a severed limb.
⁹ Where a man who brought a sin- or guilt-offering died before it was sacrificed, the animal for the former had to be killed and the latter turned into the fields to graze until it died naturally. But with a dying man who brought an offering, the ritual connected with his sacrifice was carried out completely.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:2)


אין קושרין את לחייו ואין פוקקין את נקביו ואין נותנין כלי של מתכות ודבר שהוא מיקר על טיבורו עד שעה שימות שנאמר (קהלת י״ב:ו׳) עד אשר לא ירתק חבל הכסף:


We do not tie up his cheek-bones,¹⁰ or stop up his apertures,¹¹ or place a metal vessel or anything which chills on his navel;¹² reads ‘on his stomach’, that it should not swell. as it is stated, *Before the silver cord is snapped asunder and the golden bowl is shattered, and the pitcher is broken at the fountain.*¹³

footnotes:
¹⁰ To prevent the jaw from dropping; cf. Shab. 151a (Sonc. ed., p. 771).
¹¹ To prevent air from entering.
¹² Shab. loc. cit.
¹³ Eccl. 12, 6. None of these acts may be done because they hasten death.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:3)


אין מזיזין אותו ואין מטילין אותו על גבי החול ולא על המלח עד שעה שימות:


We may not move him, or place him on sand or salt¹⁴ until he dies.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁴ For ‘salt’ GRA reads ‘a vessel that chills’; cf. Tosiftha Shab. XVIII, 18.
¹⁵ So that the body should keep cool and not swell.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:4)


אין (מעמידין) [מעמצין] את עיני הגוסס הנוגע בו ומזיזו הרי זה שופך דמים שהיה רבי מאיר אומר משל לנר שהוא מטפטף כיון שנגע בו אדם מכבהו כך כל המעמץ את עיני הגוסס מעלין עליו כאילו הוא נוטל נשמתו:


We may not close the eyes¹⁶ (Sonc. ed., p. 772). Closing the eyes of a corpse is a very ancient practice. According to Ibn Ezra the custom is alluded to in Gen. 46, 4, *and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes* (cf. his commentary *ad loc*.). The custom was current among the ancient Greeks and Romans and is practised by the Egyptians [cf. Seyffert, *Dictionary of Classical Antiquities*, p. 101b, and Lane, *Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians*, ch. XXVIII]. A man, at the moment of death, was believed to behold the Divine Presence (cf. Job 19, 27) and therefore it was unfitting that after that vision his eyes should look at anything mundane. Cf. A. Bender in *Jewish Quarterly Review*, VII (1895), pp. 102f. of a dying man. Whoever touches and moves him is a murderer. For R. Meir used to say: He can be compared to a lamp which is dripping;¹⁷ reads ‘a lamp that is going out’. should a man touch it he extinguishes it. Similarly whoever closes the eyes of a dying man is considered as if he had taken his life.

footnotes:
¹⁶ Shab. loc. cit.
¹⁷ Shab. loc cit.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:5)


אין קורעין ואין חולצין ולא מספידין ואין מכניסין ארון עמו בבית עד שעה שימות:


We do not rend the garments or bare the shoulder,¹⁸ in the usual sense of ‘removing the shoes’. or deliver a memorial address, or bring the coffin into the house until he dies.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁸ Cf. Rashi to M.Ḳ. 22b (Sonc. ed., p. 140). R. Meir of Rothenberg explains the word ḥoleẓin
¹⁹ These things should be avoided so as not to frighten the dying person.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:6)


אין משמעין עליו ואין משננין עליו את מעשיו רבי יהודה אומר אם חכם הוא משננין [עליו] את מעשיו:


We do not summon the people²⁰ (cf. Sanh. 47a, Sonc. ed., p. 311), ‘We do not summon the people of the townships’. or recount his good deeds. R. Judah said: If he is a scholar we recount his good deeds.²¹

footnotes:
²⁰ Cf. 1 Sam. 15, 4, XXIII, 8 for this usage of the Heb. verb. Brüll adds the word ‘ayaroth
²¹ Because he is accustomed to have his praises sung and it would not distress him in the circumstances.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:7)


אין שואלין בעיר זה את זה בד"א בכפר קטן אבל בעיר גדול מותר מחותך מסורס נפלים ובן שמונה חי בן תשעה מת אין מתעסקין עמו בכל דבר:


²² In the town people do not greet each other.²³ This applies only in a village,²⁴ but in a large city it is permissible.
We do not carry out the mourning rites for one who came out [at birth] by pieces or with feet foremost, or for one born prematurely²⁵, a child who dies within thirty days of birth. at eight months²⁶ alive or at nine months dead.

footnotes:
²² This Rule is not connected with the preceding, but speaks of a case where there is a dead person in the town.
²³ Because all must share in the mourning, and greeting is not permitted to a mourner.
²⁴ Where all learn quickly of the death.
²⁵ Heb. nefel
²⁶ And cannot therefore survive.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:8)


נכרי ועבד אין מתעסקין עמו לכל דבר אבל קורין עליו הוי ארי ארי הוי גבור רבי יהודה אומר הוי טבי הוי נאמן אוכל מעמלו אמרו לו מה הנחת לכשרים אמר להן אם היה כשר מפני מה אין קורין עליו: אין מקבלין תנחומין על העבדים ועל השפחות:


For a non-Jew or a slave we do not occupy ourselves with his funeral rites, but we exclaim of him, ‘Alas lion!²⁷ alas mighty man!’. R. Judah said: [We, for instance, exclaim], ‘Alas, Ṭabi!²⁸ alas, faithful man who ate²⁹ of his labour!’. They said to him,³⁰ ‘[If so], what have you left [to be said] of worthy men [who are not slaves]?’ He replied, ‘If he was worthy, why should we not say it of him, since³¹ we do not receive condolence for [the loss of] male or female slaves?’

footnotes:
²⁷ So H; V repeats ‘lion’.
²⁸ The faithful slave of Rabban Gamaliel (cf. Ber. 16b, Sonc. ed. p. 96).
²⁹ In Ber. ‘who worked for his living’.
³⁰ To R. Jose who, in Ber. (Sonc. ed., p. 97), suggested the praise to be made over a faithful slave.
³¹ So H; V lacks ‘since’.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:9)


ומעשה כשמתה שפחתו של ר׳ אליעזר נכנסו תלמידיו לנחמו נכנס מפניהם לחצר נכנסו אחריו נכנס לביתו נכנסו אחריו אמר להם כמדומה הייתי שאתם נכוין בפושרין והלא אין אתם נכוין אפילו ברותחין הלא אמרו שאין מקבלין תנחומין על העבדים שהעבדים חשובים כבהמה:


It is related that when R. Eliezer’s female slave died, his disciples came to comfort him. He entered the courtyard [to avoid them], but they followed him; he went into the house, but they followed him. He said to them, ‘I imagined that you would be scalded with tepid water, but now you are not even scalded with hot water.³² Have [the Sages] not said: ³³We do not receive condolence for slaves because they are reckoned as animals?’³⁴

footnotes:
³² The meaning is, I made it clear to you that I did not want to receive your condolence; cf. Ber. loc. cit.
³³ In Ber., ‘Have I not taught you’, etc.
³⁴ The text in Ber. reads: What do we say over them? As we say to a man on the death of his ox or ass, ‘May the Omnipresent repair thy loss’, so we say to a man on the death of his slaves, ‘May the Omnipresent repair thy loss’.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:10)


וכשמת טבי עבדו של רבן גמליאל קבל עליו תנחומים אמרו לו לא למדתנו רבינו שאין מקבלין תנחומין על העבדים אמר להן אין טבי עבדי כשאר כל העבדים כשר היה:


And when Ṭabi the slave of Rabban Gamaliel died, he received condolence for him. They asked him, ‘Master, have you not taught us that we do not receive condolence for slaves?’ He replied, ‘My slave Ṭabi was unlike all other slaves; he was a worthy man’.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:11)


אף הוא הניח לו להניח תפלין אמרו לו לא למדתנו רבינו שהעבדים פטורין מן התפלין אמר להן אין טבי עבדי כשאר כל העבדים כשר הוא:


He also permitted Ṭabi to put on the *tefillin*. They said to him, ‘Master, have you not taught us that slaves are exempt from [the precept of] *tefillin?*’ He replied, ‘My slave Ṭabi was unlike all other slaves; he was a worthy man’.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:12)


אין קורין לעבדים ולשפחות אבא פלוני ואימא פלונית של בית רבן גמליאל היו קורין לאבא טבי ולאימא טביתא:


We do not call male and female slaves ‘Father So-and-so, Mother So-and-so’. Those of the house of Rabban Gamaliel, however, were called ‘Father Ṭabi’ and ‘Mother Ṭabitha’.³⁵ [The female slave Ṭabitha is mentioned in j.Nid. I, 4, 49b.]

footnotes:
³⁵ Quoted from Ber. loc. cit.


###### Tractate Semachot 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/1:13)


אין קורין לאבות אבינו אלא לשלשה האבות ולא לאימהות אמנו אלא לארבע האימהות:


We confine the term ‘our father’ to the three Patriarchs,³⁶ and the term ‘our mother’ to the four Matriarchs.³⁷

footnotes:
³⁶ Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
³⁷ Sara, Rebekah, Rachel and Leah. This Rule is also culled, in a slightly different form from Ber. loc. cit.



## Chapter 2

###### Tractate Semachot 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:1)


המאבד עצמו לדעת אין מתעסקין עמו בכל דבר רבי ישמעאל אומר קורין עליו הוי נטלה הוי נטלה א"ל ר"ע הנח לו בסתמו אל תכבדהו ואל תקללהו אין קורעין עליו ואין חולצין עליו ולא מספידין עליו אבל עומדין עליו בשורה ואומרין עליו ברכת אבלים מפני שהוא כבוד חיים כללו של דבר כל שהוא כבוד של חיים מתעסקין בו כל שאין כבוד של חיים אין הרבים מתעסקין עמו לכל דבר:


We do not occupy ourselves in any respect with the funeral rites of one who committed suicide wilfully. R. Ishmael said: We exclaim over him, ‘Alas for a lost¹, ‘[a life] carried away’. H reads *nishlah* with a similar meaning (cf. *God takth away* [*yeshel*] *his soul*, Job 27, 8). GRA emends to *nithlah*, ‘hanged’. [life!] Alas for a [lost] life!’ R. ‘Aḳiba said to him, ‘Leave him unmourned; speak neither well nor ill of him’.²
We do not rend garments for him,³ Y.D., §345, near relatives do not rend their garments. bare the shoulder, or deliver a memorial address over him. We do, however, stand in a row⁴ for him and recite the benediction of mourners⁵, p. 119. for him, from respect of the living [relatives]. The general rule is: With anything that makes for respect of the living we occupy ourselves, but with anything that does not make for the respect of the living, the public do not in any way occupy themselves.

footnotes:
¹ Heb. niṭṭelah
² lit. ‘do not bless him and do not curse him’.
³ According to the Ṭur
⁴ At the cemetery after the funeral those present divide themselves into two rows and the mourners pass between them to receive condolences.
⁵ The condolence ended with the words, ‘Blessed be He Who comforteth the mourners’ (Keth. 8b, Sonc. ed., p. 40). Hence the term ‘benediction of mourners’; cf. J. Rabbinowitz, Mishnah Megillah


###### Tractate Semachot 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:2)


איזהו המאבד עצמו לדעת לא שעלה בראש האילן ונפל ומת בראש הגג ונפל ומת אלא זה שאמר הריני עולה לראש הגג או לראש האילן ואפיל עצמי ואמות ורואין אותו שעלה לראש האילן ונפל ומת הרי זה בחזקת המאבד את עצמו בדעת וכל המאבד את עצמו לדעת אין מתעסקין עמו בכל דבר:


Who [comes within the category of] ‘one who committed suicide wilfully’? He does not who climbed to the top of a tree and fell down and died, or he who went up to the top of the roof and fell down and died.⁶ But he who calls out, ‘Look, I am going to the top of the roof or to the top of the tree, and I will throw myself down that I may die’ [comes within the category]. When people saw him go up to the top of a tree or roof [for the purpose] and he fell down and died, he is presumed to have committed suicide wilfully; and with the person who commits suicide wilfully we do not occupy ourselves in any respect.

footnotes:
⁶ It may have been an accidental fall.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:3)


מצאהו חנוק ותלוי באילן הרוג ומושלך על גבי הסייף הרי זה בחזקת המאבד את עצמו שלא בדעת ואין מונעין הימנו כל דבר:


If a person was found strangled or hanging from a tree or lying dead on a sword, he is presumed not to have committed suicide wilfully, and none [of the rites] are withheld from him.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:4)


מעשה בבנו של גורנוס בלוד שברח מבית הספר והראה לו אביו באזנו ונתירא מאביו והלך ואבד עצמו בבגד ובאו ושאלו את רבי טרפון ואמר אין מונעין הימנו כל דבר:


It is related of the son of Gorgias⁷ of Lydda that he ran away from school and his father pointed to his ear.⁸ In fear of his father he went and destroyed himself in a pit.⁹ They went and inquired of R. Ṭarfon who ruled: We do not withhold anything from him.¹⁰

footnotes:
⁷ A variant is Gornos. [He is not mentioned elsewhere in Rabbinic literature.]
⁸ i.e. he threatened to punish him.
⁹ So GRA and H. V wrongly ‘with a garment’.
¹⁰ He is buried with full rites.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:5)


מעשה בתינוק אחד מבני ברק ששבר צלוחית בשבת והראה לו אביו באזנו ונתירא מאביו והלך ואבד עצמו בבור ושאלו את רבי עקיבא ואמר אין מונעין הימנו כל דבר:


It is related of a child in Benë Beraḳ¹¹ that he broke a bottle on the Sabbath and his father pointed to his ear. In fear of his father he went and destroyed himself in a pit. They inquired of R. ‘Aḳiba who ruled: We do not withhold anything from him.

footnotes:
¹¹ A town near Jaffa.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:6)


מכאן אמרו חכמים אל יראה אדם לתינוק באזנו אלא מלקיהו מיד או ישתוק ולא יאמר לו כלום ר׳ שמעון בן אלעזר אומר יצר תינוק ואשה תהא שמאל דוחה וימין מקרבת:


Hence the Sages ruled: A man should not point at the ear of a child, but either punish him immediately or keep silent and say nothing to him.
R. Simeon b. Eleazar said:¹² With human nature,¹³, which means human instinct; cf. Lazarus, *Ethics of Judaism*, II, pp. 106f. a child and a woman, the left hand should repulse them but the right hand bring them back.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹² Sanh. 107b (Sonc. ed., p. 736), Soṭah 47a (Sonc. ed., p. 246).
¹³ Heb. Yeẓer
¹⁴ One should not be too severe with them, not suppressing their desires but disciplining them.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:7)


הרוגי בית דין אין מתעסקין עמהן בכל דבר אחיהם וקרוביהם באין ושואלין את שלום העדים ואת שלום הדיינין שאין בלבנו עליכם שדין אמת דנתם ולא היו מתאבלין אלא אוננים שאין אנינות אלא בלב:


With those executed by a Court we do not occupy ourselves in any respect. Their brothers and relatives come and greet the witnesses and judges¹⁵ [as if to say], ‘We have no [ill feelings] against you in our hearts because you gave a true judgment’. They observe no [public] mourning¹⁶ for them but grieve, since grief is felt only in the heart.

footnotes:
¹⁵ Cf. Sanh. 46a (Sonc. ed., p. 305).
¹⁶ i.e. the seven days, thirty days and the twelve months.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:8)


רבי נתן אומר אין בין שתיקה לבכיה כלום:


R. Nathan said: There is no difference between silence and mourning.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ i.e. the silence of the mourners is itself a form of mourning. Hence the persons mentioned in the previous Rule must not even grieve. It is suggested that R. Nathan’s statement was originally a marginal note which found its way into the text.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:9)


אין מברין עליהם שנא׳ (ויקרא יט) לא תאכלו על הדם ב"ד שהרג לא היה טועם כל אותו היום ומניחין אותן לדבר עם אחיהם ועם קרוביהם ובשביל שלא להשהות ומשקין אותן יין ולבונה כדי שלא יצטערו ומלמדין אותן להתוודות שכל המתודה יש לו חלק לעולם הבא שכן מצינו בעכן שאמר לו יהושע (יהושע ז) בני שים נא כבוד לה׳ (אלהיך) [אלהי ישראל] ותן לו תודה והגד נא לי מה עשית אל תכחד ממני ויען עכן את יהושע ויאמר אמנה אנכי חטאתי לה' אלהי ישראל וכזאת וכזאת עשיתי ומה ת"ל וכזאת וכזאת מלמד שמעל בחרם שני פעמים אנכי חטאתי אנכי ולא ביתי אנכי ולא בני מלמד שהתודה באמונה ומניין שכיפר לו וידויו שנאמר ויאמר יהושע מה עכרתנו יעכרך ה׳ ביום הזה ביום הזה אתה עכור ואי אתה עכור לעולם הבא ואומר (דה"א ב) ובני זרח זמרי ואיתן [והימן] וכלכל ודרע כלם חמשה וכי אין אנו יודעים שכולם ה׳ אלא מלמד שאף עכן עמהם לעולם הבא (כיוצא בו הגונב את המכס ואת החרם הרי זה שופך דמים ולא שופך דמים בלבד אלא כאילו עובד עבודת כוכבים ומגלה עריות ומחלל שבתות):


The ‘meal of comfort’¹⁸]’; cf. 2 Sam. 3, 35, *to cause David to eat bread* (*lehabroth*). It was prepared by friends and consisted of lentils and eggs (cf. Sanh. 63a, Sonc. ed., p. 430, n. 6) the round shape of which being a reminder of the revolving wheel of fortune. is not eaten in their case, as it is stated, *Ye shall not eat* [anything] *with the blood*.¹⁹
[The judges of] a Court who ordered the execution of a man used not to eat anything on that day.²⁰
[The condemned] are allowed to converse with their brothers and relatives; and not to delay matters²¹ they are given to drink wine containing frankincense²² so that they should not feel grieved. They are urged²³ to confess, because he who confesses has a portion in the World to Come. We find it so with Achan to whom Joshua said, *My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord, the God of Israel, and make confession unto Him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide nothing from me. And Achan answered Joshua, and said: Of a truth I have sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done*.²⁴ What is the meaning of *and thus and thus?* It teaches that he violated the ban twice.²⁵ [44*b*] *I have sinned*, i.e. I and not my household, I and not my children. This teaches that he truthfully²⁶) is explained as *be’emunah* (‘truthfully’). confessed. And whence do we know that his confession made atonement for him? As it is stated, *And Joshua said: Why hast thou troubled us? The Lord shall trouble thee this day*²⁷. 25.—*this day* art thou to be troubled but thou shalt not be troubled in the World to Come; and it states, *And the sons of Zerah: Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol and Dara: five of them in all.*²⁸ Do we not know that there were *five of them in all?*²⁹ It teaches that Achan will be with them in the world to come.³⁰
Similarly one who steals the tax³¹ or anything devoted [to the Sanctuary] is as if he shed blood; and not only is he as if he shed blood, but he is also as if he worships idols, was guilty of immorality and desecrates the Sabbath.³², p. 198n.]

###### Tractate Semachot 2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:10)


כל הפורש מדרכי צבור אין מתעסקין עמו בכל דבר אחיהם וקרוביהן לובשין לבנים ומתעטפין לבנים ואוכלין ושותין ושמחים שנאבד שונאו של מקום שנא׳ (תהילים קל״ט:כ״א-כ״ב) הלא משנאיך ה׳ אשנא ובתקוממיך אתקוטט (מפני מה ש) תכלית שנאה שנאתים לאויבים היו לי:


We do not occupy ourselves with those who separated themselves from the community³³, I, 5, cf. *Ṭur* Y.D., §345) the reference is to those who discarded all the religious precepts and ceremonies of Judaism. in any respect. Their brothers and relatives clothe themselves in white, wrap themselves in white and eat and drink and rejoice because an enemy of the All-present perished; as it is stated, *Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate Thee? And do not I strive with those that rise up against Thee? I hate them with utmost hatred; I count them mine enemies*.³⁴

³³ According to Maimonides (Hil. ’Ebel
³⁴ Ps. 139, 21f.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:11)


הרוגי מלכות אין מונעין מהן כל דבר מאימתי מתחילין למנות להם משעה שנתייאשו מלשאול אבל לא מלגנוב שכל הגונב הרי זה שופך דמים ולא שופך דמים בלבד אלא כאילו עובד עבודת כוכבים וכו׳:


We do not withhold mourning rites from those executed by the Government.³⁵
When do we begin to count [the days of mourning] for them?³⁶ From the time that [the relatives] despaired in their appeal [for the body to be delivered to them for burial], but not [given up the hope] of stealing it. For he who steals is as if he shed blood, and not only is he as if he had shed blood, but also as if he worshipped idols, etc.³⁷

footnotes:
³⁵ i.e. the occupying power, viz. the Romans.
³⁶ Usually this begins from the moment the grave is filled in, but here the body of the victim was not handed over to the family for burial.
³⁷ This sentence is repeated from the last clause of Rule 9 and has no relevance to the present context.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:12)


מי שנפל לים מי ששטפו נהר מי שאכלתו חיה רעה אין מונעין מהן כל דבר מאימתי מתחילין למנות להם משעה שנתייאשו לבקש מצאוהו אברים אברים אין מונין לו עד שימצא ראשו ורובו רבי יהודה אומר השדרה והגלגולת הן רובו:


Mourning rites are not withheld in any respect from one who fell into the sea, or was washed away by a stream, or killed by a wild beast. When do we begin to count [the days of mourning] for such as these? From the time that hope of finding them has been given up. If they found a body limb by limb, we do not count [the days of mourning] until the head and greater part [of the torso] is found. R. Judah said: The spine and skull constitute the greater part [of the torso].


###### Tractate Semachot 2:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:13)


מי שהיה בעלה צלוב עמה בעיר אשתו צלובה עמו בעיר אביו ואמו צלובין עמו בעיר לא ישרה באותה העיר אא"כ היתה עיר גדולה כאנטוכיא לא ישרה בצד זה אלא ישרה בצד זה עד מתי הוא אסור עד שיכלה הבשר כולו ואין הצורה ניכרת בעצמות:


If one’s husband, wife, father or mother had been impaled³⁸ in his city, one should not continue to reside there³⁹ unless it is a city as big as Antioch.⁴⁰ [Even then] one should not reside in the same side of the city but in another part. Until when is one so forbidden? Until the flesh is completely decomposed and the identity⁴¹ unrecognizable from the bones.

footnotes:
³⁸ By the Roman authorities. Impaling was not a form of execution carried out by the Jews.
³⁹ On seeing him, people will recall the impaling of his relative, and that would be a slight on the memory of the victim.
⁴⁰ The ancient capital of Syria. Since it is a large city, the fact might not be generally known.
⁴¹ lit. ‘the form’.


###### Tractate Semachot 2:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/2:14)


(ב"ש אומרים) המגרש את אשתו לא ישרה עמה לא במבוי ולא בחצר אם היה מבוי של שניהם הופך פתחו לצד אחד ואם היתה חצר של שניהם מפנה זה מפני זה ומפנה אשה מפני איש בד"א בזמן שנשאו והכהנת אע"ג שלא נשאו בד"א מן הנשואין אבל מן האירוסין לא וכן החולץ ליבמתו לא יפנה מפני שאין לבו גס בה:


[Beth Shammai said:]⁴² If a man divorced his wife, he should not live in the same alley or courtyard as she.⁴³ If the alley belonged to both of them, he transfers the door [of his house] to another side; and if the courtyard belonged to both of them, one vacates it on account of the other, and the woman vacates it on account of the man. This rule only applies if she has remarried⁴⁴ and in the case of the [divorced] wife of a *kohen* even if she has not remarried.⁴⁵ may not marry a divorced woman, not even his divorced wife (Lev. 21, 7). It further applies only if she is divorced after marriage and not after betrothal.⁴⁶ Likewise one who has freed his sister-in-law from the levirate marriage⁴⁷ does not vacate on account of her, because he does not feel attracted to her.

⁴² GRA omits. For what follows, cf. Keth. 27b, 28a (Sonc. ed., p. 152).
⁴³ Lest he be tempted to cohabit with her.
⁴⁴ So GRA; V ‘they have married’. After remarriage with another she can never return to her first husband (cf. Deut. 24, 3f).
⁴⁵ A kohen
⁴⁶ Cf. Kallah 1, n. 1.
⁴⁷ Cf. Deut. 25, 5ff.



## Chapter 3

###### Tractate Semachot 3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:1)


בן יומו שמת הרי הוא לאביו ולאמו כחתן שלם לא סוף דבר בן יומו חי אלא אפי׳ יוצא ראשו ורובו בחיים אלא שדברו חכמים בהווה:


A child who lived only one day counts to his father and mother as a fully-grown man.¹, lit. ‘a complete bridegroom’, is based on *ḥathan damim, a bridegroom of blood* (Ex. 4, 25). For the idea that circumcision makes one ‘complete’, cf. Ned. 31b (Sonc. ed., p. 93). [The words] ‘who lived only one day’ are not to be taken as an [irreducible] limit;² even if only his head and the greater part of his body came out viable [he is so counted, but in their formulation of the law] the Sages speak of what actually happens.

¹ With respect to mourning; cf. Nid. 44a (Sonc. ed., p. 303). The phrase ḥathan shalem
² lit. ‘the end of the matter’.


###### Tractate Semachot 3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:2)


ויוצא בחיק נקבר באשה אחת ובשני אנשים אבא שאול אומר באיש א׳ ובשתי נשים אמרו לו אשה אחת מתייחדת עם שני אנשים ואין איש אחד מתייחד עם שתי נשים אין עומדין עליו בשורה ואין אומרין עליו ברכת אבלים עד שיהא בן שלשים יום ובן שלשים יום יוצא באנשים ובנשים ובדלוסקמא ובאגפים עד בן שנים עשר חדש בן שנים עשר חדש יוצא באנשים ובנשים ובדלוסקמא ובכתף עד בן שלש שנים רבי יהודה אומר אם רצה אביו לכבדו מוציאין לו ארון לבית הקברות עד בן שלש שנים:


³ [An infant] who is carried in the arms⁴ is buried by one woman and two men.⁵ Abba Saul said: [The burial may be done] by one man and two women. [The Sages] said to him: One woman may be alone with two men, but one man may not be alone with two women.⁶
[The people at the burial] do not stand in line on account of him and they need not recite the mourner’s benediction on account of him unless he was thirty days old. If he was thirty days old, he is accompanied [to the grave] by men and women and is carried in a case upon the arms⁷ up to the age of twelve months. If he was twelve months old, he is accompanied by men and women and is carried in a case on the shoulder up to the age of three years. R. Judah said: Should his father desire to honour him, they take him out in a coffin to the cemetery even before⁸ he is three years old.

###### Tractate Semachot 3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:3)


בן שלש שנים יוצא במטה רבי עקיבא אומר הוא בן שלש שנים ואיבריו כבן שתים (אינו יוצא במטה) הוא בן שתים ואיבריו בבן שלש יוצא במטה שמעון בן אחי עזריה אומר כל היוצא במטה מקלסין לפניו רבי מאיר אומר משום רבי אלעזר בן עזריה כל שהרבים מכירין אותו מתעסקין עמו וכל שאין הרבים מכירין אותו אין הרבים מתעסקין עמו :


If three years old he is taken out on a bier. R. ‘Aḳiba said: If he is three years old but his limbs are [developed] like those of an infant two years old,⁹ or if he is two years old but his limbs are like those of an infant three years old, he is carried on a bier. Simeon the brother of Azariah said: For anyone who is taken out on a bier the people show their distress.¹⁰ which in Rabbinic Heb. means ‘stamp with the foot’ as a sign of mourning (cf. Ezek. 6, 11).] The Talmud, which gives the name of the Rabbi as Simeon b. Eleazar, uses a different verb; cf. M.Ḳ. 24b (Sonc. ed., p. 151, n. 9). R. Meir said in the name of R. Eleazar b. Azariah: If he is known to the public at large they participate in connection with him [at the funeral], but if not, they do not participate in connection with him.

###### Tractate Semachot 3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:4)


רבי יהודה משום רבי אלעזר בן עזריה אומר אף שכיניו לענין הספד מספידין לעניים בני שלש ולעשירים בני ארבע רבי עקיבא אומר לעניים בני שש ולעשירים בני שבע בני עשירים בבני חכמים בני חכמים כבני מלכים (מתעסקין עמהם):


R. Judah said in the name of R. Eleazar b. Azariah: For the purpose of a memorial address it is sufficient that his neighbours [know him]. In the case of the poor a memorial address is delivered for a child of three,¹¹ and in the case of the rich for a child of four. R. ‘Aḳiba said: In the case of the poor, for a child of six and in the case of the rich for a child of seven. The children of the rich are like the children of scholars and the children of scholars like the children of kings.¹²

footnotes:
¹¹ The child being a greater joy to poor parents who have few pleasures in life, and so his death is a greater loss.
¹² The children are praised in the memorial address to honour the parents.


###### Tractate Semachot 3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:5)


תינוק שיודע לישא וליתן יוצא במעשה עצמו אם אין לו מעשים יוצא במעשה אבותיו ואם אין לאבותיו מעשים יוצא במעשה קרוביו הכלה יוצאת בין בכבוד אביה בין בכבוד חמיה מפני (שמעלין בכבוד ולא מורידין) לא מוסיפין בתחילה אבל מוסיפין על העיקר:


In the case of a child of developed intelligence¹³ we dwell [in the memorial address for him] on his own [good] deeds, but if he has no such deeds we dwell on the deeds of his parents; and if his parents have no such deeds we dwell on the deeds of his relatives. In the case of a bride we dwell on the honour of her father or father-in-law, because she rises [in esteem] with him¹⁴ but does not fall with him. We may not ascribe merits to one who has none,¹⁵ but we may magnify those which he possessed.¹⁶

¹⁴ viz. her father-in-law. The reading of GRA and H is adopted.
¹⁵ lit. ‘we do not add from the start’. Cf. Ber. 62a (Sonc. ed., p. 390), ‘As the dead are called to account [for their deeds], so are funeral orators [who exaggerate the merits of the dead]’.
¹⁶ lit. ‘we may add to the stock’.


###### Tractate Semachot 3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:6)


בירושלים היו אומרים עשה לפני מיטתך וביהודה היו אומרים עשה לאחר מיטתך (של) שבירושלים לא היו אומרים לפני מיטתו של מת אלא דבריו של מת וביהודה היו אומרים דברים שיש בו ודברים שאין בו המהלכין אחר המטה לא היו עונין אחריהם ואומרים אלא דברים שיש בו (ודברים שאין בו). מבן שלש ועד בן שלשים יוצא כחתן מבן שלשים עד בן ארבעים יוצא כאח מבן ארבעים ועד בן חמשים יוצא כאב:


¹⁷ In Jerusalem there was a saying, ‘Perform actions [which can be lamented] in front of your bier’,¹⁸ and in Judea there was a saying, ‘Perform actions [which can be lamented] behind your bier’. For in Jerusalem they recounted in front of a dead man’s bier only the merits which he possessed; but in Judea they recounted merits which he possessed and did not possess. They, however, who walked behind the bier only repeated after them the merits which he possessed.¹⁹
[One who dies] between the ages of three and thirty [is mourned] like a bridegroom;²⁰ between thirty and forty like a brother;²¹ between forty and fifty like a father.²²

¹⁹ The emended text of GRA and H is followed.
²⁰ Since he may be unmarried.
²¹ He may be married but childless.
²² As one mourned by his children.


###### Tractate Semachot 3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Semachot/r/3:7)


רשב"א אומר מבן שלשים ועד בן ארבעים אם יש לו בנים או לרוב בני גילו בנים יוצא כאב ואם לאו יוצא כאח מבן מ׳ ועד בן נ׳ אם יש לו בני בנים או לרוב בני גילו בנים יוצא כאב ואם לאו יוצא כאח:


R. Simeon b. Eleazar said: Between thirty and forty, if he has children or the majority of his own age have children, [he is mourned] like a father; if not, like a brother. Between forty and fifty, if he has children or the majority of his own age have grandchildren, [he is mourned] like a grandfather, if not like a father.²³
