ואומר ג"פ סימן טוב סימן טוב [תהיה] לכל ישראל ברוך יוצרך ברוך עושך ברוך קונך ברוך בוראך ורוקד ג׳ רקידות כנגדה ואומר ג"פ כשם שאני רוקד כנגדך ואיני נוגע ביך כך אם ירקדו אחרים כנגדי [להזיקני] לא יגעו בי תפול עליהם אימתה ופחד ולמפרע אמן אמן סלה הללויה ואומר לחבירו ג"פ שלום וילך לביתו בלב טוב והדא היא לכל מפסיקין לראשי חדשים:


Then one says three times, ‘An auspicious omen, an auspicious omen, shall it be for all Israel. Blessed be He Who formed thee, blessed be Thy Maker, blessed be thy Possessor, blessed be thy Creator’. Turning in the direction of the moon,⁷ he jumps three times and exclaims three times, ‘As I jump towards thee but do not⁸ touch thee, so if others should jump against me to hurt me may they not touch me. Let terror and dread fall upon them and may this be retrospective, Amen, Amen, Selah. Praise ye the Lord’. He then says ‘Peace’ three times to his fellow and goes home with a cheerful heart. That is [the conclusion of the regulations] concerning the interruptions for New Moons.⁹

What are the regulations respecting *Ḥanukkah?*¹⁰’, a reference to XVII, 2 where *Ḥanukkah* was first introduced in this set of regulations with the statement, ‘The sequence … is interrupted for … *Ḥanukkah’*. The Rabbis said: On the twenty-fifth day of *Kislew*¹¹ the *Ḥanukkah* lamp is kindled,¹² and it is forbidden to use an old lamp;¹³ but if a person has only an old lamp, he must thoroughly heat it in fire;¹⁴ nor may [the *Ḥanukkah* lamp] be moved¹⁵ from its place before it is extinguished.¹⁶ light, commemorating the miracles which led up to the celebration (cf. Rule 5), is sacred, is only to be looked at and must not be used for any other purpose.

###### Tractate Soferim 20:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:4)


מצות הדלקתו משקיעת החמה עד שיכלה הרגל מן השוק ואע"פ שאין ראייה לדבר זכר לדבר (שמות י״ג:כ״ב) לא ימיש עמוד הענן יומם ואם הדליקו ביום אין נאותין ממנו ואי׳ מברכין עליו שכך אמרו אין מברכין על הנר עד שיאותו לאורו ואין חוששין לפתילתו להחליפו עד שיכלה:


The commandment to kindle it extends from sunset until the last person has left¹⁷ the street.¹⁸ And, although there is no actual proof,¹⁹ there is an allusion to it: *The pillar of cloud by day* [*and the pillar of fire by night*,] *departed not*.²⁰ lamp, was intended to shed light, appeared in the night only If it was lit in daytime, one must derive no benefit from it, nor may the benediction be said over it; for so [the Rabbis] said: No benediction is to be pronounced over the lamp before one enjoys its light. There is no need, however, to be concerned about changing the wick before it has been used up.

¹⁸ The light is intended to serve as a public demonstration, but at such a late hour there are no passers-by to see it.

###### Tractate Soferim 20:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:5)


נר חנוכה מצוה להניחו בפתח הסמוך לרה"ר שתהא מזוזה בימין ונר חנוכה משמאל לקיים מה שנאמר (ש"ה ז) מה יפית ומה נעמת מה יפית במזוזה ומה נעמת בנר חנוכה ונרות כב"ה משום מעלין בקדש ולא מורידין כעין ימים היוצאין:


It is a religious precept to place the *Ḥanukkah* lamp by the door which is near to the public domain,²¹ in such a manner that the *mezuzah* should be on the right hand and the *Ḥanukkah* lamp on the left, to fulfil what is stated, *How fair and how pleasant art thou*²²—*how fair* with the *mezuzah* and *how pleasant* with the *Ḥanukkah* lamp. The number²³ of lights [for each night] is in accordance with the ruling of the School of Hillel,²⁴ because in sacred matters one should proceed to a higher grade²⁵ but not descend to a lower one,²⁶ [and also because the number of lights should] correspond to the days [of the Festival] as they pass.

²² Cant. 7, 7.
²³ Inserted by GRA, wanting in V, M and H.
²⁴ One light on the first night, two on the second, and so on, until eight lights burn on the eighth and last night of the Festival.
²⁵ Adding lights on the succeeding nights.
²⁶ As would happen if the number were to be reduced from eight on the first night to one on the last in accordance with the view of Beth Shammai.


###### Tractate Soferim 20:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:6)


וכיצד מברכין ביום ראשון המדליק מברך שלש והרואה מברך שתים בא"י אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו להדליק נר ואומר הנרות האלו אנו מדליקין על הישועות ועל הניסים ועל הנפלאות אשר עשית לאבותינו ע"י כהניך הקדושים וכל (מצות) שמונת ימי חנוכה הנרות האלו קודש ואין לנו רשות להשתמש בהן אלא לראותן בלבד כדי להודות לשמך על נפלאותיך ועל נסיך ועל ישועתך בא"י שהחיינו ואומר שעשה נסים לאבותינו אלו למדליק אבל לרואה אינו אומר ביום ראשון אלא שתים שהחיינו ושעשה מכאן ואילך [המדליק] מברך להדליק ושעשה והרואה אומר (אשר עשה) [שעשה] נסים:


In what manner are the benedictions²⁷ lights. said? On the first day, the person who kindles [the lamp] says three benedictions while the onlooker says two. The person who kindles says, ‘Blessed art Thou, O Lord,²⁸ Who hast sanctified us by Thy commandments and hast given us command to kindle the light of *Ḥanukkah*’. Then²⁹ he says, ‘We kindle these lights on account of the deliverances and the miracles and the wonders which Thou didst work for our fathers, by means of Thy holy priests.³⁰ During all the eight days of *Ḥanukkah* these lights are sacred, and it is not permitted to make any profane use of them but we are only to look at them, in order that we may give thanks unto Thy name for thy wonders, Thy miracles and Thy deliverances’. [The third benediction is] ‘Blessed art Thou, O Lord, Who hast kept us in life’.³¹ [Before this] he says, ‘Who wroughtest miracles for our fathers’.³² These benedictions are for the person who kindles the lights, but the onlooker says on the first day only two benedictions: ‘Who hast kept us in life’ and ‘Who wroughtest miracles’. From that day onwards the person who kindles the lights says, ‘To kindle’ and ‘Who wroughtest’, while the onlooker only says ‘Who wroughtest miracles’.

###### Tractate Soferim 20:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:7)


החזן צריך לומר אתה קדוש בשמנה עשר של חנוכה וכן בראשי חדשים וכן בחולו של מועד מפני שכתוב בהן עולת תמיד ותני רבי חייא כל יום שאין בו מוסף אין בו קדוש חוץ מן החנוכה שאע"פ שאין בה מוסף יש בה קדוש מפני (מה) שיש בה הלל וי"א אף בפורים מפני שיש בה מגילה:


The precentor must say, ‘Thou art holy’³³. It appears that, instead of beginning with ‘We will sanctify’ (P.B., p. 45) or ‘We will reverence’ (P.B., p. 160), there was a custom to begin with ‘Thou art holy’ on Sabbath and Festivals. Rule 7 extends this practice to some of the less important days as specified below. It has also been suggested to read, instead of *’attah ḳadosh* (‘Thou art holy’) *’eth haḳḳedushshah* (‘the *ḳedushshah*’). on the eight days³⁴ of *Ḥanukkah*, and similarly on New Moons and on the intermediate days of a Festival,³⁵ because *beside*³⁶ *the continual burnt-offering*³⁷ 24 (on the intermediate days of Passover); and *ibid.* XXIX, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31, 34 (on those of Tabernacles). is written in connection with them. And R. Hiyya learnt: On any day on which there is a musaf *ḳedushshah* is said except on *Ḥanukkah* on which *ḳedushshah* is said although there is no *musaf* on it, because *Hallel* is included [in the service]. Some maintain [that it is said] on *Purim* also, because the scroll of Esther is read on it.

###### Tractate Soferim 20:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:8)


ואומרים בהודייה והודאת פלאות ותשועת כהנים אשר עשית בימי מתתיהו בן יוחנן כהן גדול וחשמונאי ובניו וכן עשה עמנו ה' אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו נסים ונפלאות ונודה לשמך לנצח בא"י הטוב ונסים מרדכי ואסתר מזכירין אותן בהודייה ושניהן נזכרין בברכת המזון:


In the benediction for Thanksgiving³⁸ we include [on *Ḥanukkah*] ‘and thanks for the wonders and salvation of Thy priests which Thou hast wrought in the days of Mattathias, son of Joḥanan, High Priest, and the Hasmoneans his sons. So also, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, perform for us miracles and wonders, and we will give thanks unto Thy name for ever. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, Who art all-good’.³⁹ The miracles [of the days] of Mordecai and Esther are also mentioned [on *Purim*] in the benediction for Thanksgiving. Both⁴⁰ and *Purim*. are likewise mentioned in the Grace after meals.⁴¹

###### Tractate Soferim 20:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:9)


וגומרין את הלל כל שמנת ימי חנוכה בג׳ פרקים הראשונים אין משיבין ואין צ"ל לשאול בשנים האחרונים שואלין מפני היראה [ומשיבין] מפני השלום ומפני הכבוד ואלו הן שלשה ראשונים הללו עבדי ה׳ בצאת ישראל אהבתי שנים האחרונים הללו את ה׳ הודו לה׳ וצריך לברך בתחילתן ולקרותן בנעימה דתני ר׳ שמעון בן יהוצדק ימים שמנה עשרה ולילה אחד יחיד גומר בהן את ההלל ואלו הן שמנת ימי חנוכה וי"ט של עצרת וי"ט הראשון של פסח ולילו ובגולה עשרים ואחד יום ושתי לילות מצוה מן המובחר לקרות הלל בשני לילות של גליות ולברך עליהן ולאומרן בנעימה לקיים מה שנאמר (תהילים ל״ד:ד׳) ונרוממה שמו יחדיו וכשהוא קורא אותו בביתו אינו צריך לברך שכבר בירך ברבים:


The whole *Hallel*⁴² is recited during all the eight days of *Ḥanukkah*. During [the recital of] the first two⁴³ chapters one may not return greetings, and there is no need to say that one must not give greetings. During [the recital of] the last two chapters one may give greetings out of fear;⁴⁴ during the two middle chapters⁴⁵ [greetings may be given] for the sake of peace or out of respect. The following are the first two chapters: *Praise, O ye servants of the Lord*⁴⁶ and *When Israel went forth*.⁴⁷ CXIV. V, M and H adds Ps. 115 as the third. The two middle ones are: *Not unto us*⁴⁸ CXV; ‘the two middle … *us’* is the reading of GRA. and *I love*.⁴⁹ CXVI. The last two are: *O praise the Lord*⁵⁰ CXVII. and *O give thanks unto the Lord*.⁵¹ CXVIII. It is also necessary to say a benediction⁵²’ (P.B., p. 219). before them and read them melodiously. For R. Simeon b. Jehoẓadaḳ said:⁵³ On eighteen days and one night the individual reads the whole *Hallel* and they are: the eight days of *Ḥanukkah*, the eight days of Tabernacles,⁵⁴ the Festival of Solemn Assembly, the first Festival day of Passover and the night preceding it.⁵⁵ was recited during the sacrifice of the Paschal lamb on the eve of Passover.] In the Diaspora⁵⁶ [the whole *Hallel* is read on] twenty-one days and two nights. The most proper way of performing the commandment is to read the *Hallel* psalms on the two nights [of Passover] in the Diaspora in the Synagogue,⁵⁷ ritual. ‘In the Synagogue’ is inserted by GRA but omitted by V, M and H. to say the benediction over them, and to recite them melodiously to fulfil what is stated, *And let us exalt His name together*.⁵⁸ When, however, one reads [the *Hallel*] at home,⁵⁹. there is no need to say the benediction because it has already been said in the congregational service.⁶⁰ in the home.

ואחר כך מוציאין ספר וקורין בנשיאים ויהי המקריב ביום הראשון וכן לכל יום יומו עד יום השמיני ובשבת שבתוכו קוראו ויהי ביום כלות משה עד כן עשה את המנורה וכן ביום השמיני עד וזה מעשה המנורה כל הפסוק ומפטיר בותשלם כל המלאכה (מלכים א ז׳:נ״א):


A scroll⁶¹ is then taken out⁶². and we read in the section of the princes,⁶³ *And he that presented his offering the first day was;*⁶⁴ 12-17. and likewise for each day [the corresponding section of the offering] of that day,⁶⁵ day corresponding to the respective number of the days of the offerings of the princes. until the eighth day. (אין) מקדימין בשמנת ימי חנוכה לומר ביום השני ביום השלישי ביום הרביעי ביום החמישי ביום הששי ביום השביעי ביום השמיני כדי לגמור עשרה פסוקים:


During the eight days of *Ḥanukkah* we read the following one day earlier:⁷² *On the second day*,⁷³ *On the third day*,⁷⁴ 24-29. *On the fourth day*,⁷⁵ 30-35. *On the fifth day*,⁷⁶ 36-41. *On the sixth day*,⁷⁷ 42-47. *On the seventh day*,⁷⁸ 48-53. *On the eighth day*,⁷⁹ 54-59. so as to complete ten verses.⁸⁰.

###### Tractate Soferim 20:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/20:12)


בזמן שחל ר"ח טבת להיות באחד בשבת ביום ראשון קורין בענין ר"ח תחלה שלשה והרביעי של חנוכה שכל התדיר מחבירו תדיר קודם והוא קודם את חבירו אבל ביום שני אינו כן אלא קורים שלשה בשל חנוכה והרביעי בשל ר"ח שאין חשבון חודש מיום שני אלא בזמן שהשנים כסדרן דר׳ יצחק סחורה שאל את ר׳ יהושע נפחא ר"ח טבת שחל להיות בשבת במה קורין לענין כלות שלמה והמפטיר בשל שבת ור"ח חל להיות בחול קורין ביום הראשון שלשה [בשל] ר"ח [והרביעי] בשל חנוכה [שכל] התדיר מחבירו (תדיר) קודם את חבירו והואיל וקרא תחלה בשל ר"ח ביום השני קורא ג׳ לחנוכה והרביעי בשל ר"ח ובראשי חדשיכם עד שישלים (כל השיטה) ולמה כן שלא בא הרביעי אלא מחמת מוסף של ר"ח הרי מפסיקין לחנוכה:


When the New Moon of *Ṭebeth*⁸¹. falls on a Sunday, three persons read on the first day⁸² in the passage of the New Moon first, while the fourth reads the passage of *Ḥanukkah*, because that which is more frequent takes precedence,⁸³ once a year. and so [the reading for the New Moon] precedes the other. On the second day, however, the order is not the same, but three persons read the passage of *Ḥanukkah* while the fourth reads that of the New Moon, because on the previous day the section of the New Moon had been read first.⁸⁴ [This is the procedure] because R. Isaac Seḥorah asked R. Isaac Nappaḥa, ‘Which do we read [first]⁸⁵ when the New Moon of *Ṭebeth* falls on a Sabbath?’ [He replied,] ‘In the section of *kalloth Mosheh*,⁸⁶ (Num. 7, 1). The extent of the reading is given in Rule 10 above. while the *mafṭir* reads⁸⁷ the passages relating to the Sabbath and the New Moon.⁸⁸ If it falls on a week-day, on the first day [of the New Moon] three persons read [the passage] for the New Moon, the fourth reading that of *Ḥanukkah;* because that which is more frequent takes precedence. As, however, the section of the New Moon was read first,⁸⁹ three persons are to be called up on the second day for the reading of the *Ḥanukkah* section,⁹⁰. while the fourth reads⁹¹ the section of the New Moon, viz. *And in your new moons* to the end of the section.⁹² Why is this so?⁹³ Because it is only on account of the *musaf* of New Moon⁹⁴ there is no *musaf*. This argument cannot be applied to the first day of New Moon because it is the second day which begins the month, the first being the last day of the old month. that a fourth person is added.⁹⁵ Behold [we have concluded the regulations respecting] the interruption which is made for the sake of *Ḥanukkah*.⁹⁶

###### Tractate Soferim 21:1

מפסיקים לפורים כמנהג רבותינו שבמערב להתענות שלשה ימי צום מרדכי ואסתר פרודות ולאחר פורים שני וחמישי ושני:


[Reverting to the sequence of the readings which] is interrupted for *Purim*.¹ It is² the custom of our Rabbis in the West to afflict themselves by fasting the three days of the fast of Mordecai and Esther³ intermittently, viz. after *Purim* on the Monday, Thursday and Monday.

###### Tractate Soferim 21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:2)


ולמה אין מתענין אותן בחדש ניסן מפני שבאחד בניסן הוקם המשכן וי"ב נשיאים הקריבו קרבנם לי"ב יום יום לכל שבט ושבט וכל א׳ היה עושה ביומו י"ט וכן לעתיד לבא עתיד המקדש להבנות בניסן לקיים מה שנאמר (קהלת א׳:ט׳) אין כל חדש תחת השמש:


And why do we not fast in the month of *Nisan?* Because on the first of *Nisan* the Tabernacle was erected⁴ and twelve princes offered their sacrifices during [the first] twelve days, a day for each tribe,⁵ and everyone held a festival on his day.⁶ and the fifteenth, on which Passover begins, only two days intervene; therefore they, too, are regarded as festival days. The Passover ending on the twenty-first (in the land of Israel) or on the twenty-second (in the Diaspora), only eight or nine days of the month remain. As by far the greater part of the month was made up of festival days, the entire month is treated as a festival season in which fasting is prohibited. Furthermore, in the time to come the Sanctuary will be rebuilt in *Nisan*, to confirm what is stated, *There is nothing new under the sun*.⁷

footnotes:
⁴ Cf. Ex. 40, 2.
⁵ Cf. Num. 7, 1ff.
⁶ Between the twelfth of Nisan
⁷ Eccl. 1, 9.


###### Tractate Soferim 21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:3)


לפיכך אין אומרין תחנונים כל ימי ניסן ואין מתענין עד שיעבור ניסן אלא הבכורות שמתענין בערב הפסח והצנועין בשביל המצה כדי שיכנסו בה בתאוה והתלמידים מתענין בו שני וחמישי מפני חילול השם ומפני כבוד ההיכל שנשרף:


For this reason⁸ no supplications⁹ are offered on any of the days of *Nisan* and there is no fasting until *Nisan* has passed. The only exception is [the fast of] the firstborn who fast on the eve of Passover.¹⁰ The very pious also fast on that day on account of the unleavened bread, in order that they shall begin to eat it¹¹. Lit. ‘that they shall enter it’. with relish.¹² Scholars fast on Mondays and Thursdays [throughout the year] on account of the desecration of the name of God¹³ and for the honour of the Temple which was burnt.

footnotes:
⁸ That most of the month contained festival days.
⁹ This refers in particular to the prayer, ‘And He, being merciful’, etc. (P.B., pp. 57-65).
¹⁰ In thanksgiving for the deliverance of the Israelite firstborn on Passover eve when Egypt’s firstborn perished (Ex. 12, 29).
¹¹ On the evening preceding the fifteenth of Nisan
¹² In honour and appreciation of the commandment.
¹³ By the heathens who destroyed Jerusalem.


###### Tractate Soferim 21:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:4)


בד"א בצנעה אבל להזכיר בציבור אסור עד שיעבור ניסן. ובאחד באדר משמיעין על השקלים ולמה באחד באדר שהיה צפוי וגלוי וידוע לפני מי שאמר והיה העולם שיהיה המן עתיד לשקול על ישראל לפיכך הקדים ואמר למשה (שהיו ק׳) שקלי ישראל קודמין להמן וצריכין ישראל לתת שקליהם לפני שבת זכור ואסור לומר עליהם לשם כופר אלא לשם נדבה צריכין להספיק מים ומזון לאחיהם עניים משום קובלין ומתנות לאביונים ויש שמספיקין לחם ויין ויש שמספיקין לחם ודגים ומ"מ לא יפחות משתי מתנות אפילו חטים ופולים:


To what does the foregoing apply? To fasting in private, but it is forbidden to proclaim a public fast until *Nisan* has passed.
On the first day of *Adar* a public proclamation is made regarding the shekels.¹⁴ Why on the first of *Adar?* Because it was foreseen, revealed and known before Him Who spoke and the world came into being that Haman would in time to come weigh [shekels] against Israel.¹⁵ He, therefore, forestalled him and instructed Moses that the shekels of Israel should precede Haman’s. It is required that Israel shall give their shekels before [43*b*] the Sabbath of Remember;¹⁶ when the *mafṭir* reads the passage beginning *Remember* (Deut. 25, 17-19). and it is forbidden to say of them¹⁷ that they are ‘for a ransom’ [but must be given] for a freewill-offering. From the proceeds water and food should be supplied for their poor brethren on account of a sacrifice¹⁸ with GRA. V has ‘on account of complaints’ (*ḳoblin*). [M has *ḳislin* which Krauss, *Lehnwörter*, p. 531, renders ‘feast’.] and gifts to the poor.¹⁹ Some supply bread and wine, others supply bread and fish; in any event not less than two gifts²⁰ speaks of *gifts*, in the plural, which indicates not less than two. should be given, although they consist only of wheat and beans.

¹⁵ Cf. Esth. 3, 9.
¹⁶ The Sabbath before Purim
¹⁷ The half-shekels.
¹⁸ Reading ḳorban
¹⁹ Cf. Esth. 9, 22.
²⁰ Since Esth. loc. cit.


###### Tractate Soferim 21:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:5)


בי"ד ובט"ו יושבין שולחנות של חבירים בכפרים בי"ד ובכרכים בט"ו בו:


²¹ (“associates”, i.e. men who observed levitical purity) were set up (for changing foreign currency into half-shekels); in the villages on the fourteenth and in the walled cities on the fifteenth’. In villages and towns [the *Megillah*] is read on the fourteenth [of *Adar*], and in walled cities²² on the fifteenth of the month.

###### Tractate Soferim 21:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:6)


קורין בויבא עמלק ואע"פ שאין בה [אלא] תשעה פסוקין אין מתחילין בוישמע יתרו אלא ראשון קורא שלשה פסוקים ויבא עמלק ויאמר משה ויעש יהושע. ושני קורא והיה כאשר ירים משה וידי משה ויחלש יהושע שלישי קורא ויאמר ה׳ ויבן משה ויאמר כי יד על כס יה מלחמה לה׳ ומניחין ספר תורה במקומו ואומר (תהילים קי״ג:ב׳) יהי שם ה׳ מבורך מעתה ועד עולם וקדיש (שאין לך קריאה שטעון קדיש עד שיחזיר אלא של שבת בלבד מפני המפטיר ועל הנביא לאחר שמניחין ס"ת במקומו אומר קדיש וקדיש למה אלא ללמד) שאין אומרי׳ קדיש לא בראשי חדשים ולא בתעניות ולא בשני ובחמישי ולא בחולו של מועד ולא בשמונת ימי חנוכה ולא בפורים עד שמחזירים ספר תורה למקומו בשעה שהעם עומדים והן עונין אמן יהא שמיה רבה בכוונה בעמידה :


We read²³ in the morning service. from *Then came Amalek;*²⁴ and although it consists of only nine verses,²⁵ we do not begin²⁶ *Now Jethro … heard*,²⁷. but the first [to be called up] reads three verses, viz. *Then came Amalek … And Moses said … So Joshua did;*²⁸ XVII, 8-10. the second reads *And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand … But Moses’ hands … And Joshua discomfited;*²⁹ 11-13. the third reads *And the Lord said … And Moses built … And he said: The hand upon the throne of the Lord: the Lord will have war*.³⁰ 14-16. The scroll of the Torah is then put back in its place, and *Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for ever*³¹ and *ḳaddish* are said;³² until after he restores [the scroll in the ark] except that of the Sabbath alone on account of the *mafṭir* and over the Prophet. After the scroll of the Torah is put in its place one says *ṭaddish;* and why *ṭaddish?* Only to teach’. GRA transposes this to the end of the Rule in an emended version. because neither on New Moons, nor fast days, nor Mondays and Thursdays, nor on the intermediate days of a Festival, nor the eight days of *Ḥanukkah*, nor *Purim* is *ḳaddish* said until after the Torah scroll had been restored to its place, while the people stand and respond ‘Amen, let His great name’, etc.,³³ with devotion and [still] standing. Furthermore, you have no reading that requires a *ḳaddish* before [the scroll] is put back except that of Sabbath and Festivals alone, [when it is said] before the *hafṭarah* is read in the Prophet.

###### Tractate Soferim 21:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:7)


רב הונא אמר שלש קריות שבתורה לא יפחתו להם מעשרה פסוקים חזקיה אמר כנגד עשרת הדברות והתנינן ביום הראשון [בראשית] ויהי רקיע דהא לית בהון אלא תמניא רב אידי אמר איתפלגין בה כהנא ואשי חד אמר חוזר וחד אמר חותך מאן דאמר חוזר חוזר לשני פסוקים ומאן דאמר חותך ויהי ערב ויהי בקר פסוק בפני עצמו הוא והתנינן בשני יהי רקיע ויקוו המים מאן דאמר חוזר חוזר לשני פסוקים ומאן דאמר חותך אפילו חותך לית בהון התיב רבי פוליפא בר רבי פריט קמית ר׳ יונה הרי פרשת עמלק אמר לא שנויה היא היא סדרה של יום התיב רבי אליעזר ברבי מקום המפטיר בנביא לא יפחות מעשרים ואחד פסוקים (מדלגין בנביא ואין מדלגין בתורה שאפילו אם דלג פסוק אחד ולא קראו והחזיר את התורה ואמר קדיש חוזר ופותח ומברך וקורא הוא ושנים אחרים):


R. Huna said: For three readings in the Torah³⁴ not less than ten verses must be allotted.³⁵ Hezekiah³⁶ explained [the reason:³⁷ The number] corresponds to the Ten Commandments. But have we not learned in a Mishnah:³⁸ ‘On Sunday [the men of the *ma‘amad* read] *In the beginning*³⁹ and *Let there be a firmament*’⁴⁰ 5-8. although they contain not more than eight verses?⁴¹ R. Iddi said: Kahana and Ashë differ [on the method of procedure],⁴² one holding that [the reader] goes back, and the other maintaining that he cuts.⁴³ According to him who holds that ‘[the reader] goes back’, he repeats two verses;⁴⁴ and according to him who maintains that ‘he cuts’, *And there was evening and there was morning*⁴⁵ is a verse on its own.⁴⁶ But have we not learned in [the same] Mishnah: ‘On Monday [the reading of the *ma‘amad* was] *Let there be a firmament*⁴⁷ and *Let the waters … be gathered together’?*⁴⁸ 9-13, five verses. Now, according to him who holds that ‘[the reader] goes back’, he goes back over two verses, but according to him who maintains that ‘he cuts’, even if he does so, there are not ten⁴⁹ verses!⁵⁰, etc., forms the whole of verse 13 and cannot be reckoned as two verses as in the case of verses 5 and 8. R. Polippa b. R. Pariṭ raised an objection before R. Jonah,⁵¹ ‘Behold the section of Amalek!’⁵², which consists only of nine verses. ‘This is different’, he replied, ‘since⁵³ it is the prescribed portion for the day’.⁵⁴ R. Eliezer b. R. Maḳom raised an objection:⁵⁵ [It has been taught,] ‘He who reads the *hafṭarah* from the Prophet shall read not less than twenty-one verses’,⁵⁶, he must unroll it again, say the benedictions, and read that verse and the two verses which follow it’. This is a repetition of XI, 2, 6. but [if R. Huna’s ruling] is valid, twenty-three verses should be required, ten for the first three,⁵⁷ ten for the second three, and three for the last one!⁵⁸

V omits it but inserts in brackets: ‘It is permitted to skip in a Prophet but not in the Torah, because if [a reader] skipped even one verse by not reading it, and restored the scroll [to the ark] and recited ḳaddish
⁵⁷ In accordance with R. Huna’s ruling above that ‘for three readings … no less than ten verses must be allotted’.

No reply is given to the objection, but it is possible to provide the following explanation: Only when no more than three persons are called up is it necessary to allot ten verses, but when the number of persons is more than three, as, e.g., on the Sabbath when not less than seven persons must be called to the Torah, three verses for each person or twenty-one in all are sufficient.


###### Tractate Soferim 21:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:8)


מקום שנהגו לקרות את המגילה שני ימים קורין לילה ויום קורין הכל כמנהג המדינה וחייבין כל ישראל לקרותה בלשון הקודש:


Where the custom is to read the *Megillah* on two days⁵⁹. it should be so read, [and where it is customary to read it] in the night and in the day, it should be so read; all depends on the practice of the country. Furthermore, all Israel must read it in the holy tongue.⁶⁰

⁵⁹ The fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar
⁶⁰ In Hebrew.


###### Tractate Soferim 21:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Soferim/r/21:9)


האדם הגדול בענקים (הגדול היה אברהם אבינו גבוה יותר מענק) בענקים זה אברהם אבינו שהיה גבוה קומתו כנגד שבעים וארבעה אנשים ואכילתו ושתייתו כך היה כנגד שבעים וארבעה אנשים וכוחו כן מה עשה נטל שבעה עשר בני קטורה ובנה להן כרך של ברזל והכניסן לתוכה והשמש מעולם לא נכנס בתוכה מפני שהיא גבוה הרבה ומסר להן דיסקרין של אבנים טובות ומרגליות ומשתמשין לעתיד לבא כשעתיד הקב"ה להחפיר חמה ולבנה כמה דכתיב (ישעיהו כ״ד:כ״ג) וחפרה הלבנה ובושה החמה שמהן עתידין לשמש: עוג הוא אליעזר ופרסות רגליו אברהם אבינו היה טומנו בכף ידו ופעם אחת גער בו ומיראתו נפל ממנו שינו ונטלו אברהם אבינו ועשאו מטות שהן של שן והיה ישן שם ויש אומרים כסא עשאו וישב בו כל ימיו ומי נתנו לאברהם נמרוד והלך עוג ובנה ששים עיירות והקטן שבהן היה גובהן ששים מיל שנאמר (דברים ג׳:ד׳) ששים עיר כל חבל ארגוב ומה היה אכילתו אלף שורים וכן כל מין חיה ושתייתו אלף מידות ומה שהיתה טיפת זריעתו שלשים וששה ליטרין (וכן לכל דורות). תני מה עשה יעקב אבינו כשהביאו בניו את הכתונת בדם לא האמין להן כל עיקר מנין דכתיב (בראשית ל״ז:ל״ה) וימאן להתנחם לפי שאין מקבלין תנחומין על חי אבל שמת הוא מעצמו משתכח מן הלב שנאמר (תהילים ל״א:י״ג) נשכחתי כמת מלב ומה עשה הלך בהרים וחצב שנים עשר אבנים והעמידן שורה וכתב על כל אחת ואחת שם שבטו ושם מזלו ושם ירחו היאך (אלא) הוא על (האחת) האבן [האחת] ראובן טלה ניסן וכן לכל אבן ואבן התחיל משמעון ואמר להו גוזרני עליכם שתעמדו לראובן ולא עמדו לשמעון ולא עמדו לכל שבט ושבט ולא עמדו האבנים וכיון שהזכיר להם שם יוסף מיד עמדו וכרעו לפני אבן יוסף ועדיין לא ברור הדבר לו שהוא חי ועוד הלך ובחן באלומות כדעת הראשון וכתב עליהן שמות השבטים והמזלות והחדשים ואמר להן גוזרני עליכם שתשתחוו ללוי שהוא לבוש אורים ותומים [ולא] עמדו ליהודה שהוא מלך ולא עמדו וכשהזכיר להן יוסף עמדו וכרעו כולן ליוסף ועדיין לא נתברר כל עיקר שהוא חי אלא מן המשמרות אלישב כהן אלקנה שקנה פוטיפר (בראשית ל״ט:א׳) ויוסף הורד מצרימה ויקנהו פוטיפר וגו׳ (שם מא) (ויקרא פרעה שם יוסף צפנת פענח וגו׳). בת שלש שנים (ושלשה ימים) היתה רבקה כשיצאת מבית אביה שכן דרכן של מלכים כשתוליד להן בת מנהגן לשמוע לאחר ג׳ ימים ולפי שלא שמע אביה ולכך נעשה לה נס שלא תטמא שכך היה מנהגן של ארמיים לשכוב עם בנותיהם בתולות ואחר כך משיאין אותן (על שם דכתיב (שם כד) ואיש לא ידעה ואין איש אלא אביה). בת שש שנים היתה דינה כשהולידה את אסנת משכם מנין שש שנים של שכר הצאן שעבד יעקב אבינו ללבן והוסיף עשרים שנה שמת מכאן ואילך יוסיף המבין דעת וירד מיכאל והוליכה לבית פוטיפר:


⁶¹ *The greatest man among the Anakim*⁶²*—among the Anakim* refers to our father Abraham whose height was equal to that of seventy-four men; his eating and drinking were of a similar proportion, equal to those of seventy-four men; so too his strength. What did he do?⁶³. He removed the sixteen⁶⁴ sons of Keturah, built for them a walled city of iron and settled them in it. The sun never penetrated into it because it was exceedingly high, so Abraham handed to them disks of precious stones and pearls of which use will be made⁶⁵ in the hereafter when the Holy One, blessed be He, will cause the sun and moon to be confounded, as it is written, *When the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed*,⁶⁶ because use will be made of these [disks as luminaries].
Og⁶⁷ is identical with Eliezer,⁶⁸ and [he was so huge that] he could hide Abraham’s feet in the palm of his hand. Once he was rebuked [by Abraham] and from fright his tooth fell out. Abraham picked it up and made ivory beds of it in which he slept. Others say that he made of it a chair which he used⁶⁹ all his life. Who gave him to Abraham? Nimrod.⁷⁰ Og went and built sixty cities, the smallest of which was sixty miles high, as it is stated, *Threescore cities, all the region of Argob*.⁷¹ And what did he eat? A thousand oxen and the same [number of] other animals, and his drink consisted of a thousand measures. A⁷² drop of his semen weighed thirty-six pounds.⁷³
It was taught: What did our father Jacob do when his sons brought him the coat [stained] with blood?⁷⁴ He did not believe them at all. Whence do we infer this? For it is written, *But he refused to be comforted*,⁷⁵ 35. because no consolations are acceptable for a living person. One, however, who is dead passes naturally from the mind,⁷⁶ as it is stated, *I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind*.⁷⁷ What then did he do? He proceeded to make a test with sheaves,⁷⁸ writing upon them the respective names of the tribes, their constellations and the months, and said to them, ‘I order you to prostrate yourselves before Levi because he wears the Urim and Thummim’,⁷⁹ but they did not stand up. ‘Before Judah who is king’, but they did not stand up; but when he mentioned Joseph to them, they all stood up and bowed before Joseph. But it was not yet quite clear that he was alive. So Jacob went to the mountains, hewed twelve stones, arranged them in a row, and wrote on each the name of its tribe, the name of its constellation and the name of its month. On one stone he wrote ‘Reuben, lamb, *Nisan*’⁸⁰ and similarly on every stone. He began from Simeon and said to them, ‘I order you to stand up for Reuben’, but they did not stand up. ‘For Simeon’, but they did not stand up. ‘For every tribe’, but the stones did not stand up. As soon, however, as he mentioned the name of Joseph to them, they stood up at once and bowed before Joseph’s stone.⁸¹ For this reason, all the tribes were written on Joseph’s stone. Similarly, all Israel are called by Joseph’s name, as it is stated, *Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock*.⁸² is a synonym of all Israel. So also all the heads of the families of the priests and Levites, [e.g.] *Eliashib*,⁸³ because of the phrase *lahashibo ’el ’abiw;*⁸⁴. The name Eliashib is broken up in three parts corresponding in sound and meaning to these three Heb. words. From ‘For this reason’ to *’abiw* is the reading of GRA. V and H have instead: ‘but from the *mishmaroth*, Eliashib the priest’. *Elḳanah*,⁸⁵, ‘he bought’. because Potiphar had bought him [as it is stated,] *And Joseph ms brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar … bought him*.⁸⁶, etc. (*ibid.* XLI, 45), which has no relevance to the subject.
When Rebekah left her father’s house⁸⁷ XXIV, 59ff. she was three years old,⁸⁸ because it is customary among kings, when a daughter is born to them, to hear of it after three days;⁸⁹ but as her father did not hear [of her birth] he did not defile her up to that time; and now a miracle happened to her in that her father died so that he should not defile her, as it is written, *Neither had any man known her*,⁹⁰ and by *man* only her father could be meant,⁹¹ for such was the practice of the Arameans to lie with their virgin daughters after they were three years of age,⁹² and then to give them away in marriage.⁹³, and by *man* only her father could be meant’.
Dinah was six years old when she bore Asenath from [her association with] Shechem,⁹⁴ corresponding to⁹⁵ the six years which Jacob served Laban in payment for the flock,⁹⁶ XXXI, 41. thus completing⁹⁷ the twenty years of his service. [The Archangel] Michael then descended and took her away to the house of Potiphar.
From here onward let the man of understanding increase knowledge.⁹⁸

footnotes:
⁶¹ From this point to the end of the tractate is an aggadic addendum.
⁶² Josh. 14, 15.
⁶³ This is probably a reference to Gen. 25, 6, But unto the sons of the concubines … Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away … eastward, unto the east country
⁶⁴ So GRA in accordance with Gen. 25, 2-4. V, M and H incorrectly ‘seventeen’.
⁶⁵ So GRA. V, M and H read, ‘and they will be used’.
⁶⁶ Is. 24, 23.
⁶⁷ King of Bashan; Deut. 3, 11.
⁶⁸ Abraham’s servant; cf. Gen. 15, 2, XXIV, 2ff.
⁶⁹ lit. ‘and sat in it’.
⁷⁰ Mentioned in Gen. 10, 8ff.
⁷¹ Deut. 3, 4.
⁷² So GRA. V, M and H read ‘and what was the’.
⁷³ V and H add ‘and so for all generations’, which makes no sense.
⁷⁴ Cf. Gen. 37, 31ff.
⁷⁵ ibid.
⁷⁶ lit. ‘he is forgotten from the heart of his own accord’.
⁷⁷ Ps. 31, 13.
⁷⁸ GRA transposes the order of V, M and H by putting the test of the sheaves before that of the stones, and omits ‘according to the first opinion’.
⁷⁹ Cf. Ex. 28, 30.
⁸⁰ The name of the tribe, constellation and month.
⁸¹ The translation follows the text of GRA.
⁸² Ps. 80, 2 where Joseph
⁸³ Neh. 3, 1.
⁸⁴ In the story of Joseph (Gen. 37, 22), E.V. to restore him to his father
⁸⁵ Connected with ḳanah
⁸⁶ Gen. 39, 1. V inserts in parentheses, And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Ẓaphenath, paneah
⁸⁷ Cf. ibid.
⁸⁸ V, M and H add ‘and three days’.
⁸⁹ H reads ‘after three years and three days’.
⁹⁰ Gen. 24, 16.
⁹¹ From ‘he did not’ to ‘meant’ is GRA’s reading. V, M and H read: ‘therefore a miracle happened to her that she should not be defiled’.
⁹² ‘After … age’ is inserted by GRA; omitted in V, M and H.
⁹³ V, M and H add: ‘on account of that which is written, Neither had any man known her
⁹⁴ Cf. Gen. 34.
⁹⁵ lit. ‘the number of’.
⁹⁶ ibid.
⁹⁷ lit. ‘until’.
⁹⁸ From ‘completing the twenty years’ to ‘knowledge’ is GRA’s text. V and M have instead: ‘and he added twenty years, because he died. From this point onwards let the man of understanding increase knowledge. And Michael descended and led her to Potiphar’s house’.

# Tractate Tefillin

מסכת תפילין

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin)

הכנת תפילין והנחת תפילין.

Preparing and wearing Tefillin, leather boxes containing biblical passages written on parchment.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 21, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 21)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Tefillin 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:1)


אין כותבין תפילין לא על עורות בהמה טמאה ולא על עורות חיה טמאה אבל כותבין על עורות נבלות וטרפות ואין חוששין שמא עורות לבובין הן:


It is not permitted to write [the four scrolls of] *tefillin*¹ on skins of ritually unclean cattle or on skins of ritually unclean wild animals. It is permitted, however, to write them on skins of *nebeloth* and *ṭerefoth* and there is no need to consider the possibility of their having been pierced at the animal’s heart.²

footnotes:
¹ These are specified below. Cf. also the Introduction.
² There was a heathen practice to remove the heart from an animal while it was still alive and offer it as a sacrifice. Rabbinic law regards such an animal as an idolatrous offering (cf. Mishnah ‘A.Z. 29b, Sonc. ed., p. 145) and forbids its entire use, including the skin.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:2)


נקבו במקום הכתב פסולים במקום הריוח כשרים עשאן ווין זיינין זיינין ווין פשוטים כפופים כפופים פשוטים פתוחים סתומים סתומים פתוחים או ששנה אותיותיהן או שכתבן עברית או שעשאן כמין קמיע הרי אלו פסולים:


If [*tefillin* scrolls] were perforated, they become unfit for religious use [if the hole occurred] in the written part; but if it occurred in the margin they remain fit. If the letter *waw* was shaped like a *zayin* or *vice versa*, straight-lined letters like curved ones³, e.g., like an ordinary *kaf.* or *vice versa*, open letters closed⁴ like a final *mem.* or *vice versa*, or if the shape of their letters had been altered [in any other way], or if they were written in [obsolete] Hebrew, or were made as a kind of amulet—they are unfit for religious use.

footnotes:
³ The final kaf
⁴ Such as an ordinary mem


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:3)


נשים ועבדים וקטנים פטורין מן התפילין כל קטן שהוא יודע לשמור את תפיליו חייב בתפילין מעשה בטבי עבדו של רבי גמליאל שהיה מניח תפילין מיכל בת שאול היתה מנחת תפילין אשתו של יונה היתה עולה לירושלם:


Women, slaves and minors⁵ §1. are exempt from [the commandment of] *tefillin*. A minor who knows how to take care of his *tefillin* is subject to the law of *tefillin*. It is related that Ṭabi, R. Gamaliel’s slave, used to put on *tefillin;* Michal, Saul’s daughter, used to put on *tefillin;* Jonah’s wife used to make the festival pilgrimages⁶ to Jerusalem.⁷

footnotes:
⁵ Boys under thirteen years of age. On the exemption of women, cf. Ẓiẓith
⁶ [For Ṭabi, cf. j.‘Erub. X, I, 26a; for the two women, cf. ‘Erub. 96a (Sonc. ed., p. 665).]
⁷ Although the commandment applied only to males (cf. Ex. 34, 23).


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:4)


נושאי המטה וחילופיהן וחילופי חילופיהן (או) [את] שלפני המטה (או) [את] שלאחר המטה כל שלצורך המטה פטורין ושאין צורך המטה בהם חייבין עמדו להספד המספידין פטורים והרואים את הפנים חייבין:


[Regarding] the bearers of a bier [to the burial place] and those who relieve them⁸ and those who relieve the latter, whether in front of the bier or behind the bier⁹—all who are required [to carry] the bier are exempt¹⁰). [from putting on *tefillin*], but those who are not required for the bier are liable. When a halt is made for lamentations,¹¹ those who are engaged in the lamentations are exempt, but those¹² who cannot see¹³ the inside [space between the rows]¹⁴ are liable.

footnotes:
⁸ In carrying the bier.
⁹ Who have not yet carried it or have done so respectively.
¹⁰ This is in disagreement with the ruling in the Mishnah (Ber. 17b, Sonc. ed., p. 106) where only those who are in front of the bier are exempt if they are required to carry it. Those behind are always liable even if their help is required, since they had already done their duty to the dead (cf. Rashi ad loc.
¹¹ A number of such halts were made by those who returned from a burial to the mourner’s house. (Cf. Semaḥoth X.]
¹² In the back rows when they stand several deep.
¹³ So in accordance with Ber. 19b (Sonc. ed., p. 117). V reads ‘those who see’.
¹⁴ Where the mourner is.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:5)


האומר בא על פני שהוא כתב או נתן עליו ספר נתן עליו תפילין ה״ז לא ישמע לו:


If a person says [to another], ‘Come and read [a Scriptural text] over my son because he is frightened’, or ‘Write, or place, upon him a [holy] scroll’, or ‘Put *tefillin* upon him that he may sleep’,¹⁵ he should not be listened to.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁵ This is the reading in j.Shab. VI, 2, 8b. The text in V is corrupt.
¹⁶ Because sacred objects should not be used for such purposes. Cf. Sanh. 101a (Sonc. ed., p. 684, nn. 6f.).


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:6)


(ש)התפילין מקבלת טומאה מזה ושונה ומטביל רבי חנינא בן גמליאל אומר צריך הוא להתירה נפלה לתוך המים ושהתה כדי שתמחק צריכה בדיקה:


A *tefillah*¹⁷ is susceptible of ritual uncleanness. [If it becomes unclean, the priest] sprinkles upon it [the water of the red heifer]¹⁸ and repeats the process, and then immerses it [in a ritual bath]. R. Ḥanina b. Gamaliel says: It is necessary to unloose it.¹⁹ If [a *tefillah*] fell into water and remained there long enough [for the writing] to be washed away, it should be subjected to an examination.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁷ V has the plural form.
¹⁸ Cf. Num. 19.
¹⁹ To remove the stitches that hold the parts of the capsule together, in order that the water may penetrate to all parts.
²⁰ To make sure that the writing is still in a good condition or to repair it if necessary.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:7)


רצועות תפילין לוקחין מכל מקום רשב״ג אומר כל עור שנעשה בו מלאכה אסור:


Straps of *tefillin* may be bought anywhere.²¹, to buy them from a reliable person. R. Simeon b. Gamaliel says: Any skin that had been used [for a secular] purpose is forbidden [to be used for the straps of *tefillin*].²²

footnotes:
²¹ There is no need, as in the case with the tefillin
²² Hence they must be bought only from a reliable person who can guarantee that no previous use had been made of the skin.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:8)


אין לוקחין תפילין אלא מן המומחה ואם אין שם מומחה נותן זוג אחד ובודק לא שיתן לו פרשיות המוכר אלא שיטול הוא לעצמו ויבדוק בדק ומצא כראוי נוטל כל האגודה ואינו חושש:


*Tefillin* may be bought only from a reliable person;²³ and where there is no reliable person a pair of *tefillin* should be given [to an expert] who examines them. This does not mean that the seller gives him the scrolls, but that he himself chooses what he pleases and has them examined.²⁴ If on examination the selected *tefillin* prove to be fit,²⁵ he may take all the batch without any scruples.²⁶

footnotes:
²³ One who can testify that they were prepared in accordance with the law.
²⁴ lit. ‘that he takes for himself and he examines’.
²⁵ lit. ‘he examined and found as proper’.
²⁶ The fitness of the sample is assumed to represent the fitness of the whole batch.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:9)


תפלה של ראש נכתבת ארבע פרשיות קדש לי והיה כי יביאך שמע והיה אם שמוע וכן של יד אלא שהוא עושה של יד פרשה אחת ואם עשאה ארבע פרשיות כשרה רבי יהודה אומר יתפור ויתנם לתוך קמיע מודה ר׳ יהודה שאם היה שניהם של ראש חופה אחת מהן (כעודן) [בעור] ועושה אותה של יד:


The [sections of the] head-*tefillah* are written on four separate scrolls²⁷ [beginning with] *Sanctify unto Me;*²⁸ *And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee;*²⁹ 11-16. *Hear;*³⁰ *And it shall come to pass, if ye shall hearken*.³¹ XI, 13-21. So also with the hand-*tefillah*, except that [all the four sections] are written in one scroll.³² If one wrote them in four separate scrolls [the *tefillah*] is fit for religious use. R. Judah says: They should be sewn together and put into one capsule.³³, which consists of four compartments joined together to form one capsule. R. Judah, however, admits that if two *tefillin*³⁴ were [like] the head-*tefillah*, one may wrap one of them in a piece of leather and so convert it into a hand-*tefillah*.

footnotes:
²⁷ lit. ‘sections’.
²⁸ Ex. 13, 1-10.
²⁹ ibid.
³⁰ Deut. 6, 4-9.
³¹ ibid.
³² lit. ‘he makes one section’.
³³ Unlike the head-tefillah
³⁴ lit. ‘both of them’.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:10)


תפלה של יד ניתנה בגובה של יד אף בין עיניך בגובה של ראש על ידך בין עיניך מה על ידך בגובה של יד אף בין עיניך בגובה של ראש כדברי ר״א בן יעקב ר׳ יהודה אומר נאמר על ידך ונאמר בין עיניך מה על ידך שהוא ראוי ליטמא (ברגע) [בנגע] אחד אף בין עיניך מקום שהוא ראוי ליטמא (ברגע) [בנגע] אחד נאמר בין עיניך ונאמר (דברים י״ד:א׳) ולא תשימו קרחה בין עיניכם מה קרחה במקום השער אף תפלה לא תתן אלא במקום השיער נאמר וכתבתם ונאמר וקשרתם יד הכותבת היא יד הקושרת:


The hand-*tefillah* is put on the upper part of the hand³⁵ [because Scripture declares, *And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thy hand*,³⁶ which means that the sign shall be for thee³⁷ can see it, i.e. on the biceps covered by the sleeve. but not for others³⁸ been put on the palm of the hand it would be visible to all.]. ³⁹So also [the Scriptural expression] *between thine eyes*⁴⁰ [implies] the upper part of the head, [because] *upon thy hand* and *between thine eyes* [occur in juxtaposition we infer]: as *upon thy hand* [means] on the upper part of the hand, so *between thine eyes* [means] on the upper part of the head. This is according to R. Eliezer b. Jacob; R. Judah says: It is stated *upon thy hand* and it is also stated [in the same verse] *between thine eyes* [the inference being that] as *upon thy hand* [refers to] a place that is susceptible of ritual uncleanness by one [symptom of] leprosy,⁴¹ so also *between thine eyes* [refers to] a place that is susceptible of ritual uncleanness by one [symptom of] leprosy.⁴² [Another reason:] It is stated *between thine eyes* and it is also stated, *Nor make any baldness between your eyes:*⁴³ as baldness occurs where there is hair [on the head] so you must put the *tefillah* only where there is hair [on the hand].⁴⁴. It is stated, *And thou shalt write them*⁴⁵ (Deut. 6, 9). and it is also stated [in juxtaposition] *and thou shalt bind them;*⁴⁶ (*ibid.* 8). [hence the inference that] the hand that writes [the *mezuzah*]⁴⁷ is the hand that binds [the *tefillah*].⁴⁸ is therefore put on the left hand.

footnotes:
³⁵ The biceps, and not on the palm of the hand.
³⁶ Ex. 13, 9.
³⁷ Where only he who wears the tefillah
³⁸ Had the tefillah
³⁹ The part enclosed in square brackets is based on Men. 37b (Sonc. ed., p. 229).
⁴⁰ Ex. 13, 9.
⁴¹ The biceps, like any other part of the body that is free from hair, is declared ritually unclean by one symptom only, viz. white hair in the leprous spot.
⁴² Viz. the upper part of the head, whose symptom of uncleanness is yellow hair in the leprous spot. The region between the eyes, however, where both hair and clean flesh are to be found, can be declared unclean by either of the two symptoms (yellow or white hair) and must therefore be ruled out.
⁴³ Deut. 14, 1.
⁴⁴ Since both verses contain the expression between … eyes
⁴⁵ Referring to the mezuzah
⁴⁶ The tefillin
⁴⁷ i.e. the right hand, with which most people write.
⁴⁸ The hand-tefillah


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:11)


מצות תפילין מהשחר עד הערב הישן ביום אינו חושש לחלוץ את תפילין (המתכנין) [המשכים] לילך בדרך לא יתננה קודם למצוה ואם נותנה קודם למצוה נותן ידו עליהם בשעת מצוה ומברך:


The commandment of [wearing] *tefillin* is from dawn until evening. If a person sleeps in the day-time he need not trouble to remove his *tefillin*. If a man rises early to go on a journey, he should not put them on before the time [for the performance] of the commandment; but if he had put them on before [the proper time for the performance of] the commandment, he should place his hand upon them at the time [for the performance] of the commandment⁴⁹ and say the benedictions.

footnotes:
⁴⁹ At dawn.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:12)


תפלה של יד אינה מעכבת של ראש ושל ראש אינה מעכבת של יד אם הפך את הקמיע מלמעלה לא יצא כשהוא נותן נותן של יד תחילה וכשהוא חולץ חולץ של ראש תחלה וכן לענין הסנדלין כשהוא נועל נועל של ימין תחלה וכשהוא חולץ חולץ של שמאל תחלה כיוצא בו כל הנכנס לסעודה (ראשון) [אחרון] יוצא ראשון חוץ מן הפת:


[Absence of] the hand-*tefillah* does not prevent the religious use of the head-*tefillah*, neither does [the absence of] the head-*tefillah* prevent the religious use of the hand-*tefillah*.⁵⁰ is independent of the other. If a man inverted a *tefillah* capsule⁵¹ he has not fulfilled his religious duty.
When a man puts on [the *tefillin*], he should put on that of the hand first; and when he takes them off, he should take off that of the head first. A similar rule applies in the case of sandals, viz. when he puts them on, he should put on that of the right foot first, and when he takes them off, he should take off that of the left foot first.⁵² Likewise, any [dish] that is served last⁵³ is removed first, except bread.⁵⁴

footnotes:
⁵⁰ Each tefillah
⁵¹ When it is on his hand or head.
⁵² [Cf. DER. X, 1.]
⁵³ Another and better reading is ‘first’.
⁵⁴ Which must remain on the table until the Grace after meals had been recited (cf. Sanh. 92a, Sonc. ed., p. 617).


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:13)


העושה תפלתו עגולה סכנה שאין בה מצוה נותנה על מצחו או על פיסת ידו הרי זו דרך המינות ציפה זהב ונותנה על נקלה שלו והוא בית יד הרי זו דרך החיצונים בית:


If a man makes his head-[*tefillah*] round, this is a dangerous practice⁵⁵ which does not carry with it [the fulfilment of] the commandment.⁵⁶ To put [the head-*tefillah*] on one’s forehead or [the hand-*tefillah*] on the palm of one’s hand⁵⁷ (Deut. 6, 8), which is contrary to the traditional interpretation. is in the manner of heresy.⁵⁸, used especially of the views and practices of the early Jewish-Christians. According to Maimonides the *minim* were Sadducees. To overlay them with gold or put [that of the hand] on one’s *neḳlah*, which means a sleeve, is the manner of the outsiders.⁵⁹, pp. 128f.] [63*a*]

footnotes:
⁵⁵ Because an accidental blow on it might split one’s head. Cf. Meg. 24b (Sonc. ed., p. 148, n. 2).
⁵⁶ The commandment being that it must be cube-shaped and flat at the base.
⁵⁷ In accordance with the literal meaning of the verse, And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes
⁵⁸ Heb. minuth
⁵⁹ Persons who follow their own interpretation of Scripture and not that of the Rabbis. [On this paragraph, cf. J. Rabbinowitz, Mishnah Megillah


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:14)


מטלטלין תפילין בתוך הבית המוצא תפילין ברשות הרבים מכניסן זוג זוג ר״ג אומר שני זוגות אחד איש ואחד אשה אחד חדשות ואחד ישנות ר׳ יהודה אומר מותר בישנות ואסור בחדשות:


*Tefillin* may be moved within a house [even on the Sabbath].⁶⁰ If [on the Sabbath day] a man finds *tefillin* in a public domain,⁶¹ he should carry them [into a safe place] one pair at a time.⁶² on his arm and the head-*tefillah* on his head in the same manner as they are worn on week-days. R. Gamaliel says: Two pairs at a time.⁶³ on his arm and two head-*tefillin* on his head. [This rule applies to] both men and women,⁶⁴. to new *tefillin* and to old. R. Judah says: [This procedure] is permitted with old *tefillin*⁶⁵. but forbidden with new.⁶⁶

footnotes:
⁶⁰ They are not regarded as articles forbidden to be handled on the Sabbath or Festival, although not worn on the holy days.
⁶¹ Where they may be trodden upon.
⁶² The hand-tefillah
⁶³ As there is sufficient room on the arm and on the head for two sets, he may put two hand-tefillin
⁶⁴ Although the latter are exempt from the commandment of tefillin
⁶⁵ Which show marks of wear or have a proper knot, so that there can be no doubt that they were genuine tefillin
⁶⁶ Since they may be only amulets.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:15)


המוצא ספר או תכריך של תפילין נותנם לחבירו וחבירו לחבירו בשבת ואפילו הם מאה אם עמו נוטלו אחד מתוך ארבע אמות ונותנו לתוך ארבע אמות שהיה ר׳ שמעון אומר כל שהוא עומד בפני ב״ד אינו עומד ולא בכתבי הקדש מי שהיה בבית הספר או בבית המדרש בבית הכסא או בבית המרחץ ושכח לחלוץ את תפילין מכסן בשערו ויוצא ואם אינו יכול נכנס לבית קרוב וחולצן:


If a man finds a [Torah] scroll or a bundle of *tefillin*,⁶⁷ he should pass them on to his fellow, and his fellow should pass them on to his fellow on the Sabbath,⁶⁸ even though they be a hundred persons. If [there is no other person]⁶⁹ with him, he⁷⁰ should take them up [while standing] within four cubits [distance from them] and remove them to [the next point] within four cubits [distance from the first point];⁷¹ because R. Simeon said: Any prohibition⁷² with H instead of *‘omed* (standing) in V. imposed by a Rabbinical Court⁷³ does not apply to holy writings.⁷⁴ to a place of safety, provided all the stages between the points of taking up and setting down are each less than four cubits in length.
If a man is in a school house or in a House of Study,⁷⁵ would not be sufficiently protected if left there. [or] in a privy or a bath-house,⁷⁶ to be left there. and forgot to remove his *tefillin*,⁷⁷ he should cover them with his hair⁷⁸ on the Sabbath in public. and leave the place.⁷⁹ If he is unable to do so, he should proceed to a near-by house where he takes them off.⁸⁰

footnotes:
⁶⁷ In a public domain where they may be trodden upon.
⁶⁸ Each one carrying them a lesser distance than four cubits. Carrying an article a longer distance in a public domain is forbidden on the Sabbath.
⁶⁹ The words in square brackets are missing in V but inserted by H.
⁷⁰ lit. ‘one [man]’.
⁷¹ And so on, until he reaches a place where they can be properly deposited.
⁷² Read ’issur
⁷³ Such as the prohibition to carry objects in a public domain even within a distance of four cubits.
⁷⁴ Consequently it is permitted on the Sabbath to carry a Torah scroll or tefillin
⁷⁵ Places in which the tefillin
⁷⁶ It would be disrespectful for the tefillin
⁷⁷ Before the Sabbath had commenced, or before he entered the two last-mentioned places.
⁷⁸ So as not to be seen wearing tefillin
⁷⁹ Taking them off when he reaches his home.
⁸⁰ Leaving them there until the termination of the Sabbath.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:16)


ונותנן לתוך אפונדתו אע״פ שיש לתוכה מעות ותולה אותם בכרעי המטה אם יש עמו אחר אסור לא יתנם תחת ראשו ואם היה משמרן מותר אם היה משא כבוד והזיע אינו חושש לחלוץ את תפילין היוצר חולץ של יד ומניח של ראש הנחתום חולץ של ראש ומניח של יד ואם היה אופה בשתי ידיו חולץ אף של יד:


[*Tefillin*] may be put into a money-bag even when there is money in it. They may also be suspended from the legs of a bed; but if another person⁸¹ be with him [in bed] it is forbidden. They must not be placed under one’s head;⁸² but if thereby they are protected⁸³ it is permitted.
If a man carried a heavy load⁸⁴ were worn throughout the day and not, as now, only during the morning prayers.] and was perspiring, he need not trouble to remove his *tefillin*. A potter should remove the hand-*tefillah* but wear the head-*tefillah*.⁸⁵ A baker should remove the head-*tefillah*⁸⁶ and wear the hand-*tefillah;*⁸⁷ but if he uses both hands in baking he also takes off the hand-*tefillah*.

footnotes:
⁸¹ A variant reading is: ‘if his wife be with him’.
⁸² To sleep on them; and much more so under any other part of the body.
⁸³ From thieves or disrespectful treatment.
⁸⁴ [This and the following regulations applied at the time when the tefillin
⁸⁵ Since his work requires the use of his hands only.
⁸⁶ Otherwise the heat of the oven might damage it.
⁸⁷ Using his right hand for the baking.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:17)


הנכנס לבית הערומים חולץ את תפיליו ורוחק ארבע אמות מבין הערומים מקצתן ערומים ומקצתן מכוסים לא יחלץ בתחלה:


[Regarding a bath-house], if a man is about to enter the room where persons are undressed, he removes his *tefillin* at a distance of four cubits from the nude persons. If some are undressed and others dressed, he does not remove his *tefillin* but should not put them on at the outset.⁸⁸

footnotes:
⁸⁸ So according to H. V reads: ‘he shall not remove them at the outset’.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:18)


הנכנס לבורסקי למשרה ולכובסים חולץ את תפיליו ורוחק ארבע אמות הנכנס לבית הכסא חולץ את תפיליו ורוחק ארבע אמות ואם היתה רחיצה של כבוד לא יחליץ עד שיגיע:


If a person is about to enter a tannery,⁸⁹ a pond [enclosure]⁹⁰ or a wash-house, he removes his *tefillin* at a distance of four cubits. If a person is about to enter a privy, he removes the *tefillin* at a distance of four cubits. If it was a superior bathing-place,⁹¹ one does not remove the *tefillin* before he reaches it.

footnotes:
⁸⁹ Where there are unpleasant smells.
⁹⁰ For steeping flax or similar things.
⁹¹ [Cf. Tamid I, 1, Sonc. ed., p. 2, where the Temple was said to have ‘a superior privy’, its superiority being that it could be locked to prevent intrusion.]


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:19)


מעשה שהלך ר׳ אליעזר לאובלין אצל בעל הבית אחד נהגו שיטבל במערה פשט ר״א את כליו ופשט את תפיליו אמר ליה רבי והלא מי המערה זו יפים משל זו ולא היה בין זו לזו אלא ארבע אמות לבש ר״א את כליו ונתן את תפיליו שלא היה ר״א מהלך ארבע אמות בלא תפילין:


It once happened that R. Eliezer went to Ubelin⁹² [where he stayed] with a certain house-owner. It was a practice there to bathe in a cave. When R. Eliezer took his clothes off and removed his *tefillin*,⁹³ [the host] said to him, ‘Rabbi, is not the water of that cave better than that of this one?’ And although there was only a distance of four cubits between the one and the other, R. Eliezer dressed and put on his *tefillin*,⁹⁴ because he never walked four cubits without *tefillin*. In this manner did R. Eliezer make the commandment of *tefillin* a permanent practice.

footnotes:
⁹² Or, ‘Obelin’. There was a village of that name near Jaffa in S. Palestine, and one near Sepphoris in Galilee. A visit by R. Eliezer to Obelin is mentioned in ‘Erub. 11b-12a (Sonc. ed., pp. 71f.).
⁹³ To bathe in one of the caves.
⁹⁴ To walk to the other cave.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:20)


כך היה ר״א עושה מצות תפילין קבע כך היה י׳א אומר גדולה היא מצות תפילין שכך אמר הקב״ה לישראל (יהושע א׳:ח׳) והגית בו יומם ולילה אמרו ישראל לפני הקב״ה רבון העולמים וכי אנו יכולין להגות יומם ולילה אמר להם הקב״ה בני הוו נותנים תפילין על ראשיכם ועל זרועותיכם ואני מעלה עליכם כאילו אתם הוגים בתורה יומם ולילה שנאמר (שמות י״ג:ט׳) והיה [לך] לאות על ידך ולזכרון בין עיניך למען תהיה תורת ה׳ בפיך:


Thus used R. Eliezer to say: Great is the commandment of *tefillin*, for the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke as follows to Israel, *But thou shalt meditate therein day and night*.⁹⁵ ‘Sovereign of the universe,’ said Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, ‘is it possible for us to meditate day and night [in the Torah]?’ The Holy One, blessed be He, answered them, ‘My children, put *tefillin* on your heads and on your arms and I shall account it to you as if you meditated in the Torah day and night’; as it is stated, *And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thy hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the law of the Lord may be in thy mouth*.⁹⁶

footnotes:
⁹⁵ Josh. 1, 8.
⁹⁶ Ex. 13, 9.


###### Tractate Tefillin 1:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tefillin/r/1:21)


חביבים ישראל שהם מקיימין כל המצות שבתורה הא כיצד תפילין על ידיהם ותפילין על ראשיהם ומזוזה על פתחיהם וארבע ציציות על בגדיהם עליהם אומר דוד מלך ישראל (תהילים קי״ט:קס״ד-קס״ה) שבע ביום הללתיך על משפטי צדקך משלו משל למה הדבר דומה למלך שאמר לאשתו תהא מקושטת ומתוקנת לפני אמרה לו מפני מה אמר לה כדי שתהא רצויה לי כך אמר הקדוש ברוך הוא לישראל בני הוו מתוקנים ומקושטים לפני במצות אמרו לו מפני מה אמר להם כדי שתהיו רצוים לי שנאמר (שה״ש י) יפה את רעיתי כתרצה יפה את כשתהא רצויה לי במצות:


Beloved are Israel [by God], for they observe all the commandments that are in the Torah. How? *Tefillin* on their hands, *tefillin* on their heads, a *mezuzah* on their doors and four *ẓiẓith* on their garments. Concerning them David, king of Israel, said, *Seven times a day do I praise Thee, because of Thy righteous ordinances*.⁹⁷
[The Sages] illustrated this with a parable. To what may this be compared? To a king who said to his wife, ‘Be well dressed and adorned in my presence’. ‘For what reason?’ she asked him. ‘In order that you may be acceptable to me,’ he replied. Similarly the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, ‘My children, be well dressed and adorned in My presence with [your performance of] the commandments’. ‘For what reason?’ they asked Him. ‘In order,’ He replied, ‘that you may be acceptable to Me’; as it is stated, *Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirẓah*,⁹⁸ [which means,] ‘Thou art beautiful when thou art acceptable⁹⁹ is of the same root as *raẓuï* (acceptable). to Me through [thy performance of] the commandments’.

footnotes:
⁹⁷ Ps. 119, 164.
⁹⁸ Cant. 6, 4.
⁹⁹ Tirẓah

# Tractate Tzitzit

מסכת ציצית

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit)

פתילים הקשורים לבגדים בעלי ארבע כנפות.

Fringes tied to garments with four corners.

Sections: Chapter-Halakhah

Location: Talmud/Bavli/Minor Tractates

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Talmud Bavli, Vilna 1883 ed. (Segments: 11, License: Public Domain)

Version (En): The Minor Tractates of the Talmud, trans. A. Cohen, London: Soncino Press, 1965 (Segments: 11)


## Chapter 1

###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:1)


הכל חייבים בציצית רבי שמעון פוטר בנשים מפני שהזמן גרמא כל קטן שהוא יודע להתעטף בציצית אביו עושה לו ציצית טלית שהוא מכסה ראשו ורובו חייבת בציצית:


All¹ are subject to the obligation of *zizith*. R. Simeon exempts women since [the commandment of *zizith*] is a positive commandment which is dependent on a fixed time.² is restricted to day-time. Any minor who knows how to wrap himself with a *ṭallith*³, but applied to the shawl to which it is attached. [Cf. the wording of the benediction connected with the performance of the commandment in P.B., p. 14, where ‘fringed garment’ is simply *zizith* in the Heb.] should be provided with it by his father. A *ṭallith* which is [long enough to] cover one’s head and the greater part of the body is subject to *zizith*.

footnotes:
¹ Even women.
² From which women are exempt. The duty of wearing zizith
³ lit. zizith


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:2)


וסדין ב״ש פוטרין וב״ה מחייבין אפיקרסין פטורה ור׳ עקיבא אומר חייבת טלית כפולה חייבת בציצית ר׳ שמעון פוטר טלית שכולה תכלת חייבת בציצית כר שעשאו סדין וסדין שעשאו טלית הרי אלו חייבין כסות הלילה ופרסי המטה הרי אלו פטורין מן הציצית והטריגון והפילגס ופוכלתרין וארביקוה ואנטנה הרי אלו פטורין זה הכלל כל שאין לו ארבע כנפים פטור מן הציצית:


As regards a [linen] sheer, Beth Shammai exempt it [from *zizith*],⁴ in a linen garment are forbidden as *mingled stuff, wool and linen together* (Deut. 22, 11). but Beth Hillel declare it liable.⁵ is superseded by the commandment of *zizith*, since the prohibition in Deut. is immediately followed (in verse 12) by the commandment of *twisted cords* or *zizith*. The juxtaposition of the two commandments indicates that the latter supersedes the former. An undergarment is exempt, but R. ‘Aḳiba holds that it is liable. A [double-sized] *ṭallith* that is folded over is subject to *zizith*, but R. Simeon exempts it.⁶ would not be in their proper place, in the four corners, but in the middle of the sheet. A *ṭallith* consisting entirely of blue wool is subject to *zizith*.⁷ does not exempt it from *zizith* although one *thread of blue* (Num. 25, 39) in each of the four *zizith* is sufficient. A bolster converted into a sheet or a sheet converted into a *ṭallith* is subject to *zizith*. A night garment and bed-curtains⁸ are exempt from *zizith*.⁹ (*ibid.*), which rules out garments worn during the night. A toga,¹⁰ with Jastrow. V has *ṭrigon* which means ‘a triangular [cloak]’. [It was oval in shape and therefore did not require *zizith;* cf. Krauss, *Talmudische Archäologie*, I, p. 611, n. 589.] a travelling cloak,¹¹ which Jastrow emends to *pinolës* (the Greek *phainoles*). [It is the *paenula* worn by Roman slaves; Krauss, *op. cit.* I, p. 170.] shawls fastened at the shoulder,¹², which Jastrow reads as *pibolaṭorin*, the Latin *fibulatorium*. a cloak worn on the head,¹³. [Krauss *loc. cit.* identifies it with *saga Nervica*, a garment of various materials and in different colours.) and an *’anṭenah*¹⁴, a kind of Roman toga. are exempt. This is the general rule: Any [garment] that is without four corners is exempt from *zizith*.

footnotes:
⁴ Because woollen zizith
⁵ In their view the prohibition of wearing mingled stuff
⁶ Since if it should happen to be unfolded, the zizith
⁷ The blue texture of the ṭallith
⁸ Or, ‘covers’.
⁹ In the commandment it is stated, That ye may look upon it
¹⁰ Reading ṭoga’
¹¹ In V pilgas
¹² In V pokaltorin
¹³ In V ’arbiḳwah
¹⁴ According to Jastrow possibly a corruption of the Greek tebenna


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:3)


מצות ציצית ב״ש אומרים ארבע חוטין של ארבע אצבעות וב״ה אומרים שלש חוטין של שלש אצבעות א״ר יוסי בר יהודה אף שאמרו ב״ה שלש של שלש קרובים דברי אלו להיות כדברי אלו:


As for the commandment of *zizith*, Beth Shammai say: [It requires that there shall be] four threads, [each] of four finger-[breadths in length]; but Beth Hillel say: Three threads [each] of three finger-[breadths in length]. R. Jose b. Judah remarked: Although Beth Hillel said, ‘Three [threads, each] of three [finger-breadths in length]’, their ruling is practically identical with that of the other.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁵ lit. ‘the words of these are near to be like the words of those’; i.e. of Beth Hillel, who refer to the fingers of a larger hand, and Beth Shammai to those of a smaller hand.


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:4)


שייר את התכלת ולא שייר את הלבן את הלבן ולא את התכלת מעכב שהתכלת והלבן מעכבין זה את זה רבי אומר אינם מעכבים:


Leaving out [from the *zizith*] the blue threads though not the white ones, or the white threads though not the blue ones, invalidates them because [the absence of] either the blue or the white invalidates the other. R. [Ishmael]¹⁶ maintains: The absence of one does not invalidate the other.

footnotes:
¹⁶ The name is added in H.


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:5)


ארבע ציציות מעכבות זו את זו מפני שכולן מצוה אחת הן ר׳ ישמעאל אומר ארבע מצות הן:


[The absence of one] of the four *zizith* invalidates the others, because all of them [constitute] a single religious observance. R. Ishmael says: They are four independent observances.


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:6)


הציצית ניתנה בתוך ג׳ אצבעות של כנף יתר מכאן פסולה ניתנה בפתיל פסולה בין טפח לפתיל כשרה ר׳ אליעזר בן יעקב פוסל קצצה וחיברה כשרה ר״מ פוסל עשאה בפני עצמה כשרה :


[Each] *zizith* is inserted [in a hole] within three finger-[breadths] of [each] corner; farther away than this is invalid If it was inserted in the border, it is invalid; if between a handbreadth [from the edge] and the border, it is valid. R. Eliezer b. Jacob declares it to be invalid. [If a strip less than three finger-breadths in length]¹⁷ was cut off [from a *ṭallith*]¹⁸ (Rashi *ad loc.*). and then rejoined to it, [the *ṭallith*] is valid. R. Meir declares it to be invalid.¹⁹ within three finger-breadths from the corner, one might use a hanging thread left from the sewing as one of the four threads required for the *zizith*. But that would render the entire fringe invalid, since all the threads have to be made specifically for the purpose of the commandment, whereas the hanging thread was one ready made (cf. Men. Sonc. ed., p. 248, nn. 1f.). [If the detached part] was made into [a smaller *ṭallith*] on its own, it is valid.

footnotes:
¹⁷ So according to Men. 41a (Sonc. ed., pp. 247f.).
¹⁸ That had no zizith
¹⁹ His reason being that, as it is proper to insert zizith


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:7)


הלוקח טלית מן העובד כוכבים ומן הכותי ומצא בה תכלת הרי זו פסולה ומשל ישראל הרי זו בחזקתה:


If one buys a *ṭallith* from an idolater or a Samaritan and found blue threads in it, it is invalid;²⁰ blue, which is the only colour that is recognized. but [if a *ṭallith* is bought] from an Israelite, it is presumed to be valid.

footnotes:
²⁰ The colour might not be that of the ḥillazon


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:8)


טלית שנטלה אחת מציציותיה אוחז בה ויוצא ניטלו שתים מכסה כמין טריגון ניטלו שלש אסור לצאת בה:


A *ṭallith*, one of whose *zizith* is missing,²¹ may be worn in public.²² If two *zizith* are missing it may be folded into triangular shape.²³. If three *zizith* are missing, it may not be worn in public.²⁴

footnotes:
²¹ lit. ‘taken’.
²² lit. ‘one takes hold of it and goes out’.
²³ So covering the missing zizith
²⁴ lit. ‘to go out with it’.


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:9)


אין מתירין ציצית על המת אבא שאול בן בטנית אומר אבא אמר לי כשאמות התיר לו ציציות שיש בה משום קדושה וחכמים אומרים אין בה משום קדושה אלא עושה אותה תכריך למת ומרדעת לחמור:


*Ẓizith* [of a *ṭallith* used as a shroud] upon a corpse should not be undone.²⁵ would be an insult to the dead, which is condemned in Prov. 17, 5, *Whoso mocketh the poor blasphemeth his Maker*, and a dead man is the poorest of all. Abba Saul b. Boṭhnith said, ‘My father told me, “When I die, undo the *zizith* [in my *ṭallith*] because they come within the category of holiness”‘.²⁶ is used as a shroud. The Sages said: It does not come within the category of holiness, so one may use it as a shroud for the dead or as a pack-saddle for an ass.

footnotes:
²⁵ The removal of the zizith
²⁶ And should be undone before the ṭallith


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:10)


הצובע טלית לעצמו אם (לכסות) [לנסות] בה הרי זו פסולה צבעה אפילו ארבעה וחמשה פעמים פסולה שאין צובעין תכלת אלא בחלזון חלזון למה הוא דומה בריאתו דומה לדג וגופו דומה לרקיע ואינו עולה אלא (לשבע) [לשבעים] שנים לפיכך דמיו ביוקר:


Should a man dye [the *zizith* of] a *ṭallith* for himself, they are invalid for religious use if he intended to test [the dye].²⁷ must be for the specified purpose of the commandment. The reading ‘to test’ [*lenassoth*] is preferable to the variant ‘to cover himself’ [*lekassoth*]. If he dyed them [with an ordinary dye], even four or five times, they are invalid, since the blue [of the *zizith*] must be dyed only with that of *ḥillazon*.²⁸ What does the *ḥillazon* resemble? In its formation it resembles a fish and [the colour of] its body resembles [the blueness of] the sky. Its appearance is a very rare occurrence²⁹ and consequently it is very costly.

footnotes:
²⁷ The dyeing of zizith
²⁸ A species of mollusc.
²⁹ lit. ‘it only rises [from the sea] in seventy years’.


###### Tractate Tzitzit 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Tractate%20Tzitzit/r/1:11)


המוצא תכלת אף על פי שהיא שזורה פסולה שאין לוקחין תכלת אלא מן המומחה:


If one finds blue [threads], even though they are twined,³⁰ are. they are invalid, since the blue [for *zizith*] may be bought only from a reliable person.³¹ blue may be used.

footnotes:
³⁰ As zizith
³¹ Or, ‘expert’, who knows that only ḥillazon
